- **Kollam, Kerala**, eight-branched estuarine/backwater system; **Kallada River** main freshwater inflow; connection to Arabian Sea through **Neendakara**.
- **Ramsar site 1204**, designated **2002**; brackish-water habitats, mangroves, fish/shellfish and livelihoods. Kerala's second-largest lake is a common extent description; wetland boundaries and open-water area are different metrics. [Ramsar information sheet](https://rsis.ramsar.org/RISapp/files/RISrep/IN1204RIS.pdf).
- Historic **Quilon/Kollam** maritime trade, including Ibn Battuta's fourteenth-century account; lake origin cannot be dated merely from that trade reference.
- **Syzygium travancoricum** is an important threatened wetland tree. Source lists **Calamus rotang** as endangered without an assessment; do not treat both as having identical verified current IUCN status.
- Threats: sewage, reclamation, altered inflow and unsustainable extraction; improve catchment water quality and community-based wetland management.

topics.title: PM SHRI: exemplar schools and NEP implementation
topics.subject: Governance in India
topics.markdown:
## Scheme design
- **Pradhan Mantri Schools for Rising India**, centrally sponsored scheme approved **7 September 2022**; strengthen **over 14,500 existing schools** as exemplars of **NEP 2020**, not create that many universities/new institutions.
- Scheme period **2022–23 to 2026–27**; States/UTs sign MoU and maintain achieved standards afterward. Eligible government/local-body schools, **KVs/JNVs** subject to selection criteria. [Education Ministry framework](https://pmshri.education.gov.in/about-us).
| Funding category | Centre : State/UT |
| --- | --- |
| Ordinary States / UTs with legislature | 60 : 40 |
| Northeastern / Himalayan States and J&K | 90 : 10 |
| UTs without legislature | 100% Centre |
- Holistic/inclusive learning, multilingual needs, experiential inquiry, communication/collaboration and competency-based assessment; labs, smart facilities and vocational exposure support pedagogy, not replace teachers.
- Green schools: water conservation, recycling and resource efficiency. **SQAF = School Quality Assessment Framework**, tracks quality/implementation.
- Evaluate attendance, inclusion, teacher capability, learning and maintenance; infrastructure selection/MoUs alone do not prove school transformation.

topics.title: Nuclear liability reform: compensation, investment and safety
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## February 2025 proposal
- Budget proposed amendments to **Atomic Energy Act, 1962**, and **Civil Liability for Nuclear Damage Act, 2010**, to support nuclear expansion and private/foreign participation; announcement ≠ enacted amendment.
- **100 GW by 2047** target; **₹20,000 crore SMR R&D mission**, at least **five indigenous SMRs by 2033** sought. Targets are not current installed capacity. [DAE Budget account](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2099244&lang=2&reg=48).
## Liability distinction
- **Operator** bears statutory no-fault liability toward victims; **section 17** gives a right of recourse after compensation in specified circumstances, including contractual rights and supplier-related defects. Supplier recourse is not identical to automatically assigning every supplier direct primary victim liability.
- **Section 46** preserves other applicable law; interpretation and insurability raised concerns. **CSC** supplements the compensation framework; India's ratification **2016** should not be confused with merely signing it. [DAE explanation](https://dae.gov.in/frequently-asked-questions-and-answers-on-civil-liability-for-nuclear-damage-act-2010-and-related-issues/).
- Source says **Fukushima 2011 caused clauses in the 2010 Act**: chronologically impossible. Bhopal **1984** informed accountability concerns; Fukushima later influenced safety debate.
## Projects and policy trade-off
- **Jaitapur, Maharashtra—EDF**; **Kovvada, Andhra Pradesh—Westinghouse**. Liability is one obstacle alongside cost, financing, technology, approvals and local concerns; amendment alone does not guarantee completion.
- SMRs may offer modular construction/flexible deployment; safety, waste, fuel security and commercial costs still require assessment.
- Balance reliable low-carbon power and investment with enforceable compensation, supplier quality, independent safety oversight, emergency readiness and parliamentary/public scrutiny.

topics.title: Gold imports and smuggling: incentives and enforcement
topics.subject: Internal Security of India
topics.markdown:
## Economy and corrected tax context
- Jewellery, investment and cultural demand; imported gold affects the merchandise balance and forex demand. Gold has store-of-value/collateral uses; jewellery manufacture and recycling create output/jobs, so “no economic output” is too broad.
- **23 July 2024** Budget cut customs duty on gold/silver to **6%**, from the earlier 15% structure; **GST is separate**. The source's February claim of “15% including GST/customs” is stale/inconsistent with its later duty-cut paragraph. [Budget 2024 summary](https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=2035618&lang=2&reg=48).
- Source **750–900 tonnes imports**, **7.5% GDP**, **four million jobs**, demand shares lack consistent period/scope; do not equate the entire gems/jewellery sector with gold alone.
- Domestic production limited; **Kolar Gold Fields** is a historic closed-mine example, not a principal then-operating source. Recycling can reduce import needs.
## Why illicit trade persists
- Tax/price arbitrage, demand, laundering and organised cross-border networks; land borders, airports and coast routes create enforcement challenges.
- Fiscal leakage, hawala, corruption and possible criminal/terror-financing links; **not every gold import or smuggling case is automatically terrorism**.
- Customs/DRI, ED and financial intelligence cooperate within respective laws; **DGGI's GST role is distinct from DRI customs-smuggling investigations**.
## Response
- Proportionate duty design, risk-based inspection, legal trade traceability, anti-corruption controls and financial investigation; international information sharing improves network detection.
- **Gold Monetisation Scheme / Sovereign Gold Bonds** were policy alternatives to idle/physical gold demand; dated discussion is not proof every scheme/tranche remains open now. SGBs are securities, not the same product as unregulated “digital gold”.
- Evaluate legitimate demand, enforcement cost and revenue before recommending further tax cuts; technology cannot replace sound intelligence and due process.
## Correcting source-era claims
- July 2024 Budget reduced standard gold/silver customs duty from 15%to 6%; **GST is separate**, so 15%“including GST”is incorrect for March 2025.
- Imports, recycling and limited mining supply demand; **Kolar Gold Fields closed 2001**, not an operating example of current output. Hutti is the useful operating Karnataka example.
- Gold imports affect goods trade/forex demand; jewellery manufacturing provides economic output, so“gold creates no output”is too broad. Source 7.5%GDP and import-volume figures need matching scope/year.
- Customs/DRI, financial intelligence, ED and GSTauthorities have distinct powers; PMLA is not simply a blanket ban on high-value cash transactions.
- Duty incentives, corruption, hawala and cross-border networks can facilitate smuggling; not every gold transaction finances terrorism. Traceability, cooperation and proportionate enforcement support legal trade.
- GMS/SGB reduce demand for idle/physical gold through different mechanisms; regulated bonds are not equivalent to every commercial “digital gold”product.

topics.title: Articles 371–371J: differentiated federal safeguards
topics.subject: Indian Polity
topics.markdown:
## Constitutional framework
- **Part XXI**, special State provisions; the heading “temporary, transitional and special” does **not** make every Article 371 safeguard temporary. Constitutional text controls scope.
| Article | State and principal safeguard |
| --- | --- |
| 371 | Maharashtra/Gujarat: regional development boards, equitable funds and education/employment opportunities; Governor's special responsibility |
| 371A | Nagaland: Parliamentary laws on specified Naga practices/customary justice and land/resources need Assembly resolution; special law/order responsibility under conditions |
| 371B | Assam: Assembly committee for specified tribal areas |
| 371C | Manipur: Hill Areas committee; Governor reporting and Union directions |
| 371D | Andhra Pradesh **and Telangana**: equitable education/public-employment opportunity arrangements |
| 371E | **Andhra Pradesh**: Parliament may establish a university; do not automatically extend it to Telangana with 371D |
| 371F | Sikkim: integration safeguards, Assembly **at least 30**, Governor's special responsibilities |
| 371G | Mizoram: specified religious/social practice, customary justice and land safeguards; Assembly **at least 40** |
| 371H | Arunachal Pradesh: Governor's law/order responsibility; Assembly **at least 30** |
| 371I | Goa: Assembly **at least 30** |
| 371J | Karnataka's Hyderabad–Karnataka / Kalyana Karnataka: development board, equitable resources and local education/employment provisions |
- **371B inserted 1969; 371C 1972**. Article 371's original 1950 form is not identical to today's Maharashtra/Gujarat wording; later additions/changes came by constitutional amendment.
- Recall **371D ≠371E**, **Nagaland ≠Mizoram land wording**; safeguards are specific, not blanket exemptions from every parliamentary law.
- [Constitution of India: official text](https://www.legislative.gov.in/documents).

topics.title: Railways Budget 2025–26: capex, safety and implementation
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Budget and promises
- Railway Budget merged with Union Budget from **2017**. FY2025–26 source capex **~₹2.62 lakh crore**, safety **₹1,16,514 crore**; distinguish total capital investment, gross budget support and actual spending.
- **200 Vande Bharat, 100 Amrit Bharat, 50 Namo Bharat rapid rail and 17,500 non-AC general coaches** planned over **two to three years**; source's “no timeline” omits the announced window. [Railway Ministry, 1 February 2025](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2098714&lang=2&reg=48).
- **100% electrification by end FY2025–26** was a target. Source **95%, ₹13 lakh crore decade investment, ~1.6 billion tonnes freight** are dated estimates; electrification does not alone mean zero-carbon electricity.
## Execution and data traps
- **Kavach** automatic train protection is one safety layer alongside track, signalling, maintenance, staff and operating discipline. **1,465 route-km** is historical coverage, not proof no further installation/upgrade work exists.
- Source “new track 113 →150 km/year” lacks category/period and is implausible as all-India aggregate; do not memorise without the original series. “5,000 underused diesels / ₹30,000 crore” is an unverified utilisation claim.
- DFCs, Mumbai–Ahmedabad high-speed rail and station redevelopment need project-wise progress; conversion of all ICF coaches into Vande Bharat is not an interchangeable technical programme.
- Freight share, speed, reliability, passenger affordability and financial sustainability should be assessed from matching data periods, not a global ranking slogan.
## Mains framework
- **Capex → bottleneck removal → dependable capacity → competitive freight / safe passengers → audited outcomes**.
- Prioritise maintenance/Kavach delivery, general-class capacity, intermodal terminals, realistic procurement and transparent costs; evaluate diesel assets' residual uses and electricity mix before declaring all stranded.

topics.title: Urban Budget 2025–26: funding, mobility and local capacity
topics.subject: Governance in India
topics.markdown:
## Compare like estimates
| Item (₹ crore, source figures) | Comparison |
| --- | --- |
| Urban Ministry | FY2024–25 BE **82,576.57**, RE **63,669.93**; FY2025–26 BE **96,777** |
| PMAY-U | Earlier BE **30,170.61 →RE 13,670** (~54.7% fall); not automatically the next year's BE cut |
| Metro / MRTS | RE **21,335.98 →new BE 31,239.28** (~46.4% rise) |
| SBM-U | Allocation **5,000**, reported lower use/RE **2,159**; establish period/status before calling audited spending |
- **RE ≠final audited actual expenditure**. Total new BE is about **17.2% above prior BE**; source's automatic inflation-adjusted decline is unsupported without a deflator and consistent baseline.
- Source **ULB 26,653 →26,158**, **21% revenue loss**, **cities 67% GDP** need category/year/method; a Union budget line is not all municipal revenue.
## Urban Challenge Fund
- Announced corpus **₹1 lakh crore**, FY2025–26 allocation **₹10,000 crore**; bankable growth-hub, redevelopment, water/sanitation projects.
- Finance **up to 25% of project cost**; **at least 50% from bonds, bank loans and PPPs**, not necessarily 50% private equity alone. [Budget announcement](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx/pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=2098385&lang=2&reg=48).
## Priorities and risks
- Metro versus buses/last-mile access, affordable housing, sanitation, climate resilience and employment need integrated assessment; capital intensity is not in itself proof of poor public value.
- **74th Amendment** concerns urban self-government; **73rd** rural panchayats. Municipal taxes, predictable transfers, State Finance Commissions, staffing and transparent borrowing determine usable autonomy.
- PPP/bond finance needs repayment capacity, risk allocation and disclosure; otherwise projects may favour profitable enclaves while excluding smaller cities and poorer residents.

topics.title: LCA Mk2, AMCA and stealth fighter technology
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Indian programmes
| Programme | February 2025 source account |
| --- | --- |
| LCA Mk 2 | Larger multirole Tejas development, GE-F414 engine; **11 weapon stations**; projected prototype end-2025, flight 2026, induction 2028–29 |
| AMCA | Fifth-generation stealth development; five planned prototypes, reported **~1.5-tonne internal weapons bay**; projected rollout 2026–27, flight 2028, certification 2032, induction 2034 |
- Source initial **four AMCA aircraft/year** is a production-plan claim, not then-achieved output.
- **These dates were reported development targets, not confirmed completed milestones or current schedules.** Source April-2024 sanction timing needs confirmation against official approval history; do not universalise it.
- IAF source **31 squadrons versus sanctioned 42** is a dated readiness comparison, not a theorem that exactly 42 guarantees two-front success.
## Stealth comparison
| Aircraft | Recall |
| --- | --- |
| Su-57 | Sukhoi, Russia; low-observable multirole design, thrust vectoring; capability varies with engine/version |
| F-35 | Lockheed Martin, US; **A conventional, B short take-off/vertical landing, C carrier**; sensor fusion, quoted max Mach 1.6 |
| AMCA | Indian development goals; planned capability is not operational performance |
- Stealth reduces radar/other signatures; **not invisibility**. External stores can increase signature; internal bay trades payload flexibility against observability.
- **Supercruise** = sustained supersonic flight without afterburner, not any supersonic speed. Source's categorical supercruise/data-fusion ranking lacks common testing criteria; avoid memorising it as settled superiority.
- India withdrew from the joint Russian FGFA development in **2018**; Aero India displays or F-21/MRFA marketing do not establish a fighter order. Neither “India will buy” nor “India will never buy” follows from attendance.
## Industrial constraints
- Engines/materials, stealth shaping, sensors/software, test/certification, funding and production capacity; local manufacture does not establish complete imported-component independence.
- Stage-gated development, reliable supplier/IP arrangements, private capability and realistic delivery plans balance near-term readiness with long-term autonomy.
## Su-57 offer, February 2025
- Russia offered cooperation/local manufacture of **Su-57**, with proposed radar, engine and software access; this was an **offer**, not a signed Indian procurement contract or confirmed 2025 production start.
- Evaluate stealth/sensor integration, sortie availability, engine maturity, cost, Indian manufacturing/IP access and interoperability. India's earlier FGFA withdrawal does not automatically settle a fresh offer.
- Russian assurances cannot determine whether US **CAATSA** sanctions or waivers apply. Technology-transfer promises need contractual scope and independent performance assessment.

## 2024 PYQ recall
- **Rafael (official printed spelling, referring to Rafale), Mi G-29, Tejas MK-1:** none is a fifth-generation fighter; answer **(d) None**. Capability upgrades do not automatically change the platform generation.

## Squadron capacity debate
- Source compares~31 squadrons with a sanctioned 42; delivery forecasts and retirements are not completed fleet changes.
- Aircraft numbers need engines/components, trained personnel, maintenance, sensors, AEW/refuelling and timely production. Private/DPSU collaboration cannot eliminate every supply constraint.
- LCA Mk 2/AMCA are development programmes; reported foreign purchase interest is not equivalent to aircraft delivered. Draft industrial policies must be labelled as drafts.

## Private rear-fuselage delivery
- **Alpha Tocol** handed a privately produced LCAMk 1 Arear fuselage to HAL; module production supports capacity while HALassembles final aircraft/ADAprovides design role.
- Otherpartners include L&T, Tata Advanced Systems, VEMand LMW; component handover is not delivery of an entirefighter or proof every 83 aircraft-contractdeadline will be met.
- rear fuselage supports aft structure/engine/tail; advancedradar, EWandavionics distinguish Mk 1 A. DPEPP2020 was a draft.
- IAMaerospace medicine work includes centrifuge/spatial-disorientationtraining and research forpilot safety; occupationalhuman factors complement manufacturing.

## AMCA and readiness: March 2025
- CCS approved AMCA development in **March 2024**, not 2023; five prototypes and a roughly ₹15,000 crore programme are development plans, not an operational fleet.
- Initial F414-powered designs and a proposed higher-thrust future engine are different stages. Stealth and supercruise are design objectives until demonstrated.
- Proposed Pakistani J-35/KAAN acquisitions must not be recorded as completed deliveries. Hotan is in Xinjiang, not Tibet.
- India's sanctioned fighter strength is 42 squadrons; MRFA 114-aircraft proposals are not completed procurement. LCA Mk1A production and Mk2 development are distinct.
- Readiness also depends on engines, spares, weapons, training, airborne warning, logistics and delivery capacity—not aircraft counts alone.

## Tejas variants: avoid mixing specifications
- Programme launched in 1983; ADA established in 1984; Tejas achieved final operational clearance in 2019. **HF-24 Marut preceded it** as an indigenous fighter.
- Mk1/Mk1A use the **GE F404 family**; **Mk2 plans use F414**. Mk1A improvements do not mean it has already switched to F414.
- Ferry range differs from combat radius and depends on configuration. Naval LCA is a technology demonstrator, not an inducted carrier fighter fleet; TEDBF is a separate development programme.
- Engine supply, domestic subsystems, certification, production capacity and maintenance determine operational readiness, beyond an order announcement.

topics.title: India–UK defence partnership: missiles and electric propulsion
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## Aero India agreements, February 2025
- **Defence Partnership–India (DP-I)**: dedicated UK Ministry of Defence programme office, coordinating bilateral industrial collaboration.
- **Thales–BDL** laser-beam-riding MANPADS contract; official release planned initial **STARStreak missiles/launchers in 2025**, correcting source “already supplied in 2024”. Later **LMM** co-production collaboration is a distinct step.
- **MBDA–BDL**, **ASRAAM assembly/test facility, Hyderabad**; air-to-air missiles differ from MANPADS. Source Jaguar/Tejas integration should be read as platform-specific programmes, not universal deployment.
- **IFEP Statement of Intent**, next-generation Navy **Landing Platform Docks**; **GE Vernova–BHEL** land-based testing work. Full electric propulsion converts supplied energy into ship propulsion; **not fuel-free operation**.
- [UK official announcement](https://www.gov.uk/government/news/uk-india-defence-agreements-boost-atmanirbhar-bharat-ambition).
## Assess outcomes
- Potential: co-production, jobs, interoperability, supplier capacity and exports. Constraints: IP/critical technology, local content, certification, costs and reliable delivery.
- Agreement/SoI, factory readiness and delivered operational systems are different stages. India–UK cooperation does not imply the UK joined **Quad** or every transfer makes India wholly self-reliant.

topics.title: Bombay blood phenotype and cross-group kidney transplantation
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Blood-group distinction
- **Bombay phenotype, Oh / hh**, identified **1952 by Y.M. Bhende and colleagues**: absence of **H antigen**, precursor for A/B expression; can resemble O on routine forward typing but anti-H antibodies complicate compatibility.
- Red-cell transfusion generally needs appropriately compatible Bombay-phenotype blood; ordinary O is **not automatically safe**. Source notation **“HH phenotype”** is misleading; rare prevalence varies by population/study.
## Kidney-transplant report
- February report describes **MIOT International, Chennai**, cross-group kidney transplant with specialised desensitisation, **double-filtration plasmapheresis (DFPP)** and B-cell-directed immunosuppression.
- DFPP reduces circulating antibodies; immunosuppression reduces immune response/rejection risk. **Blood transfusion compatibility ≠organ-transplant eligibility**: the source's “can receive organs only from Bombay donor” contradicts the reported cross-group transplant.
- A reported innovative case does not establish a universally safe protocol or benefit to “millions” of rare-phenotype patients. Source's exact journal/world-first attribution needs case-publication verification; do not confuse a Bombay **donor** report with a Bombay **recipient**.
## Ethics and governance
- Informed consent, independent clinical/ethics oversight, infection/rejection follow-up, donor welfare, lawful allocation and affordability.
- **Transplantation of Human Organs and Tissues Act, 1994**, donor registries, rare blood banking and referral networks; documented outcomes and reproducibility matter more than novelty claims. [Earlier primary Bombay-donor case](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5830818/).

topics.title: Budget 2025–26: science funding, deeptech and research balance
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Separate corpus, allocation and mission
- **₹1 lakh crore** private-sector R&D corpus announced earlier; **₹20, 000 crore FY2025–26 allocation** to implement private-sector-driven research/development/innovation, **not total DST spending**. [Budget overview](https://static.pib.gov.in/WriteReadData/specificdocs/documents/2025/feb/doc202521492801.pdf).
- **DBT ₹3, 446.64 crore**, source **+51.45%** must specify BE/RE comparator; separate Department of Scientific & Industrial Research and DST totals.
- Source **National Geospatial Mission ₹100 crore**, germplasm/high-yielding seeds, cotton productivity, manufacturing and deeptech initiatives; distinguish individual budget lines from total ministry resources.
- Additional **₹10, 000 crore Fund of Funds for start-ups** and proposed exploration of a **deeptech fund** are not identical to a confirmed single SIDBI deeptech-only fund.
- **Nuclear SMR R&D ₹20, 000 crore /100 GW 2047**, separate from the equal-sized private-R&D allocation; avoid adding them as one fund.
## Programmes and priorities
- **Bio-RIDE**: biotechnology R&D, innovation/entrepreneurship, biomanufacturing/biofoundry; National Manufacturing Mission supports technology/commercialisation.
- Source CSIR missions: **aroma/floriculture, millets, cotton, seaweed, packaging and indigenous manufacturing**; some predate the Budget and should not all be presented as new FY2025 announcements.
- Green hydrogen and nuclear initiatives support energy transition; agricultural seed/genetic work links climate resilience and productivity.
## Mains balance
- Private capital, translational research and domestic supply capability complement curiosity-driven public research and university capacity.
- “Basic-science funding reduced” needs scheme-wise and BE/RE comparisons; nominal ministry rise does not prove every institute received more.
- **NEP 6% GDP** public-education aspiration cannot be compared with an allocation percentage unless both denominator and period are supplied. Source **2.54%** is insufficiently labelled; do not silently treat it as either GDP share or Union-Budget share. Evaluate actual spending, research autonomy, access and measurable additional R&D.
## Private-sector R&D financing
- March 2025 discussion of ₹1 lakhcrore corpus concerned a proposed financing mechanism; concessional long-term loans/risk finance differ from university research grants and PLI output incentives.
- Final terms, eligibility, administrator and tenor require notified scheme checks; newspaper 5–7 year/nearly-zero-interest/IT-exclusion claims are not all final rules.
- Source GERD~0.65%GDP and private 30–36%share are dated estimates. ANRF's ₹50, 000 crore ambition, including non-government contributions, is a different funding envelope.
- Commercialisation, industry–academic collaboration, patient capital, transparent selection and measurable additional research matter; applied research support need not replace basic science.

topics.title: Lumpy skin disease and DIVA-marker vaccination
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Disease
- **LSDV**, genus **Capripoxvirus**, family **Poxviridae**; principally cattle/buffalo disease, **not a human zoonosis**. Skin nodules, fever, swollen nodes/limbs, reduced milk/weight and sometimes death.
- Blood-feeding arthropods such as flies, mosquitoes and ticks transmit infection; animal movement/biosecurity also matter. Different from bacterial mastitis or foot-and-mouth disease virus.
## February 2025 vaccine report
- **Biolumpivaxin, Biovet (Bharat Biotech group)**, developed with **ICAR**; source reports **CDSCO licence**, testing through **ICAR-NRCE /IVRI** and **Malur/Mallur, Karnataka** capacity **500 million doses/year**.
- **DIVA = Differentiating Infected from Vaccinated Animals**: marker vaccination plus suitable diagnostic tests helps distinguish infection-derived response from vaccination; **not an automatic zero-false-positive guarantee**.
- “World's first/safest” is the producer's claim; licence, efficacy under field conditions, delivered doses and maximum manufacturing capacity are different measures. [Company announcement reported 10 February](https://www.biospectrumindia.com/news/22/25654/biovet-gets-cdsco-license-for-worlds-first-ever-diva-marker-vaccine-for-lumpy-skin-disease-.html).
## Why it matters
- Dairy livelihoods, milk supply and animal welfare; public–private research partnerships can reduce outbreak losses.
- Link vaccination with surveillance, cold chain/coverage, vector control, movement safeguards and farmer information. Export potential is conditional on domestic needs and importing-country approvals.

topics.title: SHAKTI–IRIS and India’s semiconductor ecosystem
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Indigenous processor: division of work
- **IRIS-LV**, SHAKTI-based **180 nm** processor; conceived by ISRO's **IISU, Thiruvananthapuram**, designed by **IIT Madras**; software booted by IIT Madras.
- Fabricated at **SCL, Chandigarh** → packaged by **Tata Advanced Systems, Karnataka** → motherboard PCB by **PCB Power, Gujarat** → assembled by **Syrma SGS, Chennai**. [IIT Madras announcement](https://www.iitm.ac.in/hi/node/17019).
- **RISC-V:** open instruction-set architecture; no ISA royalty does not imply every processor design, fabrication tool or component is automatically open/free. SHAKTI designs support customised embedded/strategic applications.
- Mature **180 nm** technology can suit rugged industrial/space applications; it is not a leading-edge 2 nm commercial fabrication achievement. Radiation tolerance and space qualification need specific testing.
## Semiconductor chain
| Stage | Recall |
| --- | --- |
| Design | Architecture, circuits, verification; EDA tools and intellectual property |
| Fabrication | Patterning/transistors on wafers; capital-intensive cleanrooms |
| Packaging/test | Interconnections, protection, validation; ATMP/OSAT capabilities |
| Systems | Boards, software, application integration |
- Chips underpin electronics, communication, vehicles, AI and defence. India's design workforce strengths coexist with imported fabrication equipment/materials and limited domestic fabrication capacity.
- **India Semiconductor Mission / semiconductor and display programme:** support fabs, compound semiconductors, ATMP and design; PLI and design-linked incentives have different purposes. Announced facilities ≠ operational mass production.
- Benefits: supply resilience, strategic autonomy, skilled employment and domestic value addition. Constraints: capital, yields, reliable power/water, chemicals, waste control, talent and vendor ecosystems.
- Efficient cooling, renewable electricity, water reuse and hazardous-waste treatment matter. Source claim **31% of global greenhouse emissions from semiconductors** is unsupported; do not memorise it.
- Policy test: competitive sustained output and locally retained skills/IP, rather than subsidies or an “indigenous” label alone.
## Imports and ecosystem gaps
- Source FY2024 monolithic ICimports~₹1.05 lakhcrore and FY2025 April–November 2.09%total-import share are different periods; customs classifications/base effects complicate 2000–4800%growth claims.
- Semicon India 2021 supports fabrication/display/assembly-test-packaging ecosystem; Tata Dholerafab/Tata Morigaonassembly projects have different technology stages.
- Imports still cover EDAtools, core IP, wafers, manufacturingequipment and components. Indian chip-design talent does not imply all toolchains/materials are domestic.
- Source“first Indianchip 2024”is an outdated forecast and ignores earlier domestic chips; commercialfab milestones must be precisely labelled.
- Source actual spending/BE/RE mixes ₹681.11 crore and ₹1, 503.36 crore for FY2024; reconcile series before asserting utilisation. Bigcaps, long gestation, power/water, skills and supply chains require coordinated investment.
- USCHIPSAct is USlegislation, not an international alliance India joins; Quad semiconductor cooperation is a separate mechanism.

topics.title: USAID, foreign assistance and the 2025 funding freeze
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## Institution and February context
- **1961:** Foreign Assistance Act and Kennedy's executive order established **USAID**; development/humanitarian assistance also serves US foreign-policy and soft-power objectives. [Official historical account](https://2017-2020.usaid.gov/sites/default/files/documents/1868/pub_outreach_final.pdf).
- **20 January 2025:** Trump ordered a 90-day foreign-assistance review/pause; subsequent implementation disrupted programmes and staffing. Emergency waivers and litigation meant “every programme permanently abolished” was an inaccurate February conclusion. [Contemporaneous account](https://apnews.com/article/8253d7dda766df89e10390c1645e78aa).
- Work spans health, food security, disaster response, education, livelihoods, governance and climate; **Feed the Future** and support to **PEPFAR** programmes illustrate inter-agency links, not exclusive USAID ownership of all US aid.
## India and global consequences
- US development assistance to India began **1951**, before USAID's creation. Source reports roughly **US$1.5 billion over a decade / US$79.3 million in 2024**; dated estimates require consistent disbursement/commitment definitions.
- Disrupted HIV treatment, food supply, disease surveillance and partner organisations can create immediate humanitarian losses and longer-term instability.
- Source **42%** concerns a particular tracked humanitarian-aid denominator, not 42% of all world development finance; staffing and projected **six-million HIV-death** figures are dated estimates/scenarios, not observed outcomes.
- Accountability debate: effective aid, transparency and recipient ownership versus abrupt withdrawal, dependency and geopolitical influence. Reform can improve evaluation without abandoning life-saving continuity.
- India: assess actual project exposure, protect essential services, diversify finance and strengthen domestic/public-health institutions; opportunities for other powers to fill gaps are possibilities, not automatic outcomes.

topics.title: R-37M and long-range air-to-air missiles
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## System and use
- Russian **R-37M**, long-range beyond-visual-range air-to-air missile; evolution of the R-37 family associated with the earlier R-33 interception role.
- Source specifications: **over 4 m, about 510 kg, 60 kg warhead, Mach 6, 300–400 km**. These are reported variant/envelope figures; maximum range varies with launch altitude, target motion and missile version, not guaranteed combat reach.
- Inertial/mid-course updating followed by radar terminal homing; do not casually substitute semi-active homing for the advertised active-radar seeker.
- Targets can include high-value **AWACS, tankers and surveillance aircraft**, as well as combat aircraft. Disrupting support assets affects an opponent's wider air operations.
- Export **RVV-BD** and domestic R-37M specifications are not interchangeable. Aircraft integration, sensors, targeting data and rules of engagement limit operational effectiveness.
- February source links the missile to a Su-57 offer; this does **not prove an Indian acquisition**, assured integration or unrestricted technology transfer.

topics.title: Criminalisation of politics and electoral disqualification
topics.subject: Indian Polity
topics.markdown:
## Conviction, accusation and disqualification
- **RPA 1951 section 8(3):** conviction with imprisonment **at least two years** disqualifies from conviction and for **six years after release**. Section 8(1) separately covers specified offences; do not impose a universal “moral turpitude” exception. [Official Act](https://www.indiacode.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/2096/9/A1951-43.pdf).
- **Lily Thomas, 2013:** struck down section 8(4)'s protection for sitting legislators; filing an appeal alone does not erase disqualification. A judicial stay of **conviction** differs from bail/stay of sentence.
- **Jan Chaukidar, 2013** incarceration/elector ruling must be read with the **2013 statutory amendment** preserving elector status despite section 62(5)'s voting restriction. An undertrial is not automatically disqualified merely by being detained.
- **Section 11:** Election Commission can remove/reduce specified statutory disqualification, subject to the Act; source cites the **2019 Prem Singh Tamang** decision. This is different from parliamentary immunity.
## Evidence and reform
- Source ADR figures for elected MPs in **2024: 46% declared criminal cases; 31% serious cases**; charges/declarations are not convictions. Higher reported win rates show association, not proof criminality causes electoral success.
- Causes: money/muscle power, slow trials, weak party screening, patronage and voters' expectations of protection/service. Costs: intimidation, corruption, institutional distrust and skewed policy.
- Law Commission **1999 / 2014** proposals on serious charges and safeguards are **recommendations**, not an enacted blanket ban. Lifetime-ban petitions were not a February 2025 settled judgment.
- Responses: candidate disclosures, party accountability, transparent campaign finance, timely fair trials and witness protection. Charge-stage exclusion needs judicial scrutiny and safeguards against politically motivated prosecution.
- Balance electoral integrity with presumption of innocence, proportionality and voters' choice; reform should target conduct/evidence rather than stereotypes.

topics.title: AI in drug development and regulatory evidence
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Uses and limits
- AI can identify targets, predict protein/drug interactions, screen molecules, assess toxicity and ADME, select trial participants and analyse evidence. **ADME = absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion**.
- Human organ models, organoids and other new approach methodologies may reduce animal use; they do not automatically replace every animal study or human clinical trial.
- Development cost/time and success-rate figures vary by study, drug class and denominator; source “10 years / billions / 14% success” is contextual, not a universal law.
## FDA January 2025 draft framework
- Applies to AI-generated information supporting **drug/biological regulatory decisions**, not only preclinical testing. **Draft guidance**, not an automatic approval for every model. [FDA draft](https://www.fda.gov/regulatory-information/search-fda-guidance-documents/considerations-use-artificial-intelligence-support-regulatory-decision-making-drug-and-biological).
- Define question/context of use → assess model risk → set credibility requirements → validate/evaluate evidence → document limitations → monitor when use/data changes.
- Fit-for-purpose data, external validation, reproducibility and representative populations matter. Model confidence cannot substitute for demonstrated clinical benefit or safety.
## India and governance
- 2023 drug-rule changes recognised suitable alternative testing approaches; regulatory acceptance depends on the relevant endpoint and evidence, not wholesale abolition of trials.
- Risks: biased training data, rare adverse effects, poor generalisation, privacy breaches, opaque predictions and overreliance. Not every AI model continuously learns after deployment.
- Response: human/regulatory oversight, auditable datasets, secure consent-based use, staged validation and independent review. Opportunity: faster discovery and reduced animal use alongside equitable, reliable evidence.

topics.title: Avian influenza H5N1 and One Health surveillance
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Virus and spread
- **Influenza A**, family **Orthomyxoviridae**; H and N refer to **haemagglutinin / neuraminidase**. Influenza A has **18 H /11 N** identified subtypes; **H5N1** is a subtype, not the only avian influenza virus.
- H5N1 lineage first identified in **Guangdong, 1996**; highly pathogenic **clade 2.3.4.4b** spread widely among wild birds/poultry and reached mammals. Europe 2020, North America 2021, South America 2022 and Antarctic-region detections in 2024 illustrate dated spread.
- Human infections generally follow exposure to infected animals/contaminated environments; 2024 US dairy-cattle outbreaks underline the need for cross-species monitoring.
- **No sustained human-to-human transmission reported** in the relevant period; adaptation requires surveillance rather than assuming an inevitable pandemic. [WHO risk assessment](https://cdn.who.int/media/docs/default-source/influenza/avian-and-other-zoonotic-influenza/2024_07_18_fao-woah-who_h5n1_assessment.pdf?sfvrsn=a3a2b2b_4).
## Exam traps and response
- Source **~60% fatality** describes a selected historical set of confirmed cases; not fatality among every infection or a prediction for a future pandemic.
- Wild-bird migration, poultry production/trade and exposure interact; climate change can alter ecology but is not a demonstrated sole cause of every outbreak.
- **One Health:** animal/wildlife surveillance + human clinical monitoring + environmental information; biosecurity, laboratory sequencing, timely reporting, worker protection and safe outbreak control.
- Coordinate public-health/veterinary agencies without unsupported blanket claims about all poultry products or ordinary person-to-person contagion.

topics.title: Public Accounts Committee and parliamentary financial control
topics.subject: Indian Polity
topics.markdown:
## Composition
- Origin **1921**; parliamentary form after independence. **22 members: 15 Lok Sabha +7 Rajya Sabha**, elected annually by proportional representation through single transferable vote; **ministers cannot be members**.
- Chair appointed by **Lok Sabha Speaker**; Opposition chair is a convention since **1967–68**, not a constitutional command.
## Role and limits
- Examines appropriation/finance accounts and relevant **CAG reports**: spending authorised by Parliament, legal purpose, economy and financial accountability.
- **CAG audits; PAC examines and reports.** PAC does not replace the executive, itself implement programmes or function as a criminal court.
- Excess expenditure and reappropriation receive scrutiny; witnesses/explanations and follow-up action-taken reports connect audit findings to accountability.
- Distinguish **Estimates Committee** (economy/organisation and estimates) and **Committee on Public Undertakings** (public-enterprise oversight).
- Challenges: delayed reports, limited research capacity and weak recommendation follow-up. Improve timely evidence, bipartisan scrutiny and tracked implementation while preserving executive responsibility.

topics.title: P-8I maritime patrol and anti-submarine warfare
topics.subject: Internal Security of India
topics.markdown:
## Platform
- **Boeing P-8I**, Indian derivative of **P-8A Poseidon /737**; long-range maritime reconnaissance, anti-submarine and anti-surface warfare.
- India-specific subsystems alongside radar, electro-optical/infrared sensors, electronic surveillance, magnetic-anomaly detection and deployable **sonobuoys**. Radar detects appropriate electromagnetic returns; submerged-submarine acoustic sensing is a different task. [Boeing design announcement](https://boeing.mediaroom.com/2010-07-26-Boeing-Completes-Final-Design-Review-for-P-8I).
- Source's **AN/APS-137** designation should not be learnt as the P-8I's standard radar; the platform is associated with the **AN/APY-10** family.
- **Mk 54 torpedoes / Harpoon** illustrate weapons roles; sensor detection, classification and prosecution require an integrated mission system.
- Dimensions reported **39.5 m length /37.6 m span /12.4 m height**, CFM56 engines, about nine mission crew; range/radius/on-station time must not be conflated.
## Fleet and strategy
- **Eight ordered 2009; four additional 2016 →12** in the February 2025 fleet. Additional **six** were a procurement discussion, not delivered aircraft.
- Supports Indian Ocean sea-lane security, surveillance, search/rescue and interoperability with partner navies; costs, maintenance, data security and domestic capability remain important.
- A bilateral technology dialogue does not mean every purchase is a completed co-production/technology-transfer project.

topics.title: AASM HAMMER precision-guided air-to-ground weapons
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Manufacturer and architecture
- **Safran AASM HAMMER** = Highly Agile Modular Munition Extended Range; **not an MBDA product** and not simply a cruise missile.
- Guidance and propulsion kit fitted to bomb bodies; advertised configurations **125 /250 /500 /1,000 kg**. Combines inertial/GPS guidance with infrared or laser terminal options depending on version. [Safran product](https://www.safran-group.com/products-services/aasm-hammer-tm-highly-agile-modular-munition-extended-range).
- Booster permits stand-off attacks; commonly reported **~70 km** depends on release conditions/version. “Mach 1.5” is not a universal speed for every configuration.
- Precision/all-weather claims depend on guidance type, target data and countermeasures; laser designation conditions differ from GPS/INS or imaging guidance.
## Indian relevance
- Rafale-associated Indian procurement/deployment interest; the PDF's MBDA manufacturer/contract attribution is erroneous.
- Potential: accuracy, flexible bomb sizes, reduced exposure and aircraft integration. Assess integration/certification, cost, electronic warfare resilience, supply assurance and genuine domestic technology access.
- A precision weapon can reduce some collateral risks but does not eliminate targeting obligations or guarantee zero civilian harm.

topics.title: TRAI, telecom regulation and TDSAT
topics.subject: Governance in India
topics.markdown:
## Institution
- **TRAI Act 1997**, established **20 February 1997**, New Delhi; statutory regulator for specified telecommunications/broadcasting matters.
- **Chair +not more than two whole-time +not more than two part-time members**, appointed by the Central Government. Do not learn source's different fixed membership as the Act's rule. [Official annual report](https://www.trai.gov.in/sites/default/files/2024-10/TRAI-English-Annual-Report-10032014.pdf).
## Division of responsibility
| Institution | Main distinction |
| --- | --- |
| TRAI | Tariff/quality/interconnection regulation and recommendations; competition/consumer interests |
| DoT /Government | Licensing and spectrum administration under the legal framework; TRAI does not itself allocate every spectrum licence |
| TDSAT | Telecom dispute adjudication/appellate tribunal, separated by **2000 amendment** |
- Regulation balances affordable access, quality, innovation, fair competition and viable investment. Recommendations are not identical to binding government licensing decisions.
- Individual subscriber complaints ordinarily use service-provider grievance mechanisms; TRAI is not a general consumer court adjudicating every complaint.
- Digital divide, unsolicited communication, service quality and emerging technologies require transparent consultation, evidence and coordination with other regulators.

topics.title: Easterine Kire and Naga literary memory
topics.subject: Indian Art and Culture
topics.markdown:
## Author and recognition
- Naga writer **Easterine Kire**, English-language novels/poetry rooted in oral traditions, memory and community experience.
- **Spirit Nights (2022)** won the **Sahitya Akademi English award for 2024**; award year and publication year differ. [Akademi newsletter](https://sahitya-akademi.gov.in/e-newsletter/Jan-March_2025_Newsletter.pdf).
- **When the River Sleeps (2014)**: **Hindu Prize 2015**. Other works: **A Naga Village Remembered (2003), A Terrible Matriarchy (2007), Mari (2010), A Respectable Woman (2018)**; later editions can bear other years. “Mari 2003” confuses separate books. [Publisher-supplied bibliography](https://books.google.com/books/about/A_Respectable_Woman.html?id=q0YEEQAAQBAJ).
## Themes and significance
- Folklore/spirit beliefs, human–nature relationships, women and social expectations, war's impact, intergenerational memory and cultural identity.
- Kohima's wartime/post-war experience appears in her fiction; literary memory illuminates lived history but does not replace documentary evidence for every event.
- Preserve oral knowledge and indigenous voices; translate/support regional writing without treating all Northeast communities as one undifferentiated culture.
- Novels can challenge stereotypes and expose social change while sustaining storytelling traditions; award recognition improves visibility beyond the region.

topics.title: President’s Rule: constitutional limits and federal safeguards
topics.subject: Indian Polity
topics.markdown:
## Trigger and effect
- **Article 356:** State government cannot be carried on according to the Constitution; President may act on Governor's report **or otherwise**. Ordinary law-and-order difficulty or a hung Assembly does not automatically justify it.
- **Article 355:** Union duty to protect States and ensure constitutional government. **365:** failure to comply with lawful Union directions may support a constitutional-breakdown assessment, not automatic dismissal.
- President may assume specified State executive functions and declare legislative powers exercisable by Parliament. **High Court powers cannot be assumed**.
## Approval and duration
- Both Houses must approve within **two months**, by ordinary majority. Special Lok Sabha dissolution rule: Rajya Sabha approval plus Lok Sabha approval within **30 days of its first sitting after reconstitution**.
- Approved proclamation operates **six months**, renewable by both Houses in six-month periods, **maximum three years**.
- Beyond **one year**, both conditions: a national emergency operates in India or all/part of the State **and** ECI certifies election difficulties. Do not substitute either condition alone. President can revoke without parliamentary approval. [Parliamentary reference](https://eparlib.sansad.in/bitstream/123456789/761237/1/Presidents_Rule_in_St_UT_Eng_9th_ed_2016.pdf).
- **Article 357:** Parliament may confer State legislative power on the President, with permitted delegation; this is different from an **Article 123 ordinance**.
## Safeguards and reform
- **S.R. Bommai, 1994:** judicial review, floor-test primacy for majority disputes, limits on dissolution before parliamentary approval; courts may restore unconstitutional dismissal.
- **Rameshwar Prasad, 2006:** Bihar Assembly dissolution held unconstitutional. Political apprehensions are not a substitute for relevant constitutional evidence.
- **Sarkaria 1988:** last resort, warning/remedial options where feasible. **Punchhi 2010:** proposed localised responses; district-level Article 356 is **not existing constitutional law**.
- Assess federalism, democratic mandate and prompt return to representative government. Source counts of impositions are dated, not a current total.

topics.title: Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Institution and mission
- India-led **CDRI**, launched at **UN Climate Action Summit, 2019**; headquarters **New Delhi**. Partnership of governments, international organisations, development banks, academia/private sector.
- Resilience across **planning →design →construction →operation →recovery**; maintain critical water, transport, power, communication and health services during disasters/climate extremes.
- Source **40 countries /seven organisations** is a dated membership count, not a fixed legal composition or current total.
## Initiatives and frameworks
- **IRIS, 2021**: Infrastructure for Resilient Island States, especially **SIDS**; distinct from IIT Madras's IRIS processor. [IRIS vision](https://iris.cdri.world/upload/pages/IRIS_Vision.pdf).
- **Global Infrastructure Resilience Report 2023**, **DRI Connect**, international resilience conferences; **IRAF** supports infrastructure-resilience action with partner institutions including UNDP/UNDRR.
- Connect to **Sendai Framework 2015–30**, SDGs and Paris climate goals; India's **Disaster Management Act 2005 /National Policy 2009** are domestic frameworks.
- CDRI is not a single global emergency-relief force or replacement for national agencies.
## Mains application
- Risk assessment/standards, retrofit, resilient finance, local capacity and nature-based solutions reduce future service disruption and recovery costs.
- Constraints: affordability, data, maintenance, institutional coordination and unequal small-island capacity. Measure service continuity and avoided losses, not only new construction.

topics.title: India–Myanmar border and free movement arrangements
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## Geography and original arrangement
- **1,643 km** border: **Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram**; Myanmar's adjoining administrative areas include **Kachin, Sagaing, Chin**. **Shan does not directly border India**.
- Traditional cross-border ethnic/family networks predate modern borders. Original FMR permitted eligible residents within **16 km**, with specified border-pass/stay conditions; not unrestricted entry for every person.
## Changing policy: distinguish dates
- **8 February 2024:** MHA announced decision to scrap FMR and recommended immediate suspension pending the process. [Official announcement](https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=2003884&lang=2&reg=48).
- A **December 2024 revised border-pass arrangement** was reported with **10 km eligibility /seven-day visits**; therefore the PDF's unqualified 16 km description is historical. [Contemporaneous district-implementation report](https://www.newindianexpress.com/amp/story/nation/2025/Jan/05/mizoram-myanmar-border-movement-regulated-following-union-govts-directives-official).
- Suspension announcements, fencing plans and locally implemented permits are distinct stages; source 50 km/six-month descriptions should not override the specified rules.
## Security–community balance
- Concerns: insurgent movements, narcotics/arms trafficking, identity verification and spillover from Myanmar conflict. Refugees, ordinary ethnic visitors and criminals are not interchangeable categories.
- Restrictions affect kinship, medical access, local trade and livelihoods; consultation with border States and communities is essential.
- Improve lawful monitored crossings, verifiable documentation, intelligence cooperation, humanitarian safeguards and livelihood alternatives; fencing alone cannot address every security driver.
- **Act East /Kaladan /India–Myanmar–Thailand highway** connect regional strategy to border management; a proposed corridor is not automatically a functioning infrastructure network.
## Border management update
- The approximately 1,643 km India–Myanmar border touches Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, Manipur and Mizoram—not Tripura.
- Fencing and road announcements are plans; expenditure, sanctioned length and completed infrastructure are different measures.
- Earlier FMR arrangements allowed specified movement within 16 km; late-2024 revised pass arrangements used 10 km. Withdrawal announcements and implementation differed across locations; do not describe an unconditional permanent visa-free entitlement.
- Terrain, forests, drainage and cross-border Naga/Kuki-Zo ties complicate fencing. Combine lawful controls with community consultation, livelihood access and humanitarian safeguards; displacement does not itself establish criminality.

topics.title: Malaria: parasite cycle, vaccines and elimination
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Organism and life cycle
- Protozoan **Plasmodium**, transmitted principally by infected **female Anopheles**; important human species include **P. falciparum /P. vivax**. Not bacterial and not spread by every mosquito species.
- Mosquito injects **sporozoites →liver stage →merozoites infect red cells →some develop into gametocytes →mosquito ingests them →sexual development →sporozoites**.
- Repeated red-cell infection causes illness; falciparum can cause severe disease. Vivax dormant liver stages complicate relapse/elimination.
- **Laveran 1880** identified parasites; **Ronald Ross 1897** demonstrated mosquito-linked development; **Grassi and colleagues 1898** clarified human-malaria transmission. Science's colonial setting does not imply equitable health delivery.
## Vaccines: recommendations versus experiments
- WHO recommended **RTS,S/AS01 in 2021; R21/Matrix-M in October 2023**, for children against **P. falciparum** in endemic settings. [WHO vaccine explanation](https://www.who.int/news-room/questions-and-answers/item/q-a-on-rts-s-malaria-vaccine).
- Liver/pre-erythrocytic targeting complements nets, vector control and treatment; neither vaccine is 100% protection against every species.
- Source **36% over four years /77% over one year** arise from different trial settings/timeframes; do not compare as identical head-to-head effectiveness measures.
- **PfSPZ**, blood-stage **RH5** and transmission-blocking approaches are research strategies at different stages; not all licensed routine vaccines.
## Elimination and public health
- **Georgia certified malaria-free, 23 January 2025**; WHO certification requires at least **three consecutive years without indigenous transmission** plus prevention-of-re-establishment capacity. [WHO announcement](https://www.who.int/laos/news/detail-global/23-01-2025-georgia-certified-malaria-free-by-who).
- National elimination ≠global eradication. Imported infections do not automatically negate absence of indigenous transmission.
- Surveillance, timely diagnosis/treatment, insecticide-treated nets, appropriate spraying, vector management and sustained funding; resistance, climate suitability, migration and weak health systems threaten progress.
- Equity matters: reach remote/marginalised communities, sustain surveillance after case declines and integrate vaccination with existing services.

topics.title: SIDBI–AFD and green MSME finance
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Institutions
- **SIDBI:** statutory **SIDBI Act 1989**, operational **2 April 1990**; promotion, financing and development of MSMEs, with direct finance, refinance, risk capital and institutional support.
- **AFD:** French development institution, founded **1941**; loans, grants and technical cooperation across sustainable development, not a commercial Indian bank.
- Collaboration directs long-term development finance towards **green MSME investment**, energy efficiency, low-carbon technology and resilience.
## Financing mechanism
- External development credit →SIDBI/intermediaries →eligible MSME investments →technical support/monitoring.
- **US$100 million AFD co-finance** appears in SIDBI's FY2024–25 account; distinguish sanctioned funds, on-lending and final disbursement. [SIDBI annual report](https://www.sidbi.in/uploads/announcements/Annual_Report_Part_1_00_compressed.pdf).
- Source AFD **108-country /€1.7-billion** figures lack a clear programme/period denominator; not reliable descriptions of the institution's entire current worldwide annual lending.
## Benefits and safeguards
- MSMEs face credit, collateral, technical-assessment and technology-upgrade barriers; blended finance/capacity building may lower transition costs.
- Verify additional investment, energy/emission savings, repayment viability and small-firm access; guard against greenwashing, currency risk and subsidising projects that would proceed anyway.
- Green finance is complementary to cleaner production skills, reliable electricity, market demand and proportionate regulation.

topics.title: India–US partnership: February 2025 agenda
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## Relationship and dated developments
- **Trump became 47th US President on 20 January 2025**; Modi's Washington visit **13 February 2025**. India's “natural ally” rhetoric is not a mutual-defence treaty.
- **COMPACT:** Catalyzing Opportunities for Military Partnership, Accelerated Commerce & Technology; **TRUST** technology initiative; intent to expand bilateral trade to **US$500 billion by 2030**, and negotiate a first trade-agreement tranche. **Targets/negotiations**, not achieved outcomes. [Joint statement](https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=2103037&lang=2&reg=48).
- Defence cooperation includes proposed procurement/production, autonomous systems and logistics; US statements about offering advanced fighters do not establish an Indian F-35 order.
- **STA-1 eligibility, 2018:** facilitates specified licensed-exception exports; not blanket access to every controlled technology. **Quad revived 2017 /INDOPACOM renamed 2018** are separate institutional developments.
## Trade, technology and tensions
- Defence, digital/critical technology, space, energy, education and diaspora deepen ties; tariff reciprocity, market access, immigration and strategic differences can create friction.
- Trade-partner and FDI figures must distinguish fiscal/calendar years, goods/services and investment stock versus annual inflow; source's undifferentiated US$51.6-billion figure should not be used as one year's FDI.
- Tariff threats and an “External Revenue Service” proposal are not proof a new statutory agency or all levies had taken effect in February.
- India's **2025 Budget was already presented on 1 February**; the PDF's “upcoming Budget” is stale. Market/currency predictions remain forecasts.
- Mains approach: expand reciprocal, transparent cooperation while preserving strategic autonomy, data/technology safeguards and diversified partnerships.
## Defence technology and autonomy
- Engine delays and export/licensing constraints illustrate dependence on critical foreign subsystems; assess co-production, IP access, spares, supply-chain diversification and lifecycle support.
- Partnership does not require abandoning independent decisions on other partners. SIPRI import-volume shares cannot be interpreted as shares of India's entire defence budget.

## February 2025 agenda: additional details
- The meeting discussed in the April issue was an **official working visit on 13 February 2025**, rather than a fresh April state visit.
- **TRUST = Transforming the Relationship Utilizing Strategic Technology**: defence, AI, semiconductors, quantum, biotechnology and space; resilient supply chains include critical minerals and active pharmaceutical ingredients. Strategic Mineral Recovery seeks recovery from heavy-industry streams such as aluminium, coal and oil/gas.
- February defence intentions included a new **10-year framework**, pursuing additional P-8I aircraft, Javelin/Stryker procurement and co-production, and review of arms-transfer rules. These were prospective commitments in this issue; the F-35 discussion established no Indian purchase contract.
- **ASIA = Autonomous Systems Industry Alliance**: Anduril–Mahindra maritime/counter-drone cooperation and L3Harris–BEL towed-array sonar exemplify industry partnerships. Expanded Tiger Triumph supports tri-service interoperability.
- First BTA tranche was targeted for **fall 2025**; market access, tariff/non-tariff barriers and supply chains were negotiation objectives. Civil-nuclear law changes were proposed, not laws already amended. Invitation to a 2025 Quad summit did not establish a completed visit.
- Source's approximately US$100-billion **US trade deficit** claim confuses trade totals and balances; retain period-specific goods/services data rather than this figure. Quad is a four-country partnership, not a treaty military alliance.
- Revision linkage: defence interoperability → technology access → co-production and resilient supply chains; manage export licensing, data rules, Russia/CAATSA differences and humane migration procedures while preserving strategic autonomy.
[February joint statement](https://www.whitehouse.gov/briefings-statements/2025/02/united-states-india-joint-leaders-statement/).

topics.title: Asteroid 2024 YR4 and planetary-defence risk
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Discovery and changing estimates
- **2024 YR4**, discovered **27 December 2024**, ATLAS, Chile. Preliminary orbital observations briefly raised concern about **22 December 2032** Earth encounter.
- Source **2.1%** is a temporary probability, not a certain impact prediction. Additional observations reduced uncertainty; **24 February 2025 NASA reported no significant Earth-impact risk** for 2032 or beyond. [NASA facts](https://science.nasa.gov/solar-system/asteroids/2024-yr4-facts/).
- A provisional geographic “risk corridor” is conditional on an impact solution, not a prediction of destruction in every listed country. Risk estimates can rise before falling as the orbital uncertainty region narrows.
## Defence and communication
- Detection →repeated observation →orbit refinement →risk communication →mitigation assessment if warranted.
- **IAWN** coordinates warnings; **SMPAG** assesses space-mission options. Kinetic impactors demonstrated by **DART/Dimorphos, 2022**; other deflection concepts depend on warning time/size and are not approved missions for this asteroid.
- **Tunguska 1908** flattened roughly **2,000 km²**, not the PDF's 830 km². Size, composition, atmospheric breakup and trajectory determine consequences.
- Maintain observatory capacity and transparent updates; distinguish asteroid risk from sensational early headlines and hypothetical nuclear-deflection proposals.

topics.title: Black seadevil: deep-sea adaptations
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Identification and habitat
- **Melanocetus johnsonii**, humpback anglerfish/black seadevil; known deep-sea species, **not a newly discovered species**.
- February 2025 Tenerife footage concerned an unusual daylight surface sighting; it did not establish surface water as normal habitat or the fish's first-ever scientific observation.
- Lives at mesopelagic/bathypelagic depths; source “only deeper than 2,000 m” is too restrictive. Dark colour, large mouth/teeth and expandable body aid opportunistic feeding.
## Adaptations and conservation
- Modified dorsal spine bears a **bioluminescent lure**, associated with symbiotic bacteria; attracts prey in darkness. Females are much larger than males.
- Low light, pressure and limited food shape deep-sea ecology; an anatomical adaptation is not proof the fish occurs only in the abyssal zone.
- Source **IUCN Least Concern** classification does not by itself demonstrate a measured stable population; status and population trend are different.
- Ocean layers: **epipelagic 0–200 m →mesopelagic 200–1,000 m →bathypelagic 1,000–4,000 m →abyssopelagic 4,000–6,000 m**; approximate depth conventions.
- Research and habitat protection matter amid deep-sea pollution, warming and extraction pressure; rare footage alone does not establish the sighting's cause.
- [FishBase species listing](https://fishbase.org/identification/SpeciesList.php?genus=Melanocetus) identifies *M. johnsonii* as an already described species (**1864**).

topics.title: Underwater domain awareness and autonomous systems
topics.subject: Internal Security of India
topics.markdown:
## Concept and February 2025 cooperation
- **UDA:** integrated understanding of underwater activity/environment—submarines, acoustic conditions, seabed infrastructure and relevant maritime traffic.
- **ASIA =Autonomous Systems Industry Alliance**, announced **13 February 2025** to scale industrial partnerships/production in the Indo-Pacific. [Joint statement](https://www.whitehouse.gov/briefings-statements/2025/02/united-states-india-joint-leaders-statement/).
| Source-reported system /partners | Role or stage |
| --- | --- |
| ThayerMahan SeaPicket | Persistent acoustic surveillance |
| Liquid Robotics–Sagar Defence Wave Glider | Unmanned surface platform; source negotiation for 60 |
| L3Harris–BEL | Low-frequency active towed sonar discussions |
| Ultra Maritime–BDL | Multi-static sonobuoy co-production cooperation |
| Anduril large autonomous undersea vehicles | Autonomous subsea capability |
| Ocean Aero Triton | Hybrid underwater/surface unmanned system |
- Discussion, agreement, manufacture and operational deployment are different stages; not every listed platform was delivered to India. Avoid “first nation ever given any sensitive US technology”.
## Integrated surveillance
- Sensors/platforms →data fusion/classification →command assessment →appropriate maritime response. Passive sonar listens; active sonar emits sound and analyses returns; environmental noise/temperature affect detection.
- February references: **12 P-8I aircraft**, **24 MH-60R helicopters ordered**, **15 naval MQ-9B within 31 overall acquisition**, possible additional P-8Is. Ordered totals ≠delivered fleet.
- Benefits: anti-submarine capability, sea-lane/seabed-infrastructure protection, search/rescue and partner interoperability. Constraints: endurance, acoustic ambiguity, secure communications, cost, IP and autonomy safeguards.
- Quad cooperation and shared disaster-response mobility do not establish a formal military alliance or unlimited access to Indian maritime data.

topics.title: Panchayat devolution, finance and democratic participation
topics.subject: Governance in India
topics.markdown:
## Constitutional design
- **73rd Amendment Act, 1992**, effective **24 April 1993**: Part IX; elected rural local government, Gram Sabha, reservations, regular elections and State Finance Commissions.
- Village →intermediate →district tiers; intermediate tier may be omitted in States with **population ≤20 lakh**. **Article 243G /Eleventh Schedule's 29 subjects:** State legislatures may devolve authority; listing does not automatically transfer every function/staff/fund.
- **At least one-third** of seats/chairperson offices reserved for women constitutionally; many States provide **50%** by their laws. Source treats 50% as the original nationwide constitutional rule: incorrect.
## Devolution Index 2024, released 13 February 2025
- Ministry of Panchayati Raj/IIPA assessment; six dimensions: **framework, functions, finances, functionaries, capacity building, accountability**.
- Report scores: **Karnataka 72.23, Kerala 70.59, Tamil Nadu 68.38**. Scores measure the stated index, not percentages of every possible power transferred. [Official report](https://panchayat.gov.in/en/notice/devolution-index-report-2024-annexures/).
- Helps citizens compare decentralisation and governments identify weak dimensions; legal delegation must be matched by practical staff/funding authority.
## Distress and reform
- Incomplete **3Fs—functions, funds, functionaries**, weak own revenues, delayed SFC action, tied schemes and political interference can make Panchayats delivery agents rather than autonomous governments.
- **15th FC FY2021–26 rural-local grants: 40% untied /60% tied**, chiefly water/sanitation; **2020–21 interim 50/50**. PDF's “60% untied” is wrong. [MoPR Finance Commission reports](https://panchayat.gov.in/en/finance-commission/central-finance-commissions-reports-related-to-rural-local-bodies-rlbs/).
- DBT/JAM can change payment channels but do not eliminate Gram Sabha participation, local verification or grievance responsibilities. PM-KISAN source **₹6,000 annually** is a scheme entitlement, not a Panchayat grant.
- Strengthen meaningful Gram Sabha/GPDP planning, devolved staff, predictable transfers, local tax capacity, social audit, transparent digital records and elected-member training.
- Reported **14 lakh women representatives** is dated; source's 20%-State full-devolution and 40%-urban-population figures lack clear verified denominators. Avoid using them as census facts.
- Mains: fiscal flexibility +accountability +community voice; preserve welfare delivery while empowering local institutions and addressing rural–urban transition.
## Practice-question corrections
- **SFCs, the normal three-tier structure and at least one-third women's reservation** all arise from the constitutional Panchayat framework; the PDF's key incorrectly treats one-third reservation as false. Remember the small-State intermediate-tier exception.
- Untied grants support local flexibility; tied grants specify purposes. Source's **“60% untied”** and its explanation reversing the statement numbers are unreliable; use the corrected 15th FC split above.
- These questions are supplied coaching practice, not dated official PYQs.

topics.title: Typhoid, paratyphoid and vaccine development
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Disease
- Enteric fever: **Salmonella enterica serovar Typhi /Paratyphi**; faecal–oral transmission through contaminated water/food. Not caused by a virus or by ordinary airborne spread.
- Fever, gastrointestinal illness and systemic complications; sanitation, safe water, surveillance and antimicrobial resistance are central public-health issues. Source's **360/100,000 /4.5 million annual cases** need study/year context.
## ICMR vaccine initiative
- Source reports **ICMR–NIRBI, Kolkata** candidate using bacterial **outer-membrane vesicles**, targeting Typhi and Paratyphi A, with calls for industrial collaboration.
- Development/technical validation →safety/efficacy assessment →regulatory approval →manufacture/market; an expression of interest is **not a licence or proof of clinical efficacy**.
- ICMR calls for typhoid/paratyphoid vaccine commercialisation predate this February report; do not infer every reported candidate is a newly licensed 2025 product. [ICMR commercialisation invitation](https://www.icmr.gov.in/icmrobject/custom_data/1720273182_eoi_salmonella_re_publication.pdf).
## Vaccine distinctions
- **TCV:** conjugate vaccines, usable from six months for approved products; **Vi polysaccharide:** typically ≥two years; **Ty21a:** oral live vaccine with product-specific eligibility.
- Existing typhoid vaccines do not automatically protect equally against all paratyphoid strains. Availability differs by programme/product; “only private sector everywhere” is too broad.
- Vaccination complements WASH and surveillance; antibiotic choice requires resistance-aware clinical assessment, not memorising the source's drug list as guaranteed treatment.

topics.title: mRNA cancer vaccines and immunotherapy
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Mechanism
- Tumour profiling →identify relevant antigens/neoantigens →design mRNA →cells produce antigen →immune recognition targets cancer cells.
- **Therapeutic personalised vaccines** treat existing cancer; unlike preventive **HPV/HBV vaccination**, they do not automatically prevent all cancers.
- mRNA acts through cellular protein production; it does not need to alter the patient's DNA. Selection, immune response and benefit vary across tumours/patients.
## February 2025 status
- Russia/Gamaleya's **December 2024 announcement** described preclinical development and a promise of free availability in early 2025; a promise is **not evidence of routine licensed use, survival benefit or guaranteed fewer side effects**.
- UK **NHS Cancer Vaccine Launch Pad** facilitates clinical trials; it is not proof all experimental vaccines became routine NHS care.
- **CureVac is German**, correcting the PDF's US attribution; **CVGBM** brain-tumour vaccine early-phase results must not be equated with completed efficacy trials.
## Distinguish therapies
| Approach | Main principle |
| --- | --- |
| mRNA vaccine | Present tumour-related antigens to stimulate immunity |
| CAR-T | Engineer T cells to recognise targets |
| Checkpoint inhibitors | Release inhibitory immune signals |
| Monoclonal antibodies | Target specified molecules/cells |
- Risks/constraints: heterogeneous tumours, immune escape, delivery/manufacturing time, toxicity, cost and limited mature evidence. Source **120 trials** is a dated unverified count.
- Evaluate clinical endpoints, informed consent, comparative safety, regulatory approval and equitable access; novelty alone does not establish an effective treatment.
- [NHS programme description](https://www.england.nhs.uk/cancer/nhs-cancer-vaccine-launch-pad/): referral to eligible **clinical trials**, not routine efficacy confirmation.

topics.title: Faecal coliform and river-water quality
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Indicator, not a universal pathogen count
- Thermotolerant/faecal coliforms are used as indicators of possible faecal pollution; **E. coli** is an important subset. Not every detected organism is itself pathogenic, and a single indicator does not identify every virus/parasite.
- Sources: untreated sewage, animal waste, runoff and inadequate sanitation. Exposure can signal risk of enteric disease; organism concentration, exposure and other water parameters must be assessed together.
- Organic matter raises oxygen demand; nutrients can cause eutrophication. **A coliform count alone does not quantify BOD, dissolved-oxygen depletion or nutrient loading**.
## Standards and methods
- CPCB organised-bathing guidance: **500 desirable /2,500 maximum permissible faecal-coliform MPN per 100 mL**. PDF's unqualified 500 maximum and universal WHO 200 recreational limit are misleading. [CPCB restoration guidance](https://cpcb.nic.in/wqm/Ind-Guidelines-RestWaterBodies.pdf).
- Drinking-water **E. coli should not be detectable in 100 mL**; do not replace this with a vague standard for every total-coliform group in every context.
- **MPN:** statistical estimate from dilution/fermentation; **CFU:** cultured colony count; not interchangeable numerical units without the relevant method.
- Multiple-tube fermentation, membrane filtration and enzyme-substrate tests; use sampling protocols, repeat measurements and transparent laboratories.
## Control
- Sewage interception/STPs, reliable operation, safe sanitation, runoff management, riparian buffers and enforcement; publish accessible findings and address sources upstream.
- River-bathing management must assess multiple parameters and maintain infrastructure beyond festivals. Clear communication should avoid declaring water safe from one favourable metric alone.

topics.title: Election Commission appointments and institutional independence
topics.subject: Indian Polity
topics.markdown:
## Constitutional institution
- **ECI established 25 January 1950; Article 324 /Part XV**. Supervises elections to Parliament, State legislatures, President and Vice-President; **State Election Commissions** handle local-body elections.
- Currently **CEC +two ECs**; Constitution does not permanently fix three. Brief multi-member phase **1989**, reverted 1990, then multi-member again **1993**.
## 2023 appointment law
- **Anoop Baranwal, 2023:** interim PM–Opposition leader–CJI committee **until Parliament enacted a law**; do not present it as the committee under the later statute.
- **2023 Act, effective 2 February 2024**: President appoints on recommendation of **PM +PM-nominated Union Cabinet Minister +Lok Sabha Leader of Opposition**; largest Opposition party's leader acts where no recognised LoP. [Official Act](https://www.indiacode.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/19721/1/a2023-49.pdf).
- Search committee: **Law Minister +two Secretary-rank-or-above members**; prepares **five names**. Selection committee may consider persons outside the panel.
- Eligibility: current/former Secretary-equivalent officers with integrity and election-management experience/knowledge. Senior-most EC's promotion to CEC is **not legally automatic**.
- **Six years or age 65, whichever earlier; no reappointment**; combined EC/CEC tenure limits apply. Final Act provides Supreme Court judge-equivalent pay, not the earlier bill's Cabinet Secretary formulation.
- **CEC removal:** like Supreme Court judge; other ECs removable only on CEC recommendation. Removal protections and selection rules are different safeguards.
## Independence debate and recall
- Executive majority/CJI exclusion raises perceived-partisanship concerns; constitutional accountability needs fair selection, transparent criteria, secure tenure and reasoned decisions. February litigation remained pending; do not invent its outcome.
- **2017 PYQ: only statement 3 correct**—ECI resolves recognised-party split/merger disputes. ECI is not five-member; Home Ministry does not decide general/by-election schedules.

topics.title: EAST, nuclear fusion and the path to usable energy
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
