## Experiment and physics
- China's **EAST**, Hefei, superconducting **tokamak**: magnetic confinement of plasma in a toroidal chamber; “artificial Sun” is a nickname.
- **20 January 2025: 1,066 seconds** high-confinement plasma operation at about **70 million°C**. This is a confinement achievement, **not commercial electricity or proof of net power gain**; PDF's 100 million°C is not the reported figure for this record. [ITER account](https://www.iter.org/node/20687/achievements-east-and-west).
| Fusion | Fission |
| --- | --- |
| Light nuclei combine | Heavy nuclei split |
| D–T reaction yields helium +neutron, **17.6 MeV** | Typical U-235 fission releases about **200 MeV** |
| Confinement/heating needed | Controlled chain reaction in reactor |
- Source's “fusion always more energy **per reaction**” is false; energy **per unit fuel mass** is a different comparison.
## Fuel, safety and engineering
- **Deuterium** available from water; **tritium scarce**, must be produced/bred, commonly using lithium concepts. Both are not equally abundant off-the-shelf fuels.
- Plasma cannot sustain an ordinary fission-like runaway chain reaction; nevertheless heat loads, neutron damage, activated components and tritium handling require safeguards.
- Fusion is not automatically **zero radioactive waste /zero lifecycle emissions /cheap**. Commercial viability needs net electricity, long-duration reliability, fuel breeding, maintainable materials and competitive costs.
- **ITER, Cadarache, France:** international experimental project; India one of seven members alongside China, EU, Japan, Korea, Russia and US. Not a commercial power station.
- Magnets, cooling, plasma stability, materials, breeding blankets and international research are complementary tasks. A laboratory duration record does not by itself replace solar, wind or existing generation.

topics.title: Aravalli safari proposal and ecosystem protection
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Proposal and ecology
- Proposed **10,000-acre** safari park in **Gurugram/Nuh, Haryana**; February source reports objections by retired forest officers. “World's largest” is a proposal claim, not completed achievement.
- Aravallis support groundwater recharge, habitat connectivity and ecological buffering in a heavily urbanising/water-stressed region. Traffic, construction and water-intensive attractions may undermine these functions.
- Captive-animal exhibits/tourism are not automatically equivalent to protecting native wildlife and functioning habitat.
## Geography and source corrections
- Ancient **Proterozoic fold belt/residual hills**, extending through **Gujarat, Rajasthan, Haryana and Delhi**; not formed by the recent India–Eurasia collision that built the Himalaya.
- Broadly hundreds of kilometres long; mountain range, geologically buried extension and visible hill belt are different measures. Do not treat source average-height figures as the maximum elevation.
- **Carbon dating measures suitable organic material**, not the age of copper metal itself; archaeological context can date mining activity.
## Legal and policy assessment
- Forest classification, diversion permissions, protected-area notifications, ESZ rules and applicable court orders require project-specific examination; neither every activity everywhere nor all areas within a universal 10 km strip share one blanket ban.
- **ESZ extent is site-specific** and can vary; protection extends to sensitive corridors where notified. Conservation/restoration priority needs environmental assessment and legal compliance.
- Compare low-impact community tourism with large built attractions; assess water budgets, cumulative impacts, native restoration, wildlife welfare and transparent local consultation.
- Employment benefits do not automatically outweigh ecological damage. Track actual forest condition, hydrology and livelihoods rather than an attraction's advertised scale.

topics.title: Constitutional morality: values, methods and limits
topics.subject: Ethics
topics.markdown:
## Meaning and origin
- Fidelity to constitutional forms, lawful authority, rights and democratic restraint; liberty, equality, dignity, pluralism and accountability guide public conduct.
- **George Grote**'s account influenced **Ambedkar's 4 November 1948** Constituent Assembly speech. Constitutional habits must be cultivated; institutional loyalty and lawful dissent matter amid partisan disagreement. [Assembly debate](https://www.constitutionofindia.net/debates/04-nov-1948/).
- Not explicitly named as a defined constitutional provision; the idea draws from constitutional text, structure and commitments, not a decision-maker's personal moral preference.
## Case connections
| Case | Relevant theme |
| --- | --- |
| Kesavananda Bharati, **1973** | Basic structure and limits on constitutional change |
| S.P. Gupta, **1981** | First Judges case; source “1982” can be a report citation, not judgment year |
| Naz Foundation, **2009** | Rights versus prevailing social prejudice; source 2010 date is wrong |
| Manoj Narula, **2014** | Constitutional conduct/public responsibility |
| Puttaswamy, **2017** | Privacy, dignity and autonomy |
| NCT Delhi /Navtej Singh Johar, **2018** | Democratic constitutional conduct; equality and individual dignity |
- Cases have distinct holdings; do not imply one broad phrase replaces the detailed legal reasoning or that Naz's subsequent litigation history did not occur.
## Application and critique
- Officials: act within powers, give reasons, treat opponents/citizens equally and resist partisan pressure. Citizens: participate, scrutinise government and respect lawful institutions.
- Benefits: minority protection, rule of law, accountable institutions and inclusive citizenship. Critiques: vagueness, selective use, judicial overreach and weak popular legitimacy.
- Response: transparent reasons grounded in text/precedent, consistent standards, context-sensitive proportionality, institutional restraint and active democratic oversight.
- **Constitutional morality ≠popular approval of every judgment**; protect rights while explaining how the relevant institution has authority to act.

topics.title: Distributed denial of service and cyber resilience
topics.subject: Internal Security of India
topics.markdown:
## Attack and objective
- **DDoS:** distributed traffic/requests exhaust a service's bandwidth or processing resources, degrading **availability** for legitimate users.
- Compromised computers/IoT devices in **botnets** are common sources; reflection/amplification can also misuse other infrastructure. Not every source is necessarily a knowingly participating user or compromised machine.
- **DoS** can originate from one source; distributed origin complicates filtering. Floods can target network, protocol or application resources.
- DDoS does not inherently require stealing data; “never breaches security” is too absolute. A disruption may coexist with or distract from another intrusion.
## Defensive chain
- Monitor abnormal traffic →coordinate with ISP/defence provider →filter/rate-limit appropriate requests →maintain service redundancy →preserve logs and investigate.
- Capacity planning, DDoS protection, resilient load balancing, secure IoT updates and incident-response rehearsals; avoid blocking legitimate users indiscriminately.
- Government/financial services and elections depend on availability; clear public communication and recovery accountability reduce disruption. [CISA guidance](https://www.cisa.gov/sites/default/files/publications/understanding-and-responding-to-ddos-attacks_508c.pdf).

topics.title: India–Qatar: strategic partnership and energy ties
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## Background and February 2025 agreements
- Qatar independent **1971**; diplomatic relations with India **1973**. Emir **Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al-Thani** visited India **17–18 February 2025**; ties elevated to a **strategic partnership**.
- Aim to **double trade to US$28 billion over five years**; revised **DTAA** signed; prospective trade talks do not mean an FTA was concluded. [Joint communiqué](https://mofa.gov.qa/en/latest-articles/statements/qatar--india-issue-joint-communique-on-occasion-of-hh-the-amir%27s-visit).
- Source approximately US$15 billion trade differs from official FY2023–24 **about US$14 billion**; doubling target uses the latter scale, not exactly 15→28.
## Why Qatar matters
- Major **LNG supplier**, long-term Petronet arrangements, crude/petrochemical/fertiliser imports; Indian machinery, textiles, food, jewellery and services exports.
- Qatari investment in infrastructure/finance; Indian construction/IT firms; energy supply diversification must accompany long-term dependence.
- Large Indian diaspora: source **~7.5 lakh /over 20 schools /~600 prisoners** are dated figures; labour protection, consular access and recruitment safeguards matter more than memorising an undated total.
- Security: naval exchanges, maritime cooperation, counter-terrorism/cybersecurity; Qatar's mediation role and GCC membership connect to India's West Asia diplomacy.
- Ex-naval officer **Purnendu Tiwary's return issue** remained a diplomatic concern in the source; distinguish release from custody and permission to leave Qatar rather than assuming continued imprisonment.
- Balance energy/investment gains with expatriate welfare, geopolitical volatility and due process; **GCC comprises Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and UAE**.

topics.title: Employment, unemployment and PLFS measures
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Measures and classification
- **Labour force =employed +unemployed**; unemployed means seeking/available for work under the applicable survey definition, not everyone without a salary.
- **UR =unemployed ÷labour force ×100**; **LFPR =labour force ÷population ×100**; **WPR =employed ÷population ×100**. Always specify age group, rural/urban and reference period.
- **PLFS, NSO/MoSPI**: source-era annual rural/urban estimates under usual/current weekly status, quarterly urban CWS estimates. **Usual status** reflects a longer reference period; **CWS** uses the preceding seven days.
- Sampling and student/individual employment classification matter; missing formal contracts does **not make informal workers statistically unemployed**.
## Types and traps
| Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Disguised | Extra workers add little/no marginal output; may still count as employed |
| Seasonal | Work available only in specified seasons |
| Structural | Skill/location/sector mismatch |
| Frictional | Job-search or transition interval |
| Technological | Displacement following technology change; new jobs may also emerge |
| Cyclical | Demand downturn reduces employment |
- **Vulnerable employment** describes insecure categories such as own-account/contributing-family work; not an unemployment category. Source “69% year-on-year automation loss” misrepresents a risk estimate, not observed annual job destruction.
## Causes and response
- Weak labour demand, skill mismatch, seasonal agriculture, unequal access/discrimination and mobility barriers; population size alone does not mechanically determine unemployment.
- **MGNREGA** rural work guarantee, **PMKVY /PM-DAKSH** skills, **SMILE** targeted rehabilitation/livelihood support, Startup India; programme coverage and quality need assessment.
- Improve labour-intensive growth, apprenticeships, portable benefits, women's safe access/childcare, market-linked training and credible placement outcomes.
- Falling UR alone can reflect lower participation; assess job quality, earnings and underemployment alongside the headline rate.

topics.title: India’s greenhouse-gas inventory and climate commitments
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Inventory: use a stated year and denominator
- India's **BUR-4**, submitted **30 December 2024**, reports **2020** emissions. Sector shares: **energy 75.66%; agriculture 13.72%; IPPU 8.06%; waste 2.56%**. Correct source's loose 74/14/8/4 “latest” split. [Official inventory summary](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2089589&lang=2&reg=48).
- Fossil combustion →CO₂; livestock/rice/waste →CH₄; fertiliser/industrial processes →N₂O; refrigeration and specialised processes →fluorinated gases.
- India's large total emissions coexist with lower per-capita emissions; “third largest /7%” depends on year, gases, territorial accounting and inclusion of land use.
- Source gas shares **75/15/7/<3** are not a verified inventory table; compare gases using **CO₂-equivalent** and a stated warming-potential methodology.
## Commitments and programmes
- Updated **2022 NDC**: **45% reduction in GDP emission intensity by 2030 from 2005**; about **50% cumulative installed electricity capacity from non-fossil sources**; additional **2.5–3 billion tonnes CO₂-equivalent** forest/tree sink by 2030.
- **Net-zero 2070**, announced at COP26; **500 GW non-fossil capacity by 2030** is a separate policy ambition. Neither means 50% of actual generation or an absolute 45% emission cut.
- Solar mission **2010**, renewable deployment, PAT efficiency, clean transport, green hydrogen **2023 /5 MMT annually by 2030**, afforestation and waste/bioenergy improvements.
- Source assigns the whole 500 GW target to the original Solar Mission and claims “40% renewable electricity”: inaccurate scope/denominators. Non-fossil includes nuclear; programmes/timetables differ.
## Equity and implementation
- Coal dependence, growing demand, technology/finance access, agricultural methane and difficult industrial processes; protect energy access and a just transition while reducing intensity.
- Mitigation reduces emissions; **adaptation funds** reduce vulnerability, not necessarily carbon output. Forest sinks need ecological integrity and durable protection.
- **GHG Protocol:** emissions accounting/management standards, not a UN treaty or World Bank REDD+ programme. **INDCs:** countries' intended climate-action pledges, not refugee or AIIB commitments.

topics.title: Saturn’s rings, icy moons and uncertain age
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Competing age hypotheses
- Saturn's icy rings appear relatively clean; dust accumulation informed **young-ring estimates around 100 million years**, but age remains debated.
- **December 2024 study** models micrometeoroid impact/vaporisation: charged impactor material may leave the ring plane or be absorbed by Saturn. Clean appearance can therefore coexist with older rings; **does not prove a 4.5-billion-year age**. [Primary study](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41561-024-01598-9).
- Dust retention assumptions, ring mass and formation/dynamical models all matter. Proposed future sampling missions are proposals, not approved launches.
## Planet recall
- **Sixth from Sun; second largest; gas giant** dominated by hydrogen/helium; Jupiter and Saturn are gas giants, **Uranus/Neptune are ice giants**.
- Approximate **120,536 km equatorial diameter**, **95 Earth masses**, **10.7-hour rotation /29.5-year orbit /26.7° tilt**; no solid accessible surface. Do not call metallic hydrogen a simple solid planetary core.
- North-polar hexagon, strong winds/auroras and magnetosphere; major rings **A–G**, mainly water ice with dust/rock. Thickness varies; one 10–30 m number is not every ring's thickness.
## Moons and missions
| Moon | Recall |
| --- | --- |
| Titan | Larger than Mercury; nitrogen atmosphere; methane/ethane lakes |
| Enceladus | Subsurface ocean, south-polar icy plumes; material supplies the **E ring** |
| Mimas | Large Herschel crater |
| Iapetus | Contrasting bright/dark hemispheres |
- Source **146 moons** is a dated count, not permanently current. Ocean thickness is model-dependent; plume organics/hydrogen support habitability research, **not proof of life**.
- **Pioneer 11 1979; Voyager 1 1980 /2 1981; Cassini 2004–2017**, Huygens Titan landing **2005**. Europa is **Jupiter's** moon; Clipper launched **October 2024**.
- Source **Dragonfly 2027** timetable is outdated: NASA plans **2028 launch**; distinguish launch from Titan arrival. [NASA Dragonfly](https://science.nasa.gov/mission/dragonfly/).
- Practice: Saturn has no solid surface; Enceladus's ocean/plumes distinguish it from Titan and Saturn's atmospheric hexagon.
## March 2025 moon census
- Recognition of **128 additional moons** brought Saturn's confirmed total to **274 in March 2025**. Moon counts change with discoveries; this is a dated census. [NASA](https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/saturniansatfact.html).
- Edward Ashton's team used Canada–France–Hawaii Telescope observations and image stacking to detect faint objects; multi-epoch tracking establishes orbits.
- The new moons are small irregular satellites, often in distant inclined/retrograde orbits, unlike large regular satellites such as Titan and Rhea.
- Orbital groups and fragments help reconstruct capture and collision histories. Proposed explanations for Saturn–Jupiter count differences are hypotheses, not a rule that all Jupiter moons are rocky.

topics.title: Death penalty and the rarest-of-rare doctrine
topics.subject: Indian Polity
topics.markdown:
## Doctrine and case distinctions
- **Jagmohan Singh**, decided **1972** (reported 1973), upheld capital punishment; **Bachan Singh 1980**: life imprisonment is the rule, death an exception when the alternative is unquestionably foreclosed.
- Consider **both crime and offender**, aggravating/mitigating circumstances and genuine reform prospects; brutality or public outrage alone does not automatically justify death.
- **Machhi Singh 1983:** manner, motive, socially abhorrent nature, magnitude and victim circumstances; illustrative guidance, not five automatic statutory switches.
- **Mithu 1983:** struck down mandatory IPC 303 death sentence for murder by a life convict, under **Articles 14/21**.
- **Law Commission 262, 2015:** recommended abolition except **terrorism-related offences and waging war**; recommendation, not enacted general abolition. [Commission report catalogue](https://lawcommissionofindia.nic.in/cat_Indian_Penal_Code/).
## February source examples
- RG Kar rape/murder: trial court gave **Sanjay Roy life imprisonment**; Sharon Raj poisoning: trial court gave **Greeshma death**. Different case facts/sentencing evidence and appellate stages matter; trial outcomes are not final national precedent.
- **2022 sentencing-framework reference** sought proper collection/consideration of mitigating evidence; source does not establish a completed final Constitution Bench ruling.
- Court procedures, High Court confirmation, appeals/review and constitutional mercy powers are distinct from initial trial sentencing.
## Ethics and reform
- Debate: deterrence/retribution and victim justice versus irreversible error, unequal legal assistance, inconsistent sentencing and rehabilitation.
- “140+ countries abolished” may combine law/practice categories; no undated number substitutes for definitions. Article **19 concerns specified freedoms**, not a provision titled “freedom of life”.
- Improve competent defence, mitigation reports, reasoned proportional sentencing, timely review and survivor support. Special fixed/non-remittable life sentences require judicial/legal authority, not a universal ban on parole.

topics.title: Digital content: free speech, obscenity and OTT regulation
topics.subject: Governance in India
topics.markdown:
## Rights and statutory thresholds
- **Article 19(1)(a)** expression; **19(2)** permits only constitutionally valid reasonable restrictions. Public dislike/vulgarity ≠automatic criminal obscenity.
- **Apoorva Arora, 19 March 2024:** distinguish profanity from legally obscene material and assess content/context under the law; it does **not automatically decide every later creator's liability**. [Supreme Court judgment](https://www.livelaw.in/pdf_upload/243-apoorva-arora-v-state-19-mar-2024-537519.pdf).
- Modern community-standards/context analysis differs from the old **Hicklin** isolated-passage test; do not present them as one identical current test.
- **IT Act 69A** blocking: sovereignty/integrity, defence, security, friendly foreign relations, public order and preventing incitement to related cognizable offences. “Decency/morality” is not a freestanding listed 69A ground; **67/67A/67B** address different prohibited electronic content.
## OTT framework and February advisory
- **IT Rules 2021**: publisher grievance officer →industry self-regulatory body →government oversight. Distinguish OTT publishers, digital news and social-media intermediaries' obligations.
- Age ratings **U /U-A 7+ /U-A 13+ /U-A 16+ /A**; parental locks for **U-A 13+ and higher**, reliable age verification for **A**. Advisory compliance is not the creation of a new CBFC pre-certification system.
- Relevant laws include **BNS, POCSO, Indecent Representation of Women Act 1986 and IT Act**; each has a defined scope. Television **Cable Act 1995** and cinema **Cinematograph Act 1952** use different frameworks.
- Broadcasting-bill proposals and committee comments were not a February 2025 enacted universal “digital censor board”; ongoing legal challenges/implementation must be distinguished from draft policy.
## Assess regulation
- Protect children and address lawful harms through transparent rules, notice/reasons, appeals and independent scrutiny; disproportionate threats can chill journalism/art.
- Source's techno-patrimonialism/DBT-electoral-loyalty link is a political interpretation, not established proof every transfer purchases loyalty.
- International examples have different scopes: MPA ratings are not universal US statutory OTT censorship; EU on-demand obligations are not identical to every broadcasting rule.
- Improve grievance handling, media literacy and child safeguards while preserving lawful dissent and consistent, proportionate enforcement.
## X petition and Sahyog: March 2025
- IT Act **section 69A** concerns blocking public access with specified grounds and rules; **section 79** concerns conditional intermediary immunity/safe harbour.
- *Shreya Singhal* (2015) upheld 69A with safeguards and read section 79 actual knowledge narrowly around court orders or appropriate government notification, linked to Article 19(2).
- X alleged section 79 notices/Sahyog bypassed 69A safeguards; government characterised them as liability notices and coordination. These were **litigating positions**, not a final March 2025 judgment.
- A portal does not create unlimited powers for every police officer. Assess statutory authority, reasons, notice/hearing, review, transparency and remedy against unlawful removal.
- Prompt lawful action on illegal content and protection from arbitrary censorship require clear procedures; blocking, takedown and immunity loss are different legal effects.

topics.title: Deep-sea research stations, cold seeps and maritime strategy
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## February source proposal
- China reportedly approved a **South China Sea station ~2,000 m deep**, aiming for **2030** operation; approval/timetable is not proof construction or commercial resource extraction completed.
- Research goals: methane fluxes, cold-seep ecology, geological processes and deep-sea technology. Pressure, corrosion, power, life support and evacuation are demanding constraints.
- Surface ships +unmanned submersibles +seabed observatories/fibre links support measurements; AI assists data analysis but does not replace scientific interpretation or safe operational decisions.
## Concepts and limits
- **Cold seep:** relatively low-temperature release of hydrocarbons/fluids; chemosynthetic microbes support ecosystems. **Hydrothermal vents** are distinct heated systems.
- **Methane hydrate:** methane enclosed in water-ice crystal structures, stable under suitable high-pressure/low-temperature conditions; extraction faces technical/economic and methane-leakage risks.
- Species/biochemical research may yield useful compounds; potential medicinal value is not an approved drug. Geological monitoring supports hazard understanding, **not reliable exact earthquake prediction**.
## Geopolitics
- South China Sea disputes involve China and several neighbours, including Philippines, Vietnam and Malaysia; a scientific facility does **not itself confer lawful sovereignty**.
- Research infrastructure can have dual-use surveillance/resource implications. Claims that it automatically makes China the undisputed world leader are forecasts.
- Assess marine safeguards, transparent research, UNCLOS-based rights and international cooperation; scientific ambition and sustainable extraction are separate tests.

topics.title: Project Cheetah, Kuno and Gandhi Sagar
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Species and reintroduction
- **Acinonyx jubatus**: fastest land mammal, slender/spotted open-habitat predator; scrub, grassland and savanna, not only treeless desert.
- Cheetah declared extinct in India **1952**. African animals brought to **Kuno, MP: eight Namibia September 2022 +12 South Africa February 2023**; translocation of 20 founders is not evidence all survived.
- February source proposed more animals at **Gandhi Sagar Wildlife Sanctuary, MP**, around **368 km²**, with grassland/dry deciduous/riverine habitats. Prey availability requires assessment, not an automatic guarantee of viability.
- Global species **IUCN Vulnerable**; Asiatic population in Iran **Critically Endangered**; **CITES Appendix I /Indian Schedule I**, correcting source Schedule II. [Official schedule](https://upload.indiacode.nic.in/schedulefile?aid=AC_CEN_16_18_00007_197253_1517807324579&rid=759).
## Risks and evaluation
- Habitat/prey limitations, disease, conflict, dispersal and adaptation; mortality causes need veterinary evidence rather than attributing every death to collars or starvation.
- Source **December 2024: 24 animals, 12 adults/12 cubs** is a dated snapshot, not the February/current total. Founder subspecies and historical Asiatic population differ.
- **Cheetah Conservation Fund, 1990, Namibia**; NTCA/WII monitoring and habitat/community work support India's programme. [Action-plan overview](https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=1850587&lang=2&reg=48).
- Judge success by long-term survival, breeding, genetic diversity, suitable habitat, community benefits and a self-sustaining population—not arrival ceremonies or short-term cub counts alone.
## Gandhi Sagar development
- **20 April 2025:** Gandhi Sagar Sanctuary, Mandsaur district, Madhya Pradesh, received the two cheetahs **Prabhas and Pavak** transferred from Kuno; it became the programme's second Indian site. This transfer is distinct from proposed additional imports from Africa. [Akashvani announcement](https://newsonair.gov.in/two-cheetahs-to-be-released-in-mps-gandhisagar-sanctuary-today/).
- Grassland, dry deciduous forest and riverine patches offer a varied landscape. Assess prey density, enclosure/free-ranging transitions, veterinary capacity, connectivity and community impacts; listing chital, chinkara, nilgai or wild pig does not establish adequate prey quantitatively.
- Source repeat **Schedule II** is incorrect: cheetah is in Indian **Schedule I**. December 2024 survival counts remain dated snapshots; do not use them as April 2025 totals. Imported founders/cubs and future planned animals are separate categories.

topics.title: Polarised moonlight and nocturnal bull-ant navigation
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Physics and experiment
- Polarisation concerns electric-field orientation; scattering creates patterned partial polarisation in sky light. It is not simply loss of brightness or conversion to infrared.
- Moonlight reflects sunlight; its much weaker celestial polarisation pattern can supply orientation cues even when the Moon is obscured.
- **Myrmecia pyriformis /M. midas**, Australian nocturnal bull ants: researchers rotated polarisation filters above returning ants; systematic heading shifts supported use of the **e-vector compass**.
- Evidence extends across tested full/quarter/crescent conditions, with light level influencing performance. Source's “second animal” is a discovery-summary claim, not a complete count of all species capable of this behaviour.
- **Dung beetles** also use nocturnal celestial/polarisation cues; bees/ants are known for solar cues. Species capabilities and experimental conditions should not be generalised to every insect.
- Research published in **eLife 2024**, not necessarily a new study first conducted in February 2025. [University account](https://lighthouse.mq.edu.au/article/july-2024/ants-navigate-the-night-by-moonlight-discovery).
## Recall
- **Ambient polarisation rotated →heading changes →evidence for directional use**, not proof ants use no landmarks, smells or other navigation information.
- Sensory adaptation, ecology and bio-inspired navigation; supplied questions are coaching practice, not official PYQs.

topics.title: Disaster-resilient telecom infrastructure
topics.subject: Governance in India
topics.markdown:
## CDRI–DoT framework
- **DRRAF report launched 12 February 2025**: disaster risk/resilience assessment for telecom infrastructure; national and subnational planning. [DoT announcement](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2102281&lang=2&reg=48).
- Cyclones, floods, earthquakes, power failure and damaged coastal cable landings can cut communications precisely when warnings/rescue need them.
| Weak link | Resilience measure |
| --- | --- |
| Towers /overhead lines | Risk-appropriate structural design, siting, protected cables |
| Power /fuel supply | Elevate equipment, diverse backup, adequate storage/emergency access |
| Cable landing /backhaul | Protect sites, diversify routes and plan specialist repairs |
| Fragmented response | Shared damage data, drills, operator–government coordination |
- **Dig-once:** coordinate underground utilities during excavation; buried cable still faces flood/digging risk. Subsea fibre offers high-capacity intercontinental links, not automatically lower latency than every land route.
- **Parametric insurance** pays on defined hazard triggers; fast payment but **basis risk** means payment may differ from actual loss.
- Humanitarian communications, redundancy, maintenance and trained teams matter alongside new infrastructure. Measure restored service/time and vulnerable-community access.

topics.title: Software-defined radios and defence logistics procurement
topics.subject: Internal Security of India
topics.markdown:
## Contracts signed 20 February 2025
- Total **₹1,917.47 crore**: **BEL, 149 Coast Guard SDRs, ₹1,220.12 crore**; **ACE/JCB India, 1,868 rough-terrain forklifts, ₹697.35 crore**. [Defence Ministry](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2104928&reg=48&lang=2).
- **SDR:** software-configurable communication functions/waveforms support multi-band/mode operation, secure voice/data and network interoperability; not automatically immune to interception/jamming/cyberattack.
- **Forklift:** material-handling/logistics vehicle; improves loading/warehousing efficiency, not a combat tank or weapon.
## Operational and industry assessment
- Coast Guard maritime law enforcement, search/rescue, fisheries/environment protection and Navy coordination need reliable communications; field conditions, spectrum and interoperability require testing.
- Domestic manufacture and MSME supply chains support jobs/strategic autonomy; an Indian-based company label is not proof every component or design is domestically owned.
- Contracts ≠completed delivery. Train users, secure software updates, maintain spares/lifecycle support and assess operational reliability.
- Source **7,516 km coastline /2.4 million km² EEZ** are dated/conventional measures; survey methodology matters. **DAP 2020 /iDEX /positive indigenisation lists** are distinct tools; DPEPP2020 was a **draft policy**, not automatically a fully notified final framework.

topics.title: Cancer, caregiver costs and children’s education
topics.subject: Social Problems In India
topics.markdown:
## Burden beyond hospital bills
- Illness can remove a patient's/caregiver's earnings while increasing travel, accommodation, food and psychological-care costs; uninsured indirect costs can persist even where hospital treatment is covered.
- Children may lose schooling, assume unpaid care or paid work, and experience distress; reduced education can damage future earnings and deepen poverty. Individual stories illustrate mechanisms, not a measured national effect size.
- Source **Sridevi, Hyderabad /Meena, Pune** are reported examples; protect dignity and do not treat every cancer family as having identical outcomes.
## Existing support and gaps
- **PM-JAY** eligible hospital care, State financial assistance, pensions and travel concessions can help, but eligibility/availability differs; source's State/airline list is not a universal guaranteed entitlement.
- Formal employees and informal workers have unequal leave/income protections. Health-insurance coverage does not automatically reimburse all caregiver wages or children's educational losses.
## Policy response
- Need-based caregiver/income support, safe employment protection, accommodation/travel assistance and informed insurance design.
- School retention grants/scholarships, flexible attendance/learning, counselling and teacher coordination; digital learning alone can exclude families without devices or connectivity.
- Link oncology/social work with welfare referral and school support; monitor access, dropout, household financial hardship and follow-up rather than only hospital claims.
- Connect **SDGs 3,4,10**: integrated health, education and inequality policy. Proposals for paid leave/non-medical reimbursement are recommendations, not already universal legal guarantees.

topics.title: Oarfish, folklore and earthquake evidence
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Species
- Giant oarfish **Regalecus glesne**, family **Regalecidae**, order **Lampriformes**; long, ribbon-shaped silvery body, red dorsal fin; among the longest bony fishes, reported lengths about **11 m**.
- Tropical/temperate oceans, commonly deep midwater; source **200–1,000 m** is typical rather than an absolute range. Feeds on plankton/small animals; dorsal-fin undulation and near-vertical posture are distinctive.
- Rare beach/surface sightings may involve illness or ocean conditions; an unusual sighting does not by itself identify the cause.
## Myth versus testable claim
- Japanese **Ryūgū no tsukai**, “messenger from the sea god's palace”; folklore links appearances to earthquakes/tsunamis.
- The fact sightings preceded a famous earthquake does **not establish predictive power**; need systematic records including sightings without earthquakes and earthquakes without sightings.
- Source refers to **2019 Japanese analysis** finding no significant relationship; no validated oarfish-based earthquake warning system follows from this material.
- Climate change, pollution, gas release and mining are possible environmental concerns, not proved causes of the specific Mexican sighting.
- Use authoritative seismic monitoring and scientifically supported early warning; warning detects an event already underway, **not exact advance prediction from animal omens**.
- Respect cultural narratives while explaining evidence; source's “not endangered because rare interactions” is not a valid reasoning method for assessing conservation status.

topics.title: Quick Reaction Surface-to-Air Missile
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Design and role
- **DRDO QRSAM**, mobile Army air defence for mechanised formations; surveillance/tracking while moving and engagement after a brief halt, rather than an unqualified claim it fires in every movement state.
- Canisterised surface-to-air missiles, phased-array radars, inertial/mid-course data-link guidance and active-radar terminal seeker; high-explosive fragmentation warhead.
- Source **25–30 km range**, **6 km altitude**, **Mach1.8–2**, **30-second response** are reported/variant figures, not a universally guaranteed envelope. Target geometry, radar tracking and electronic conditions matter.
- Complements layered air defence against aircraft, helicopters and suitable unmanned/cruise-missile threats; not identical to Akash, naval Barak or S-400.
## Trials and procurement
- Multiple Chandipur trials since 2017; **six Army evaluation flight tests completed September 2022**, correcting the source's assertion all final trials ended December2021. [Official tests](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1857724&lang=2&reg=48).
- February forecast of contract in **four–five months /production 18 months after signing** is a conditional timetable, not delivered/operational status.
- Reliability across terrain/weather, multi-target engagement, interoperability, maintenance, crew training and secure indigenous supply determine practical capability.

topics.title: Olive ridley turtles and coastal conservation
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Species and nesting
- **Lepidochelys olivacea**, olive-coloured carapace; warm Pacific/Atlantic/Indian waters. **Arribada:** synchronised mass nesting; not every individual nests only in mass events.
- Odisha **Gahirmatha, Rushikulya, Devi-mouth** landscapes important; Gahirmatha a major rookery. **IUCN Vulnerable /CITES Appendix I /Indian Schedule I**.
- Predominantly animal prey including crustaceans/molluscs; turtle species have differing diets, so “all turtles carnivorous” is false.
## Threat →safeguard
- Fishing bycatch →seasonal exclusion/enforcement and **Turtle Excluder Devices (TEDs)**, grids/escape openings within appropriate trawls, not merely an extra exit cover on any net.
- Beach development/light disturbance →nesting-habitat safeguards; litter/plastics →source control and safer waste systems.
- Temperature-dependent sex determination relates to **nest incubation temperature**, not simply ocean-water temperature; warming and extreme conditions can alter ratios/survival.
- Tagging tracks movement; avoid assuming every predator listed in a global article occurs at every Odisha site.
- Coast Guard **Operation Olivia**, source early-1980s origin, seasonal patrol/protection and unlawful-trawling control; nesting season extends beyond an absolute November–December-only window.
## PYQ recall
- **2015 national aquatic animal: Gangetic dolphin**, not olive ridley.
- **2019:** some turtles, fish and marine mammals are herbivores; some snakes viviparous—**all four true**. Examples: green turtles, plant-eating fish, dugongs/manatees and live-bearing snakes.

topics.title: Judicial backlog and mediation
topics.subject: Governance in India
topics.markdown:
## Delay and appropriate alternatives
- Source **2024 snapshots:** SC ~82,000; HCs ~62 lakh; subordinate courts nearly five crore; ~50 lakh cases older than ten years. Totals depend on date/court scope; use NJDG for a comparable series, not these as current counts.
- Causes: vacancies/staff/infrastructure, scheduling/adjournments, process complexity and avoidable government litigation. Source government **50% /21 judges per million** need denominator/year; court use is not inherently frivolous.
- **Mediation:** neutral facilitator helps parties reach a voluntary settlement; mediator does not impose a binding adjudicated award as an arbitrator/judge does.
## Law and safeguards
- **Mediation Act 2023**, already an Act, **not a pending “Mediation Bill2023”**. Commencement is provision-specific; enacted text does not mean all institutions/procedures were operational in February2025. [Official Act](https://www.indiacode.nic.in/indiacode/handle/123456789/19637?col=123456789%2F1362&view_type=search).
- Final Act's general pre-litigation model is **voluntary**, not universal mandatory mediation. Some commercial disputes have separate pre-institution requirements; not every crime/public-law issue is suitable for settlement.
- Confidentiality, trained impartial mediators, informed consent and protection against coercion/unequal bargaining; a settlement can have specified legal effect, but not every failed mediation removes access to court.
## Delivery reforms
- Triage suitable family/civil/commercial cases, competent mediators, legal aid and tracked referrals; settlement statistics need durability/fairness, not only disposal counts.
- Fill judicial/support vacancies, improve e-court case management and evidence scheduling, reduce routine government appeals and build awareness.
- ADR complements adjudication; it cannot cure every criminal backlog or guarantee every dispute resolves in a few sessions.

topics.title: HKU5-CoV lineage 2: cell entry and zoonotic uncertainty
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## What the study shows
- Researchers reported a bat **merbecovirus HKU5-CoV lineage2**, capable of using **human ACE2** as an entry receptor in laboratory systems. MERS-CoV also a merbecovirus but normally uses **DPP4**, not ACE2; SARS-CoV-2 is a sarbecovirus.
- **Receptor recognition ≠efficient human transmission ≠a human outbreak.** Laboratory cell-entry/organ-model results do not establish person-to-person spread, clinical severity or pandemic inevitability. [Primary Cell study](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0092867425001448).
- **Furin cleavage** concerns viral-protein processing; it is not a receptor that substitutes for ACE2. Source incorrectly compresses these mechanisms into one claim.
- No human infection established by the supplied February account; its fever/cough/diarrhoea list is extrapolated from other diseases, **not observed HKU5-CoV-2 patient symptoms**.
## Surveillance and governance
- Monitor animal–human interfaces and viral evolution, coordinate human/animal/environment data through **One Health**, secure laboratory practice and transparent evidence sharing.
- INSACOG specifically supports SARS-CoV-2 genomic work; emerging-virus preparedness needs broader systems too, not automatic assumption every bat virus falls in its existing mandate.
- Discovery by a Wuhan laboratory does not demonstrate artificial creation, a laboratory leak or COVID-19's origin. Vaccine-company share movements are financial reactions, not clinical-risk evidence.
- Communicate uncertainty accurately; hypothetical mutation possibilities do not justify claims a new pandemic is underway or that an existing vaccine is proven to prevent this virus.

topics.title: Majorana1, qubits and evidence for quantum progress
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Basics and announcement
- **Qubit:** quantum information unit; superposition and entanglement enable suitable quantum algorithms. Entanglement does **not transmit messages instantly**, and quantum computers are not faster for every task.
- **19 February2025 Microsoft Majorana1:** claimed **eight topological qubits**, correcting PDF's four; million-qubit scale a design ambition, not a working million-qubit machine. [Microsoft announcement](https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/blog/quantum/2025/02/19/microsoft-unveils-majorana-1-the-worlds-first-quantum-processor-powered-by-topological-qubits/).
- **1937 Ettore Majorana:** theoretical self-antiparticle fermion concept; condensed-matter **Majorana zero modes** are quasiparticle excitations, distinct from proof of a new fundamental particle.
- **Indium arsenide/aluminium** hybrid structures seek topological superconductivity; superconductors show zero resistance under suitable conditions. Intended topological protection does not guarantee no errors under all disturbances.
## Evidence and policy
- Separate demonstrated device measurements, claimed topological interpretation, qubit operations and scalable fault tolerance; peer review of one measurement paper does not validate every company roadmap claim.
- Prior controversial/retracted evidence underscores replication and open benchmarking; do not replace hype with the equally absolute claim no relevant experimental evidence can exist.
- Applications may include simulation/optimisation and, with sufficiently capable machines, threats to some existing public-key cryptography; not instant defeat of every encryption method today.
- India's **National Quantum Mission2023: ₹6,003.65 crore,2023–24 to2030–31**, computing, communication, sensing/metrology and materials/devices. Institutions include IISc, IITs, TIFR/RRI with strategic-agency work.
- Invest in skills, rigorous research, hardware validation and post-quantum cryptographic transition; count useful logical performance, not physical qubits alone.
- **2022 PYQ: “qubit” →quantum computing**, not cloud, visible-light or wireless communication.
- [Cabinet approval of NQM](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1917888&lang=2&reg=48) confirms outlay and2023–31 period.

topics.title: Global talent shortages and India’s skilled-migration opportunity
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Opportunity and projections
- Source study forecasts **85.2 million global skilled-worker shortfall /US$8.45 trillion unrealised annual revenue by2030**; scenario estimates, not a guaranteed market India can capture in full.
- GCC: construction/manufacturing/healthcare; Europe/UK: healthcare/services; Australia: technology/services/resource efficiency. Demand depends on sector, qualifications, language and immigration policy.
- Skills shortages can coexist with domestic unemployment when competencies/locations differ; a young population does not automatically imply ready internationally employable workers.
## Barriers and safeguards
- Qualification/licence recognition, visas, language, recruitment costs and employer exploitation/trafficking; source blanket “no hostility abroad /Australia always open” is unreliable.
- Mutual-recognition agreements do not automatically license every profession; health professionals need applicable country standards.
- **Skill India, NSDC, PMKVY**, bilateral mobility/worker-protection agreements and transparent recruitment systems can support lawful placement.
- Train to verified demand, regulate recruiters, provide clear contracts/consular assistance, expand language/professional preparation and track placement/earnings.
- Circular migration/remittances and returnee skills can help; balance overseas opportunity with domestic healthcare/skill needs and avoid brain-drain assumptions without evidence.
- Source **US$6.5–9 trillion India GDP2030** is an economic forecast attributed to a speaker, not an achieved outcome or assured benefit from overseas labour demand.

topics.title: Unapproved drug combinations and pharmaceutical-export ethics
topics.subject: Governance in India
topics.markdown:
## Action and correction
- **Tapentadol:** opioid analgesic; **carisoprodol:** centrally acting muscle relaxant. Individually approved products do **not** make their fixed-dose combination approved.
- February2025 action followed reports of Aveo exports to West Africa: stop activities, withdraw export NOCs and act on unauthorised manufacturing permissions. **Joint audit21–22 February2025**, not PDF's2024. [Health Ministry23 February release](https://www.pib.gov.in/newsite/erelcontent.aspx?lang=2&reg=48&relid=267822).
- Official source reports **~1.3 crore tablets/capsules /26 API batches** and wider inspections **905 units /694 actions**; separate seizure from concluded criminal guilt and inspection from permanent closure.
- Addiction/misuse and combined CNS effects are public-health concerns; whether a drug is listed under NDPS is different from whether it is regulated under drug law.
## Institutions and ethics
- **CDSCO**, national regulator under **MoHFW**, New Delhi; headed by **DCGI**. New drugs/trials/imports/standards and specified categories involve central powers; State regulators have important manufacturing/sale enforcement roles.
- **Drugs and Cosmetics Act1940 /Rules /New Drugs and Clinical Trials Rules2019**; devices use their relevant framework. No single officer personally issues every drug licence in India.
- Safe exports require approvals/quality, traceability, importing-country coordination and ethical marketing. Weaker enforcement abroad does not justify exporting unsafe/unapproved combinations.
- Risk-based joint inspections, authentic supply-chain data, recalls/enforcement with due process and international alerts protect patients and India's pharmaceutical credibility.
- Proposal to add substances to NDPS is not proof notification occurred; do not confuse action against this combination with a blanket ban on every lawful standalone product.

topics.title: Source segregation and the municipal waste chain
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Segregation and treatment
- **Source segregation:** separate wet/biodegradable, dry/recyclable and **domestic hazardous** waste; special biomedical/e-waste streams follow appropriate rules.
- Keep streams separate in collection/transport; segregating at home achieves little if mixed again in the truck.
| Stream | Appropriate route |
| --- | --- |
| Suitable wet organics | Composting/biomethanation with contamination controls |
| Dry recyclables | Recovery/recycling through authorised systems |
| Non-recyclable high-calorific residues | Suitable controlled energy recovery, not indiscriminate burning |
| Hazardous/inert/process residues | Appropriate authorised treatment/engineered disposal |
- Benefits: less landfill methane/leachate, better recycling, safer workers and resource recovery; treatment may still generate residues/emissions.
## Rules and programmes
- Source-era **SWM Rules2016**, **Plastic Waste Rules2016/EPR**, **SBM-U2.0** and **SATAT** compressed-biogas support. **2022 SUP ban targets listed products**, not every single-use plastic object.
- Producers' responsibility and municipal obligations differ; blanket plastic/e-waste EPR cannot be attributed solely to SWM Rules.
- **Indore** collection/biogas, **Pune SWaCH** waste-picker integration, **Alappuzha** decentralised composting illustrate approaches; source's30,000-Pune-worker and100%-zero-waste claims require verification.
## Data and governance
- Source **~160,000 tonnes/day generated /79,000 processed /3,159 dumpsites /14 WTE plants**, composition and city segregation shares are mixed dated estimates; not a harmonised current national inventory.
- Sweden's “99% recycling” often conflates material recycling with energy recovery; international segregation, treatment and landfill percentages are different metrics.
- Awareness plus reliable separate collection, ULB capacity, user fees/enforcement, EPR accountability, decentralised organics treatment and dignified waste-worker inclusion.
- WTE is not an automatic answer for high-moisture mixed waste; technology choices need feedstock, pollution control, costs and maintained operation.

topics.title: Social protection, informal workers and the ILO
topics.subject: Social Problems In India
topics.markdown:
## Coverage and dimensions
- Source **24%→49%** rounds the reported **24.4%2021 →48.8%2024** coverage under **at least one social-protection benefit**; not proof everyone covered has comprehensive protection. [Official clarification](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2115391&lang=2&reg=3).
- **Social insurance**: contributory risk protection; **social assistance**: tax-financed support; labour-market programmes support income/work. Adequacy, timely payment and actual access matter with enrolment.
- **e-Shram2021**, worker database; registration is not automatic pension/insurance entitlement. DBT can improve delivery but is **not inherently leakage-free** or free from exclusion.
- **PM-KISAN₹6,000/year**, eligible **PM-JAY** hospital cover, **APY** contributory pension and **MGNREGA100 days per rural household demanding unskilled work**—not100days guaranteed to every individual regardless of demand.
- February2025 Labour Codes enacted but not all implemented; recognition of gig/platform workers did **not automatically make every gig worker an insured ESIC beneficiary**. Scheme announcement, registration and benefit receipt differ.
## ILO recall
- **1919, Treaty of Versailles; Geneva; UN specialised agency1946**. India member since **28June1919**, correcting PDF's1920. [ILO country profile](https://normlex.ilo.org/dyn/nrmlx_en/f?p=NORMLEXPUB%3A11110%3A0%3A%3ANO%3A%3AP11110_COUNTRY_ID%3A102691).
- **Tripartite: governments, employers, workers**; International Labour Conference sets standards; Governing Body executive oversight.
- Reports: **World Employment and Social Outlook, Global Wage Report, World Social Protection Report2024–26, India Wage Report2018**.
- India ratified **C100 equal remuneration, C138 minimum age, C182 worst child labour**; source-era **C87/C98** not ratified. Ratification and domestic implementation are distinct; total convention count changes with time.
- Source187members/DG **GilbertF.Houngbo** are dated institutional facts, not permanent constitutional rules. Cross-country49/70/90/100coverage table lacks comparable definitions.
## Reform
- Informal earnings, digital barriers, gender gaps and portability complicate coverage; reliable funding, outreach, grievance redress and linked schemes are needed.
- Measure effective benefits, adequacy/equity and shock resilience; protect workers through formalisation without assuming informal work means no employment.

topics.title: Right to Information: transparency, privacy and implementation
topics.subject: Governance in India
topics.markdown:
## Statutory framework: revision points
- The right to know is derived from **Article 19(1)(a)**; *State of UP v Raj Narain* was decided in **1975**, not 1976. **RTI Act 2005** supplies the request/disclosure machinery.
- **Section 2(h):** constitutional/statutory/notified public authorities; bodies owned, controlled or substantially financed by government, including substantially financed NGOs. Not every private organisation is directly covered.
- **Section 4:** record management/proactive disclosure; **6:** request procedure; **7:** response timelines; **8:** exemptions/public-interest balance; **19:** first and second appeals; **20:** penalties; **23:** statutory court bar.
- Ordinary request normally **30 days**, life/liberty **48 hours**. Information Commission may impose **₹250 per day, maximum ₹25,000**, on the PIO under section 20 after the statutory process; penalty is not automatically deducted whenever a reply arrives late.
- Applicant need not explain why information is wanted. RTI covers existing information/records rather than requiring officials to create a new analysis or answer hypothetical questions.
- Exemptions include protected national-security/foreign-relations material, commercial confidence/IP where competitive interests would be harmed, confidential sources, investigation impediments and specified Cabinet records. These are qualified statutory tests—not a blanket exemption for every document touching those subjects.
- **Section 8(2)** permits disclosure where public interest outweighs protected harm, notwithstanding the Official Secrets Act/exemptions; **section 10** allows severing exempt portions.
- Appeal within the department → **CIC/SIC** second appeal; commissions also have complaint functions. PIOs/public authorities give information in the first instance, not only commissions.
- Section 23 does not eliminate constitutional judicial review: **Supreme Court Article 32 / High Court Article 226**, not Article 225. [DoPT RTI Act](https://rti.dopt.gov.in/).
## Disclosure–privacy balance
- **CBSE v.Aditya Bandopadhyay2011:** recognised access to evaluated answer-books while discussing practical limits; not a judgment simply eliminating transparency or every student's access.
- **Girish Ramchandra Deshpande2012:** personal/service information and demonstrated larger public interest; disclosure debate needs facts and applicable law, not an assumption no public official has privacy.
- Source-era parliamentary-information proviso matters, but does not justify skipping all other statutory/contextual analysis.
## Amendments: specify status
- **2019 amendment** changed service-condition control for Information Commissioners; institutional-independence concerns differ from content exemptions.
- **DPDP Act2023 section44(3)** legislated replacement of8(1)(j)'s personal-information wording; **not operative in February2025 merely because enacted**. Distinguish that historical discussion from later commencement/notifications.
- Reforms proposed in the editorial—reverse amendments, strengthen penalties/new protection laws—are proposals, not existing provisions.
## Improve access
- Timely transparent appointments, diverse expertise, digitised records and accessible tracking; publish reasons, enforce existing non-compliance penalties and protect applicants.
- Proactive disclosure reduces repetitive requests; exemptions must be lawful/proportionate and appellate oversight timely. Compare case-disposal figures cautiously; different institutions have unlike case complexity.

topics.title: PUNCH: mapping the solar wind
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Mission recall
- **Polarimeter to Unify the Corona and Heliosphere**, NASA; four small spacecraft in low Earth orbit: one Narrow Field Imager coronagraph and three Wide Field Imagers.
- Polarised sunlight scattered by electrons helps reconstruct the corona–solar-wind transition in 3D; track coronal mass ejections and space-weather evolution.
- Complements Parker Solar Probe's in-situ measurements and Aditya-L1 observations; a remote map is different from directly sampling plasma.
- February launch plans changed: launched with SPHEREx on 11March 2025 California time, 12MarchUTC. [NASA](https://www.nasa.gov/news-release/nasa-launches-missions-to-study-sun-universes-beginning/).

topics.title: Maternity benefits and delivery gaps
topics.subject: Social Problems In India
topics.markdown:
## Law and schemes
- **NFSA2013 section 4:** maternity benefit of not less than₹6, 000, subject to specified exclusions; statutory entitlement and actual scheme design must be distinguished.
- **PMMVY:** first living child₹5, 000 in two instalments; under PMMVY2.0, second child if a girl₹6, 000 in one instalment. Eligible JSY payments can supplement support;₹6, 000 is not automatically paid to every first-child beneficiary. [WCD](https://www.wcd.gov.in/offerings/pradhan-mantri-matru-vandana-yojana).
- Maternity Benefit Act's 26-week provision applies where the woman has fewer than two surviving children; otherwise 12 weeks. It does not describe every worker's access.
## Implementation
- Source expenditure₹2, 700 crore 2018–19→₹870 crore 2023–24 and coverage 36%→9% are dated reported estimates, not universal measures of all maternity support.
- Tamil Nadu₹18, 000/Odisha₹10, 000 are source-era scheme amounts with eligibility conditions; compare coverage using matching denominators.
- Aadhaar/bank linkage, documentation and software failures can exclude eligible women. Simplify access, publish payments/denials, provide grievance redress and assess inflation-adjusted adequacy.

topics.title: Prohibitory orders, begging and lawful prosecution
topics.subject: Governance in India
topics.markdown:
## Distinguish legal stages
- **BNSS163** replaces CrPC144: urgent orders to address nuisance/danger must satisfy statutory conditions and reasons.
- **BNS223** concerns disobedience of a duly promulgated public-servant order; it is different from BNSS223's complaint procedure.
- **BNSS215 /former CrPC195:** court cognizance of specified offences requires the prescribed written complaint by the relevant public servant or authorised superior. Do not convert this into a universal prohibition on every FIR or investigation into independent offences.
- C.Muniappan 2010 and Daulat Ram/Mata Bhikh lines emphasise the complaint requirement; Jeevanandham 2018 is Madras High Court guidance, not a nationwide Supreme Court ruling on every investigation.
## Begging restrictions
- An Indore prohibitory order and editorial criticism are not themselves a final judicial finding of guilt or invalidity.
- Poverty, homelessness and exploitation need rehabilitation and social protection; restrictions require lawful, proportionate enforcement and due process. Donating to a person is not automatically a crime everywhere.

topics.title: RS-24 Yars and ballistic-missile terminology
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Recall
- Russian three-stage solid-fuel intercontinental ballistic missile, related to Topol-M; silo and road-mobile versions; entered service around 2010.
- Common NATO designation **SS-27 Mod 2**; source's SS-29 label is unreliable. Reported length~22.5 m, diameter~2 m, mass~49 tonnes and range~10, 500 km are approximate variant-dependent specifications.
- **MIRV:** independently targeted re-entry vehicles; differs from multiple vehicles without independent targeting. Source 300kilotons describes explosive yield, not warhead mass; warhead-count claims vary.

topics.title: Slender-billed gull and Pallikaranai
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Species and habitat
- **Chroicocephalus genei**, slender-billed gull; IUCN Least Concern. Mediterranean and north-western Indian Ocean coastal wetlands/lagoons; migratory movements extend to India and North Africa.
- Pale body, long slender reddish bill/legs, pale yellow iris and black wing tips; length~37–40cm, wingspan~90–102cm. Eats fish and invertebrates; proportions vary with habitat.
- Chennai sighting is a distribution/observation record, not discovery of a new species.
- **Pallikaranai**, Chennai, Ramsar site 2022; fresh/brackish marsh, flood storage and biodiversity. Its wider catchment connects through Okkiyam Madavu/Buckingham Canal towards the coast; catchment wetlands are not all inside its protected boundary.

topics.title: Spices Board and export quality
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Institution
- Statutory **Spices Board Act 1986**; Board established 1987 by merger of Cardamom Board and Spices Export Promotion Council. **Commerce and Industry Ministry; Kochi headquarters.**
- Export development for 52 scheduled spices and development of small/large cardamom; quality testing, market promotion, research and exporter support.
- Food-safety regulation and export promotion are distinct functions; FSSAI and other competent agencies retain their respective roles.
- Traceability, pesticide residues, ethylene oxide and importing-country standards influence market access. Testing must connect to corrective action across the supply chain.
## Value addition
- Source 2030 US$10 billion export target/~70%value-added share is an ambition; reported US$4.5 billion, 1.5 million tonnes, 48%processed share use dated/possibly different denominators.
- Raw spices→seasonings/extracts/essential oils→branding/standardisation; global seasoning-market share differs from India's overall spice-export share.
- FPOs, storage, packaging, traceability, IPM and farmer training; ICAR/seed-spice research supports disease/climate-resilient varieties.
- Nutraceutical/pharmaceutical opportunities require evidence, quality and applicable approvals; traditional use alone does not establish clinical efficacy. Extending PLI is a recommendation, not automatic existing eligibility.

topics.title: Selenium: essential nutrient and excess exposure
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Essential versus excessive
- **Se, atomic number 34**; essential trace element. Selenoproteins support antioxidant defence, thyroid-hormone metabolism and reproduction; examples glutathione peroxidases, thioredoxin reductases and selenoproteinP.
- USNIH reference intake: adults 55, pregnancy 60, lactation 70 **micrograms/day**, not milligrams. Food content depends on soil; sources include seafood, meat and Brazil nuts. [NIH](https://ods.od.nih.gov/factsheets/Selenium-HealthProfessional/).
- Excess can cause **selenosis**: hair loss, brittle/lost nails and gastrointestinal symptoms; deficiency and toxicity are different problems.
- Buldhana hair-loss reports linked suspect wheat/selenium exposure: an investigated hypothesis is not proof all ration wheat or every Punjab/Haryana crop is unsafe. Establish exposure through food/soil testing and clinical/epidemiological assessment.

topics.title: Black plastic, recycled e-waste and food-contact safety
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Risk pathway
- Poorly controlled recycling of electronic plastics can transfer flame-retardant chemicals into other products. **Colour alone does not establish contamination** in every black utensil.
- Bromine detection is a screening clue, not identification of every chemical or proof of illness. Migration depends on material, temperature, use and dose.
- Widely circulated exposure claims from a 2024 study were subject to a calculation correction; do not memorise the original headline as an established daily toxic dose.
- Carbon-black pigments can impede conventional near-infrared sorting. Segregate e-waste, enforce traceability and food-contact standards, and improve sorting/authorised recycling.

topics.title: Spinal muscular atrophy and prenatal research
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Mechanism and care
- Common 5qSMA: **autosomal recessive SMN1 defect on chromosome 5**→low survival motor neuron protein→motor-neuron loss→progressive weakness, often proximal, with respiratory/nutritional complications.
- SMN2 copy number can modify severity; types 0–4 reflect age/severity patterns rather than completely separate diseases.
- Disease-modifying treatments include nusinersen, risdiplam and onasemnogene abeparvovec; physiotherapy is not the only treatment. Respiratory, nutritional and orthopaedic support remain important.
- February 2025 prenatal risdiplam report concerned **one case**, not an established universal prenatal cure. [NEJM report](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMc 2300802).
- Research requires informed consent, maternal/fetal safety monitoring and long-term follow-up; access and costs raise equity concerns.

topics.title: Textiles: value chains, competitiveness and sustainability
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Value chain and clusters
- Fibre→yarn→fabric→processing→garments/home textiles; cotton and man-made fibres face different input/market conditions.
| Cluster | Recall |
| --- | --- |
| Tiruppur | Knitwear |
| Surat | Man-made textiles |
| Ludhiana | Hosiery/woollens |
| Bhiwandi | Powerloom weaving |
- Reported~4.5 crore employment refers to the broader textile sector, not cotton farming alone; around 60lakh cotton farmers is a separate dated estimate. MSMEs are important throughout the chain.
## Source-era trade and policy
- SourceFY2023–24 textile/apparel exports~US$34.1 billion versusUS$33.4 billionFY2019–20; garment and cotton/home-textile segments moved differently. Values, volumes and growth periods must match.
- Raw-material availability/cost, quality-control orders, logistics, skills and preferential trade access affect competitiveness; QCOs need quality benefits balanced with input availability.
- Traceability, cleaner processing, renewable power, water efficiency and recycling help respond to buyer sustainability requirements. PMMITRA infrastructure and production incentives require implementation/results assessment.
-2030 global fibre-demand figures and projected market values are forecasts, not achieved production.
## Circular fashion
- Source examples: **Panipat** textile recycling, **Bengaluru** waste-management innovations and **Tiruppur** cleaner production/wastewater work.
- Repair → reuse/rental → upcycling → fibre recycling, where feasible; match each route to material quality and demand.
- Mixed fibres, sorting, dyes, water/energy and transport affect actual benefits. Recycled textiles are not automatically impact-free; support worker safety, viable markets and responsible collection.

topics.title: Kalakkad–Mundanthurai Tiger Reserve
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Map and biodiversity
- Southern Western Ghats, **Tamil Nadu**, across the Tirunelveli–Tenkasi–Kanyakumari landscape near Kerala; not a reserve divided equally between the two States.
- Tiger reserve 1988, combining Kalakkad/Mundanthurai landscapes; part of Agasthyamalai region, headwaters important to the **Tamirabarani** basin.
- Evergreen/semi-evergreen forest, moist/dry deciduous forest, thorn habitats and grasslands; plantations are not equivalent to natural forest.
- Tiger, leopard, elephant, gaur, sambar, sloth bear, Nilgiri/langurs, lion-tailed macaque, slender loris and small cats; flora includes Cullenia, Hopea and **Paphiopedilum druryi**.
- Western Ghats is a biodiversity hotspot; source 18-world-hotspot count is outdated. Hotspot status concerns endemism and habitat loss, not tiger density alone.

topics.title: Honduras: map recall
topics.subject: India & World Geography
topics.markdown:
## Location
- Central America: borders **Guatemala, El Salvador and Nicaragua**; Caribbean coast on Gulf of Honduras, Pacific access through **Gulf of Fonseca**.
- Capital **Tegucigalpa**; highland terrain, highest peak Cerro Las Minas. Rivers Coco, Patuca and Ulúa; Lake Yojoa and Caratasca lagoon.
- Forest, mineral/agricultural resources and hurricane/flood exposure; source Indian 26-tonne aid report followed Tropical Storm Sara, a dated humanitarian event.

topics.title: Time use, unpaid care and the care economy
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Reading Time Use Survey 2024
- NSO survey records a 24-hour activity diary; 2019 and 2024 comparisons require matching ages, activity categories and **participant versus all-person averages**.
- Source employment participation, ages 15–59: women 21.8%→25%, men 70.9%→75%; these measures are not interchangeable with PLFS annual LFPR.
- Unpaid domestic work remains strongly gendered; reported female 15–59 participant time 305 minutes/day versus 315 in 2019. Do not present participant minutes as time spent by every woman.
- Caregiving, learning, leisure and self-care have different age/participation denominators; one table's numbers cannot be applied to all ages. [NSO release](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2106113&lang=2&reg=48).
## Care and policy
- **Recognise→Reduce→Redistribute** unpaid care; represent care workers in decisions and provide fair reward/conditions in paid care.
- Water access, reliable energy, nearby childcare/Palna, elder care and transport reduce time burdens; a registered tap is not proof reliable daily supply.
- Unpaid household care generally falls outside GDP's production boundary; unpaid work in a family enterprise/agriculture is a different category and cannot all be called excluded care.
- Gender Budget 2025–26₹4, 49, 028.68 crore/~8.86% of expenditure is an allocation classification, not money entirely dedicated to childcare or proof all women benefit.
- Bogotá care blocks illustrate linked neighbourhood services. Measure service quality, time saved and women's choices, not merely facility counts.

topics.title: Avalanches: triggers and risk reduction
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Process
- Snow mass descends a slope when gravity exceeds stability; slab failure often combines a weak layer and loading from snowfall/wind, warming or rain.
- Types: slab, loose-snow, wet-snow and powder-snow avalanches; ice/rock avalanches are related mass movements, not all identical snow processes.
- Many snow avalanches occur on~30–45° slopes; terrain, snowpack and weather interact, so angle alone is not a prediction.
## Reduce exposure
- February 2025 Mana-region disaster highlights risks to mountain workers and routes. Map runout zones, monitor weather/snowpack, issue actionable warnings and close exposed work/routes when necessary.
- DGRE expertise, Army/ITBP/NDRF coordination, trained rescue and appropriate shelters/equipment support preparedness; remote sensing cannot guarantee exact event prediction.
- Combine disaster planning with changing mountain climate and infrastructure siting; do not treat all snowfall as equally dangerous.

topics.title: India’s high-income2047 pathway
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Conditional scenario
- World Bank February 28, 2025 report: average realGDP growth~**7.8%** over 22 years could support high-income status by 2047; this is a reform scenario, not a guaranteed forecast. [World Bank](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2025/02/28/india-accelerated-reforms-needed-to-speed-up-growth-and-achieve-high-income-status-by-2047).
- Suggested investment/GDP~33.5%→40% by 2035; labour-force participation 56.4%→65%, women's participation 35.6%→50%; improve productivity and human capital.
- High-income classification uses **GNI per capita**, not aggregateGDP rank. Real growth, population, exchange rates and the classification methodology matter.
- More jobs/skills, productive cities, infrastructure, competitive firms/trade, State reforms and inclusion; climate resilience must accompany investment.
## GDP size versus living standards
- The source's US$2.1 trillion (2015) to US$4.3 trillion (2025) comparison mixes a historical value with a dated **projection**; future rankings were not achieved outcomes at publication.
- **Nominal US-dollar GDP**, real domestic-currency growth and purchasing-power-parity GDP measure different things. Dollar values change with inflation and exchange rates; country comparisons need consistent bases.
- Large total GDP does not itself establish high income per person or inclusive prosperity. Assess employment, real wages, productivity, inequality and human development.
- GST, IBC, digital payments, infrastructure and investment can support growth; attributing all observed growth to one policy/leader exceeds the evidence.
- Demographic dividend requires skills, health and productive jobs; a young population is an opportunity, not automatic growth. Forecast dates for overtaking Japan/Germany remain vintage-specific scenarios.

topics.title: Aditya-L1 and Lagrange points
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Mission
- ISRO solar observatory: **PSLV-C57 launch 2September 2023; halo-orbit insertion 6January 2024**, near Sun–EarthL1~1.5 millionkm from Earth. It does not travel to the Sun's surface.
- Seven payloads: **VELC, SUIT, SoLEXS, HEL1OS** remote solar observations; **ASPEX, PAPA, magnetometer** in-situ particles/fields.
- Study corona, heating, flares, solar wind and space weather; complements other observatories rather than duplicating every instrument.
## Lagrange points
- Five points in the rotating two-body system; L1–L3 unstable and need station-keeping; L4/L5 can be stable under appropriate mass-ratio conditions.
- Balanced effective forces do not mean zero gravity or no fuel requirement. Halo orbit provides useful observing geometry.
- Source claims of ISRO's first-ever PSLV restart are incorrect; earlier restart demonstrations preceded this mission.

topics.title: Naval Anti-Ship Missile–Short Range
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Trial and technology
- **DRDO/Indian Navy test 25February 2025**, Sea King helicopter off Chandipur; **NASM-SR means Short Range**, despite source long-range/hypersonic wording. [Defence release](https://www.pib.gov.in/pressreleasepage.aspx?lang=2&prid=2106482&reg=48).
- Sea-skimming flight; imaging-infrared seeker, fibre-optic-gyro inertial navigation, radio altimeter and two-way data link.
- **Man-in-the-loop** allows target selection/retargeting via live seeker imagery; demonstrated direct hit and relevant control modes.
- DRDO laboratory collaboration includes RCI/DRDL/HEMRL/TBRL. Successful trial is not proof every unit is operationally inducted or an export contract exists.

topics.title: Border Roads Organisation
topics.subject: Internal Security of India
topics.markdown:
## Institution and role
- **Raised 7May 1960**, under Ministry of Defence; builds/maintains strategic roads, bridges, tunnels and airfield-related infrastructure in border areas and certain overseas projects.
- Border connectivity supports defence mobility, disaster response and civilian access; BRO is not the Ministry of Home Affairs' Border Management Department.
- Mountain terrain, weather, environmental impacts and maintenance require integrated planning; road length alone does not establish year-round connectivity.

topics.title: Kandla–Gorakhpur LPG pipeline
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Project
-~2, 800 km LPG pipeline from Kandla through Gujarat/Madhya Pradesh/Uttar Pradesh to Gorakhpur; associated distribution can serve wider regions without every State lying on the main route.
- **IHB:** IndianOil 50%, BPCL25%, HPCL25%; reported capacity~8.25 million tonnes/year and project cost~₹10, 000 crore are source-era estimates.
- March 2025 commissioning schedules were plans, not proof the whole pipeline was already operational.
- LPG is principally propane/butane; LNG is mainly methane. Pipeline transport can reduce road-tanker exposure and logistics costs but retains leak/fire/maintenance risks.
- PNGRB standards, monitoring, emergency plans and maintenance matter. It does not automatically cut consumer prices or end import dependence; cited Jaipur tanker disaster occurredDecember 2024, not 2023.

topics.title: Three-language policy and foundational learning
topics.subject: Governance in India
topics.markdown:
## NEP2020
- Three-language approach retains flexibility: choices involve States/regions/students; **at least two languages native to India**; no language is to be imposed. [NEP](https://www.education.gov.in/sites/upload_files/mhrd/files/NEP_Final_English_0.pdf).
- Tamil Nadu's two-language position raises federal, identity and implementation debates; Hindi is not India's constitutionally designated national language.
- Mother-language familiarity can support early learning; multilingual benefits depend on teaching quality, exposure and resources.
## Learning priorities
- Source ASER claim about Class 3 inability to read a Class 2 passage concerns a specific rural reading benchmark, not absence of every literacy skill among all Indian children.
- Foundational literacy/numeracy, teacher vacancies, materials and training need attention alongside language policy; salary spending shares do not alone measure teaching quality.
- Flexible sequencing and local consultation can reduce overload. AI translation is a useful aid, not a substitute for language learning or reliable classroom teaching.
## Medium versus language subjects
- NEP recommends home/mother/local/regional medium **wherever possible until Grade 5, preferably Grade 8 andbeyond**; choice of medium differs from learning three language subjects.
- NCERT2024 languages initiative included primers in 104 languages/dialects, not necessarily full translated science/maths curricula in 104 languages.
- Teacher/material shortages, parental Englishpreferences and State linguistic choices affect implementation. Older AISES2002–09 percentages cannot establish a current 2025 trend.
- Classical-language learning and foreign-language options differ from formalgovernmentclassicalstatus; Sanskrit/Tamil/Telugu/Kannada/Malayalam/Odia/Pali/Prakrit and Persian references must not imply identical notified status.

topics.title: Fisheries: livelihoods, sustainability and governance
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Sector
