- Code on Social Security 2020 recognises gig/platform workers, but enactment, commencement and actual benefit delivery are distinct. Rajasthan's 2023 legislation provides a welfare framework; draft Karnataka proposals in March 2025 were not already implemented law.
- International rulings vary by jurisdiction and category: UK's “worker” status is not identical to full employee status; do not generalise one rule to all platforms.
- Reform priorities: clear earnings/fees, safety and insurance, portable welfare, access to relevant personal work data, fair deactivation appeals, representation and collective bargaining.
- Protect privacy when increasing algorithmic transparency; assess net earnings and coverage rather than registrations alone.

topics.title: IUCN Green List and effective conservation
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## What is certified?
- Voluntary global standard for **protected and conserved areas**, administered by IUCN; not a UNEP programme or mandatory status for every park.
- Four pillars: **good governance; sound design/planning; effective management; successful conservation outcomes**. It assesses how well an area works, not merely whether it has legal designation.
| January 2025 additions | Country |
|---|---|
| Sharaan Nature Reserve | Saudi Arabia |
| King Abdulaziz Royal Nature Reserve | Saudi Arabia |
| Aqaba Marine Reserve | Jordan |
| Sir Bu Nair Protected Area | UAE |
- These additions were announced in January, rather than first occurring in March. [IUCN account](https://iucn.org/story/202501/2025-kicks-growth-four-new-sites-added-iucn-green-list-and-three-relisted).
- IUCN **Red List** assesses species extinction risk; Green List assesses area conservation performance. Neither is UNESCO inscription.
- Aichi Target 11's 17% terrestrial/10% marine goals were for 2020. The current global framework's Target 3 seeks effective conservation of 30% of land/inland waters and marine/coastal areas by 2030.
- Community rights, equitable management and measurable ecological outcomes matter as much as coverage statistics.

topics.title: CAG: independence, appointment and public audit
topics.subject: Indian Polity
topics.markdown:
## Constitutional framework
| Article | Provision |
|---|---|
| 148 | Appointment by President; independence and removal safeguards |
| 149 | Duties/powers prescribed by Parliamentary law |
| 150 | Form of Union/State accounts prescribed by President on CAG's advice |
| 151 | Reports to President/Governor for laying before respective legislature |
- Appointment is by warrant under the President's hand and seal; no statutory selection collegium was established in the March 2025 source period. A PIL/notice does not enact the proposed reform.
- **Six years or age 65, whichever earlier**, comes from the CAG's 1971 service law, not an express tenure clause in Article 148. Further office under Union/State governments is prohibited after leaving office. [CAG framework](https://cag.gov.in/en/page-constitutional-provisions).
- Removal follows the same manner/grounds as a Supreme Court judge: proved misbehaviour/incapacity and special-majority parliamentary process. Salary and specified service rights cannot be varied to disadvantage after appointment; office expenses are charged expenditure.
## Scope and reform
- Audits receipts/expenditure and bodies according to law, ownership, financing and entrustment provisions. It does **not automatically audit every private firm**, nor are all PPPs/NGOs automatically exempt.
- CAG reports support PAC scrutiny; audit findings are not themselves criminal convictions or orders to spend money.
- Reforms proposed: transparent merit-based selection, protection from conflicts, skilled timely audits, accessible reports and stronger legislative follow-up. Safeguard independence while avoiding interference in ordinary executive policy choices.

topics.title: Prime Minister Internship Scheme
topics.subject: Governance in India
topics.markdown:
## March 2025 pilot design
- Ministry of Corporate Affairs; launched in 2024 following the Budget announcement. Overall ambition: **one crore internships in top 500 companies over five years**, not one crore already trained.
- Pilot eligibility: age **21–24**, not in full-time education or full-time employment; other qualification/exclusion criteria apply. It is not a programme automatically open to every current full-time student.
- **12-month internship**, ₹5,000 monthly assistance and ₹6,000 one-time grant; at least six months of relevant professional experience. [MCA pilot account](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2104914&lang=2&reg=48).
- Mobile app improves access/application management. Internship selection is not a guaranteed permanent job; overall top-500 ambition differs from actual participating-company counts in a pilot round.
- Evaluate mentorship, meaningful tasks, safe workplaces, travel/living costs, equitable selection, completion and subsequent employment. Proposed incentives are not automatically enacted tax benefits.

topics.title: Government assurances and OAMS
topics.subject: Governance in India
topics.markdown:
## Parliament to implementation
- **Online Assurances Monitoring System**, Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs: records and tracks ministerial assurances made during questions/debates.
- An assurance is an undertaking to provide information or take specified action; not every political promise becomes a parliamentary assurance automatically.
- Normally expected within three months; extensions and requests for dropping assurances undergo the appropriate process. Delay is not proof every assurance automatically lapses.
- Ministry/department follows up → implementation report → parliamentary Committee on Government Assurances scrutiny.
- Digital tracking supports visibility and coordination but cannot ensure fulfilment without accurate updates, responsible officers and committee follow-up. AI-based prioritisation is a recommendation, not the source of legal accountability.

topics.title: Bodo identity and the 2020 peace accord
topics.subject: Internal Security of India
topics.markdown:
## Identity and agreement
- Bodos/Boros are a major tribal ethnolinguistic community of Assam, within the Bodo-Kachari group; not Assam's largest ethnolinguistic group overall.
- Bodo belongs to the Tibeto-Burman branch; included in the Eighth Schedule by the **92nd Amendment, 2003**.
- Third Bodo accord signed **27 January 2020** among Union/Assam governments and Bodo representatives, including NDFB groups and ABSU. Earlier accords: 1993 and 2003.
- BTAD nomenclature changed to **Bodoland Territorial Region**, within Assam; **no new State** was created. BTC autonomy derives from the Sixth Schedule; ST recognition is distinct from Fifth/Sixth Schedule area administration.
- Provisions: stronger council powers, boundary review through the prescribed mechanism, ₹1,500 crore development package over three years, cultural/educational support and rehabilitation of surrendered cadres. [MHA implementation account](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1913900&lang=2&reg=48).
- The original four district names were Kokrajhar, Baksa, Chirang and Udalguri; subsequent district/boundary changes should not be hidden by treating that list as permanent.
- Reported “over 80% implemented” is the Home Minister's dated assessment, not proof every grievance ended. Non-Bodo representation, land rights, livelihood outcomes and monitoring remain important.

topics.title: BIS certification and consumer safety
topics.subject: Governance in India
topics.markdown:
## Standards and conformity
- National standards body under Department of Consumer Affairs; headquarters New Delhi. BIS succeeded ISI in **1987**, under the earlier 1986 Act; current **BIS Act 2016 commenced in 2017**.
- Formulates Indian Standards, runs conformity certification/testing and supports consumer awareness. Certification is generally voluntary unless an applicable **Quality Control Order** makes compliance compulsory. [BIS](https://www.bis.gov.in/product-certification/product-certification-overivews/?lang=en).
- ISI mark concerns product conformity; hallmarking concerns specified precious-metal purity. Neither means every conceivable product hazard is ruled out.
- Ecomark addresses environmental criteria; **2024 rules provide CPCB implementation in partnership with BIS**, not a wholly unchanged older arrangement. [Environment Ministry](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2061878&lang=2&reg=3).
- E-commerce enforcement targets products violating applicable compulsory standards/marking, not every uncertified product regardless of legal category.
- Use traceable licences, marketplace checks, credible testing and consumer complaints; simplify MSME compliance without weakening safety. Council-size claims require the applicable rules rather than an unexplained fixed 25-member total.

topics.title: Caracal and semi-arid habitat conservation
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Species anchors
- **Caracal caracal**, Felidae, Carnivora; medium-sized tawny cat with long black ear tufts, powerful limbs and a solitary, elusive habit.
- Broad distribution across Africa and parts of West/Central/South Asia. India's surviving records are especially associated with Rajasthan and Gujarat; older range does not prove healthy populations in every historic State.
- Uses dry forest, scrub, semi-arid grasslands; hunts small mammals and birds. Often nocturnal, but activity varies.
- **Globally Least Concern; Schedule I in India; CITES Appendix I for Asian populations**, Appendix II elsewhere. Global status can coexist with severe local rarity.
- First photographic record **in Mukundra Hills Tiger Reserve** is a local documentation milestone, not the first proof that caracals occur anywhere in Rajasthan.
- Species-recovery prioritisation, surveys, habitat connectivity, conflict reduction and anti-poaching are important. Grasslands are functioning ecosystems, not ecologically empty “wastelands”.

topics.title: Meteoroids, meteors and meteorites
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Three terms
| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Meteoroid | Small natural space object |
| Meteor | Luminous atmospheric-entry phenomenon |
| Meteorite | Material surviving entry and reaching the surface |
- Entry heating involves interaction/compression with atmospheric gas; a meteor is not simply the rock itself. A fireball is an unusually bright meteor.
- Beed, Maharashtra, was the reported fall location. Laboratory classification is needed before assigning its composition or claiming rare organic compounds were found.
- Meteorites preserve mineral/isotope records of Solar System formation; some come from the Moon/Mars and some contain organics. **Organic molecules do not by themselves prove extraterrestrial life**.
- NASA's all-sky camera network records fireballs; Canada's CMOR detects meteor trails by radar. Observations constrain trajectories, velocities and potential recovery areas.

topics.title: Biodiversity action plans and local governance
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## From global targets to districts
- Arunachal Pradesh's SBSAP was presented as a people's plan integrating district-level priorities with India's NBSAP and the **Kunming–Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework**, adopted at CBD COP15 in 2022.
- KMGBF has **four long-term goals and 23 targets for 2030**. Target 3: effective, equitable conservation of at least 30% of land/inland waters and marine/coastal areas.
- Other targets include halving global food waste, reducing pollution risks and reforming harmful subsidies. It does not require instant elimination of every agricultural subsidy or every use of pesticides.
- CBD Article 6 requires national strategies/plans and integration into sectoral policies. India's institutional tiers: **NBA → State Biodiversity Boards → local Biodiversity Management Committees**, with different legal roles rather than one command chain.
- Examples: Apatani wet-rice/fish systems and Pakke hornbill-nest adoption show local knowledge and community participation. Great hornbill is Vulnerable, not uniformly labelled Endangered.
- Make district baselines, budgets, rights-sensitive consultation and monitoring operational; eco-tourism is beneficial only with ecological limits and fair local returns.

topics.title: Human coronavirus HKU1
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Endemic coronavirus, not HKU5
- One of four common endemic human coronaviruses: **229E, NL63, OC43 and HKU1**. HKU1 is a betacoronavirus in **Embecovirus**; SARS-CoV and MERS-CoV belong to different subgenera.
- First scientific identification/publication was **2005 in Hong Kong**, using a patient sample collected in 2004. [CDC research](https://wwwnc.cdc.gov/eid/article/12/5/05-1316_article).
- Usually causes upper-respiratory symptoms; bronchiolitis/pneumonia can occur, especially in vulnerable patients. Endemic does not mean incapable of causing severe illness.
- Respiratory spread and close contact matter; no established specific vaccine or targeted routine antiviral for HKU1. Care is supportive and severity-dependent.
- Ventilation, hand/respiratory hygiene and avoiding exposing vulnerable people help prevention. A Kolkata report is not discovery of a novel COVID-like virus or proof of an imminent pandemic.

topics.title: Measles and subacute sclerosing panencephalitis
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Delayed neurological complication
- **SSPE** is a rare, progressive, usually fatal brain disorder following persistent **wild-type measles virus** infection, typically appearing years after apparent recovery.
- Mainly affects children/adolescents; early behavioural/cognitive decline can progress to myoclonus, seizures, motor/vision loss, swallowing difficulty and severe neurological disability.
- Course varies; a quoted one-to-three-year terminal course is not a rigid rule for every patient. No reliably curative treatment is established; clinical management and experimental approaches are distinct.
- Prevent measles through high **two-dose measles-containing-vaccine** coverage. India uses MR in its public immunisation programme; MMR is another measles-containing vaccine.
- High population coverage reduces transmission; it does **not erase delayed SSPE risk in someone already infected years earlier**. Measles vaccine strains are not established causes of SSPE. [WHO](https://www.who.int/groups/global-advisory-committee-on-vaccine-safety/topics/measles-vaccines).
- Mission Indradhanush helps close immunisation gaps; surveillance and equitable access complement coverage targets.
## Measles recognition and prevention
- Measles virus: **Morbillivirus, Paramyxoviridae**; highly contagious **airborne** infection. Symptoms commonly begin 10–14 days after exposure: fever, cough, coryza, conjunctivitis; **Koplik spots**, followed by face-to-body rash.
- Complications include pneumonia, diarrhoea/dehydration, blindness, encephalitis and the delayed complication **SSPE**. Infants, unvaccinated people and those with impaired immunity/malnutrition are vulnerable.
- India's UIP schedule uses **MR (measles–rubella), not MMR**: first dose **9–12 months**, second **16–24 months**. [Health Ministry schedule](https://mohfw.gov.in/sites/default/files/Final%20Printed%20English%20AR%202024-25.pdf).
- High two-dose coverage (about 95%) and surveillance prevent outbreaks; Mission Indradhanush addresses missed vaccinations. Supportive care and clinician-directed vitamin A matter; antibiotics address bacterial complications, not the measles virus itself.
- Elimination goals, verified elimination and eradication are different. A dated national/regional target is not evidence that measles has disappeared or that all regions share one deadline.

topics.title: Bar Council of India and professional ethics
topics.subject: Governance in India
topics.markdown:
## Statutory professional regulation
- BCI is established under **section 4, Advocates Act 1961**, not a constitutional body. It regulates professional conduct/legal-education standards and represents the Bar.
- Members elected from State Bar Councils plus Attorney General and Solicitor General ex officio. State Council terms and a BCI representative's term are not automatically identical; the Act specifies category-dependent tenure.
- Recognises law qualifications/institutions for professional purposes; conducts AIBE for the relevant certificate-of-practice framework. State Bar enrolment is a separate step.
- Disciplinary functions involve State and national mechanisms; BCI is not simply a department whose every disciplinary decision is directed by the Law Ministry. [Act](https://www.indiacode.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/1631/1/A1961_25.pdf).
- Rule 36 restricts solicitation/advertising, including misleading online promotion. Limited prescribed factual website information is permitted; not every informative legal post is automatically advertising.
- Professional independence, truthful communication, client confidentiality and access to justice guide digital practice. Rules permitting limited foreign-law practice are not blanket permission for foreign firms to practise Indian litigation.

topics.title: Kanger Valley National Park and tentative heritage status
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Location and landscape
- Bastar district near Jagdalpur, Chhattisgarh; national park designated in **1982**, approximately **200 sq km**, named for the Kanger River.
- Moist deciduous Sal/teak forests, bamboo, semi-evergreen patches, gorges and karst caves: **Kotumsar, Kailash and Dandak**; subterranean habitats have distinctive fauna.
- **Tirathgarh Falls is on Munga Bahar**, which joins the Kanger, not directly on the main Kanger River. Hill myna, mammals and cave species add conservation value.
- UNESCO **Tentative List**, submitted 11 February 2025, natural category: a candidate inventory, **not World Heritage inscription**. [UNESCO entry](https://whc.unesco.org/en/tentativelists/6801/).
- A national park containing tigers is not automatically a notified tiger reserve or Project Tiger critical tiger habitat.
- Protect forest/cave ecology with controlled visitation, anti-poaching, pollution prevention and community participation; Bastar's tribal knowledge and cultural associations matter.
## Other tentative-list additions in the source illustration
- Mudumal megalithic menhirs, Telangana; Ashokan edict sites across States; Chausath Yogini temples; Gupta temples; and palace-fortresses of the Bundelas.
- Keep their nomination-stage status separate from inscription; “Ashokan” sites are not collectively assigned a new archaeological date by listing.

topics.title: Mount Fuji: volcano, sacred landscape and tourism
topics.subject: India & World Geography
topics.markdown:
## Map and cultural anchors
- Japan's highest mountain, **3,776 m**, on Honshu between Yamanashi and Shizuoka, south-west of Tokyo; an active **stratovolcano**, last eruption **1707–08, Hōei**.
- Its setting involves a complex plate junction/subduction system, not a complete explanation by one simple Pacific–Eurasian boundary.
- With Mount Tate and Mount Haku, one of Japan's three holy mountains; Shinto/Buddhist traditions and Hokusai's art contribute to its significance.
- UNESCO inscription **2013, cultural category**, as Fujisan; within Fuji-Hakone-Izu National Park. Natural scenery does not make the UNESCO category natural.
- 2025 climbing arrangements introduced **¥4,000** fees across the four trails; dollar equivalents fluctuate. [Official regulations](https://www.fujisan-climb.jp/l62q6e0000000457-att/Regulations-Mt-Fuji-2025.pdf).
- Overcrowding, waste, rapid overnight “bullet climbing” and altitude exposure require booking/access rules, preparedness and carrying-capacity management. Hut exceptions and restrictions vary by trail; it is not a universal requirement that every climber must stay overnight.

topics.title: Geological hydrogen and hydrogen colour labels
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## White hydrogen
- Naturally occurring hydrogen produced by geological processes, including water–iron-rich-rock reactions and radiolysis; reservoirs, concentration and replenishment need investigation.
- Lorraine/Moselle research had already reported potential in **2023**. Approximately **46 million tonnes** was an extrapolated possible resource, not a proved economically recoverable reserve newly certified in March 2025. [CNRS](https://news.cnrs.fr/articles/a-gigantic-hydrogen-deposit-in-northeast-france).
- The source's **US$92 trillion valuation is unreliable**. Arithmetic: 46 million tonnes = 46 billion kg; at an illustrative US$2/kg, gross value is US$92 **billion**, before extraction costs—not trillion or net profit.
- Natural occurrence avoids manufacturing hydrogen by electrolysis/reforming, but extraction, separation, compression and transport still use energy. Purity, scale and lowest cost are not guaranteed.
- Combustion contains no fuel carbon, but life-cycle emissions, leakage and possible NOx still matter; “zero environmental impact” is incorrect. Helium co-occurrence is site-dependent.
## Colour comparison
| Label | Typical process |
|---|---|
| Grey | Fossil-fuel reforming without carbon capture |
| Blue | Fossil route with carbon capture; residual emissions remain |
| Green | Electrolysis using renewable electricity |
| Pink | Electrolysis using nuclear electricity |
| Brown/black | Coal-based production |
| White | Natural geological hydrogen extraction |
- Colours are shorthand, not universal legal emissions certifications. Compare measured life-cycle intensity, recoverability, infrastructure and cost.

topics.title: ATAGS and indigenous artillery procurement
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## System and procurement
- **Advanced Towed Artillery Gun System**: DRDO-led development with Bharat Forge and Tata Advanced Systems; initiated in 2013, unveiled in 2016.
- **155 mm, 52-calibre** towed howitzer: calibre length here means barrel length relative to bore diameter, not 52 mm ammunition.
- Source March 2025 plan: procurement of **307 guns**, roughly ₹7,000 crore; approval/signature differs from delivery and induction.
- Trials demonstrated ranges around 47–48 km with appropriate ammunition; this is not every shell's guaranteed range or proof of superiority on every metric.
- Electric drives, electronic controls, burst firing and repositioning support use. “All-electric” does not mean maintenance-free equipment.
- Weight above 18 tonnes creates transport/high-altitude constraints; a separate lighter TGS requirement is distinct. Assess reliability, ammunition compatibility, mobility, production capacity and life-cycle costs, not just unit-price comparisons.
- Reported explanations for a trial accident require investigation evidence; do not convert an unsupported attribution into a universal safety conclusion.

topics.title: Multilateralism, international law and unilateralism
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## Institutional distinctions
- Multilateral institutions coordinate health, climate, peace, human rights and trade; unilateral withdrawals, funding cuts and sanctions can weaken collective capacity.
- In March 2025, US WHO/Paris exit processes and institutional disengagement had different legal timelines. A withdrawal instruction is not instant completion of every treaty procedure.
- **The US was not a Rome Statute party**, so ICC sanctions are not withdrawal from ICC membership. UN Human Rights Council disengagement also differs from leaving the UN.
- A proposed US DEFUND Bill is not enacted withdrawal. UN headquarters, contributions and peacekeeping effects are scenarios conditional on actual legal action.
- WTO Appellate Body vacancies impede appeals; this does not mean all WTO rules or every dispute procedure vanished.
- Smoot–Hawley tariffs (1930) illustrate escalation risks, but cannot alone explain the Great Depression or World War II.
- India can advocate institutional reform, peaceful dispute settlement, climate/health cooperation and representative global governance; US retreat does not automatically secure India a permanent UNSC seat.

topics.title: Immigrants, protest rights and national security
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## Rights and legal procedures
- ICCPR **Article 19** protects expression; **Article 21** specifically protects peaceful assembly. Restrictions require applicable law and necessity for the permitted purposes, not any vague security assertion.
- **Article 20** addresses war propaganda and specified advocacy of hatred constituting incitement; peaceful criticism is distinct from violence, threats or material support for terrorism.
- US First Amendment protections extend to persons, including many non-citizens, but immigration status and removal law create separate legal disputes.
- INA section **212(a)(3)(C)** concerns foreign-policy grounds of inadmissibility; relevant deportability provision is **237(a)(4)(C)**. Visa revocation, detention, criminal conviction and removal are not the same step.
- March 2025 campus cases involved allegations and ongoing litigation, not final proof that every protester supported terrorism. Immigration judges operate within the Justice Department; independent judicial review remains significant.
- Analyse due process, clarity, equal treatment, academic freedom and national-security evidence. University funding cancellation may affect research and trust; predicted enrolment/soft-power losses need evidence rather than certainty.

topics.title: Data, platform dominance and competition regulation
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## WhatsApp–Meta case
- CCI's **18 November 2024** order imposed ₹213.14 crore for abuse of dominance connected with WhatsApp's 2021 privacy update and mandatory cross-Meta data sharing. Relevant markets included smartphone OTT messaging and online display advertising. [CCI order account](https://www.cci.gov.in/images/pressrelease/en/press-release1731941985.pdf).
- January 2025 appellate relief stayed the five-year advertising-data-sharing restriction and required a 50% penalty deposit. Interim relief is not a final finding that all conduct was lawful.
- Later, **4 November 2025**, NCLAT upheld the major findings/penalty while setting aside the fixed five-year ban; user-choice remedies remained significant. [CCI appellate summary](https://www.cci.gov.in/images/publications_fairplay/en/fairplay-55oct-dec20251770024440.pdf).
## Why digital markets differ
- Users → data → service/ad targeting → more users can reinforce network effects, switching costs and entry barriers. Zero monetary price does not mean zero consumer harm.
- **Dominance is not itself prohibited; abuse is**. Market definition, conduct, effects and remedies must be established, not inferred from size alone.
- Data is reusable but not legally usable without limit; privacy, consent and security requirements constrain collection/use. Competition and data-protection law are complementary.
- Consider interoperability, portability, transparent choices and proportionate behavioural/structural remedies. Mandatory data sharing can itself threaten privacy; design safeguards and regulator coordination.
- Foreign cases are jurisdiction-specific; the US AT&T breakup created seven regional holding companies, not a simplistic divestment into “22 new companies”.

topics.title: ADMM-Plus counter-terrorism cooperation
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## India–Malaysia work plan
- Co-chairmanship of the **ADMM-Plus Experts' Working Group on Counter-Terrorism, 2024–27**; proposed table-top exercise in Malaysia in 2026 and field exercise in India in 2027.
- These were planned events in March 2025, not completed exercises. Table-top discussion tests decisions; field training tests practical coordination.
- ADMM-Plus brings ASEAN and eight partners: **Australia, China, India, Japan, New Zealand, Republic of Korea, Russia and US**.
- Expert groups address areas including counter-terrorism, maritime security, peacekeeping and disaster response; ADMM-Plus is not a military alliance.
- EU–India work on preventing violent extremism complements ASEAN cooperation. Intelligence coordination, online radicalisation prevention and capacity building require due process and protection of legitimate expression.

topics.title: GM crops, mustard and biotechnology governance
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Technology and regulatory status
- GM changes a plant's genetic material through engineering; trait-specific benefits/risks cannot be generalised across all crops.
- **Bt cotton**, approved in 2002, was India's commercially cultivated GM crop in this source period.
- **DMH-11 mustard** uses barnase–barstar male-sterility/restoration technology for hybrid breeding; bar is a selectable herbicide-tolerance marker. It is not simply a Bt-style insect-resistant mustard.
- The **2022 conditional environmental-release decision** involved DMH-11/parental lines and further requirements; do not call it unrestricted nationwide commercial cultivation. [ICAR clarification](https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=1886080&lang=2&reg=48).
- July 2024 Supreme Court split verdict left legal issues unresolved; formulation of a national policy was directed. Scheduled hearings in 2025 are not a final adjudication.
- GEAC is under **MoEFCC**, not DBT; EPA 1986 and the 1989 rules govern relevant biosafety regulation. DBT, under Science and Technology, supports research.
## Assessing claims
- Potential productivity/resilience gains require field evidence; assess allergenicity, gene flow, non-target effects, herbicide practices, resistance and seed-access economics case by case.
- Public-sector research and transparent regulatory evidence can coexist with precaution and farmer participation; neither all GM crops are dangerous nor all are automatically safe/high-yielding.
- Source bioeconomy estimate **US$165.7 billion**, bio-agriculture **US$13.5 billion/8.1%**, is a dated sector estimate, not GDP. BioE3 (2024) concerns biotechnology for economy, environment and employment/high-performance biomanufacturing.

topics.title: Byadagi chilli, colour and GI protection
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Crop and value chain
- Karnataka product associated with Byadagi/Haveri and surrounding growing/trading regions; GI certificate dated **27 January 2011**. [GI register](https://search.ipindia.gov.in/GIRPublicSearch/Application/Details/129).
- Wrinkled dried fruit, deep red colour and relatively low pungency. **Capsanthin contributes colour; capsaicinoids contribute heat**—do not interchange them.
- High extractable colour supports spice/oleoresin and food/cosmetic applications. **ASTA colour value** measures extractable colour, not spiciness.
- The source's numerical capsaicin range should not override the low-pungency character; cultivar, dry-weight basis and assay matter. Prices, area and turnover fluctuate.
- Well-drained loamy soils and suitable warmth/rainfall support cultivation; thrips, climate variability, storage and market volatility are key risks.
- GI protects the origin-linked identity; it does not guarantee every producer a higher price. Quality traceability, farmer organisation, suitable storage and processing improve realised value.

topics.title: Judicial reform, access and public trust
topics.subject: Governance in India
topics.markdown:
## Diagnose the bottlenecks
- Former CJI N. V. Ramana highlighted delay, cost, language barriers, weak infrastructure, appointment opacity and under-representation. Comments are reform arguments, not adjudicated findings against every judge.
- Pendency and gender counts are **dated snapshots**; sanctioned, working and occupied posts differ. Do not treat the source's “33 positions” as the permanent Supreme Court sanctioned strength.
- Speedy trial and fair access follow Article 21 jurisprudence; Article 39A supports equal justice/legal aid. *Hussainara Khatoon* (1979) is an important undertrial/speedy-trial landmark.
- Priorities: timely vacancies, staff/infrastructure, case management, fewer avoidable adjournments, legal aid, intelligible language and accessible e-courts; digital-only access can exclude people.
- Diversity and transparent merit criteria improve legitimacy. Judicial performance cannot be reduced to disposal counts at the expense of fairness or judgment quality.
- “Indianisation” can mean accessible language/procedures, not rejection of constitutional rights. The unexplained “30th Law Commission Report” attribution should not be used as verified evidence of nepotism.
## Reform instruments and limits
- e-Courts, case management, legal aid and infrastructure address different bottlenecks; filling posts alone will not remove every delay.
- Ordinary **Lok Adalats settle eligible disputes by consent**, not adjudicate contested merits like a regular court; non-compoundable offences are outside their settlement jurisdiction. Permanent Lok Adalats have a distinct public-utility framework.
- NJAC was struck down in **2015**. Judicial Accountability and Standards Bill and **All India Judicial Service** proposals were not enacted operational institutions in March 2025.
- Article **312** allows the AIJS route under its special procedure; a service cannot include posts inferior to district judge. States' language, recruitment and federal concerns require assessment.
- Malimath Committee **2003** concerned criminal-justice reform; recommendations are not automatically law. *Vineet Narain* focuses on independence/accountability of investigation, not a generic judicial-performance ranking.
- Combine quality, rights, timeliness and access in evaluation; mandatory disposal quotas can harm fair hearings.

## All-India judicial service: proposal versus existing law
- Article **312 already authorises an all-India judicial service**, subject to its conditions; it cannot include posts below district judge. This is different from creating a UPSC selection system for SC/HC judges.
- Changing higher-court appointment rules involves Articles 124/217 and constitutional requirements; a proposal does not prove all those Articles must be amended simply to create district-level AIJS.
- Common recruitment/training may widen access and consistency; concerns include federal judicial administration, local language, diversity and independence. Competitive exams alone do not eliminate corruption or guarantee executive insulation.

topics.title: Rushikonda Vishnu sculpture and archaeological inference
topics.subject: Indian Art and Culture
topics.markdown:
## Find and interpretation
- Broken granite Vishnu sculpture found at **Pedda Rushikonda Beach, Visakhapatnam**, recovered by Andhra Pradesh archaeology authorities for conservation/display at Visakha Museum.
- Tentatively attributed to the **13th–14th centuries**, and described as a Janardana form. This is a stylistic assessment, not an independently established exact date or inscription-based donor identification.
- Shankha/conch and other iconographic attributes assist identification; missing limbs constrain certainty.
- Granite rather than local khondalite raises provenance questions but does not prove import from Tamil Nadu. Immersion of a damaged temple image is a hypothesis, not evidence of a shipwreck or specific maritime trade route.
- Document find context, material/style and condition before conservation. Regional dynastic history does not justify assigning the object to a dynasty without evidence.

topics.title: Cyclone Tauktae, intensification and INCOIS
topics.subject: India & World Geography
topics.markdown:
## Ocean–atmosphere coupling
- Tauktae was an extremely severe cyclonic storm in the **Arabian Sea, May 2021**. Warm surface/subsurface water, moisture, vorticity and favourable wind shear support intensification.
- INCOIS-associated research estimated atmospheric/ocean contributions for Tauktae at approximately **53.08%/46.92%** under its method; the source's 54/46 rounds/confuses another comparison. These are study-specific attributions, not universal cyclone weights. [Research paper](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-025-92460-4).
- Negative IOD means a relatively cooler western and warmer eastern equatorial Indian Ocean. ENSO/IOD influence conditions probabilistically; La Niña does not automatically intensify every Arabian Sea cyclone.
- Distinguish storms' basins: Amphan and Mocha were Bay of Bengal systems, not Arabian Sea examples.
- Forecast skill, shelters, evacuation, warnings reaching communities and resilient infrastructure matter; warming can increase intensity without every regional frequency trend being identical.
## INCOIS recall
- Established **1999**, autonomous under **Ministry of Earth Sciences**, based in Hyderabad; an ESSO organisation.
- Services: **Indian Tsunami Early Warning Centre; Potential Fishing Zone advisories; ocean-state forecasts; observing/data services**, including Argo and ocean-analysis inputs.
- Indian Ocean tsunami-service-provider role operates within UNESCO-IOC arrangements. Ocean forecasts support navigation, fisheries, offshore activity and coupled climate models.
- INCOIS ocean/tsunami services complement **IMD's cyclone-warning responsibility**; they are not interchangeable agencies.

topics.title: Triput, Tavasya and frigate localisation
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Project milestones
- Additional follow-on **Project 1135.6** frigates: India–Russia arrangement for four ships, two built in Russia and two at Goa Shipyard with technology transfer.
- **Triput launched July 2024**, not July 2022; **Tavasya launched 22 March 2025**. Launch is entry into water, not completed trials, delivery or commissioning. [Defence Ministry](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=2114025&lang=2&reg=48).
- Tavasya is the second Goa-built ship of this pair, not the fourth frigate ever in the wider Talwar/Krivak-derived family.
- Designed for anti-surface, anti-air and anti-submarine roles; reduced radar signature does not make a ship invisible.
- Russian design cooperation, Indian systems/shipbuilding and Ukrainian-origin gas turbines illustrate multinational supply chains. Local manufacture strengthens skills without proving every critical component is indigenous.
- Delivery schedules are targets; assess integration, trials, engine supply, maintenance and timely production.

topics.title: Jackfruit and horticultural value addition
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Species and uses
- **Artocarpus heterophyllus, Moraceae**, associated with the Western Ghats; tropical humid conditions and well-drained soils support cultivation.
- Kerala designated jackfruit its State fruit in **2018**. Important producing areas include southern India and the North-East.
- Unripe fruit used as vegetable/texture-based meat substitute; ripe flesh eaten fresh/processed; seeds used cooked or as flour.
- Provides carbohydrate, fibre and micronutrients. **Texture-based meat substitution is not nutritional equivalence to protein-rich foods**; medicinal/degenerative-disease claims need clinical evidence.
- Perishability, bulky fruit, weak aggregation and market access constrain incomes. Processing into chips, flour, preserves and suitable plant-based products reduces losses.
- ODOP/horticulture support and startups can help where actually designated/eligible; no automatic subsidy for every grower. Quality, storage, farmer organisation and buyer links determine value addition.

topics.title: Anti-dumping, countervailing duties and safeguards
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Three distinct remedies
| Remedy | Trigger |
|---|---|
| Anti-dumping | Export below normal value, material injury and causal link |
| Countervailing | Actionable subsidy with injury and causal link |
| Safeguard | Import surge causing/threatening serious injury; unfair conduct not necessary |
- **Dumping is a relative price comparison**, not every cheap import, below-cost sale or proven predatory intention. Normal value and export price need comparable trade levels/adjustments.
- DGTR, Department of Commerce, investigates/recommends; **Finance Ministry/Department of Revenue notifies anti-dumping duty**. Recommendation is not automatic imposition. [DGTR](https://www.dgtr.gov.in/faq).
- Duty cannot exceed dumping margin; India's lesser-duty approach addresses injury where a lower rate suffices. There is no universal statutory 5–35% range.
- Normal expiry is five years unless continued through appropriate sunset review. Product, country/exporter and notification details govern coverage, not a ban on every import from the country.
- Safeguard measures can involve duties or quantitative arrangements; the practice sheet's blanket exclusion of tariff-rate quotas is unsafe given the applicable safeguard framework.
- Protect injured industry while assessing downstream input costs, consumers, competition and WTO compliance; these remedies are not a guaranteed solution to the overall trade deficit.

topics.title: Lapis lazuli: mineral colour and historic trade
topics.subject: India & World Geography
topics.markdown:
## Composition and uses
- Deep-blue **metamorphic rock**, not a single mineral. **Lazurite** supplies blue colour through sulphur-related species in its structure; calcite creates pale areas and **pyrite** golden sparkles, not actual gold.
- Afghanistan's **Badakhshan** is a famous historic source; deposits also occur in Chile, Russia and elsewhere.
- Lapis ornaments at Indus civilisation sites indicate long-distance exchange much earlier than the source's narrow “as early as 1000 BCE” claim; finding an object in India does not prove local mining.
- Used in ancient jewellery/ritual artefacts and ground for valuable **natural ultramarine pigment** in European painting. Natural and later synthetic ultramarine should not be conflated.
- Colour, authenticity, mineral proportions and provenance affect value; fixed mineral percentages vary between specimens.

topics.title: Carnatic music and Music Academy awards
topics.subject: Indian Art and Culture
topics.markdown:
## Music and institution
- Carnatic music emphasises **raga, tala, compositions and manodharma improvisation**; composition-centred does not mean it lacks improvisation.
- Southern tradition with devotional/secular repertoire in Telugu, Sanskrit, Tamil, Kannada and other languages; vocal and instruments such as veena, violin, mridangam and flute are important.
- Trinity: **Tyagaraja, Muthuswami Dikshitar and Syama Sastri**. *Sangita Sampradaya Pradarsini* was authored by **Subbarama Dikshitar**, not Muthuswami Dikshitar.
- Music Academy originated in the 1927 Madras music/congress setting and was inaugurated **18 August 1928**. [Academy history](https://musicacademymadras.in/history/).
- **Sangita Kalanidhi** is the Academy's distinguished music honour; title instituted in 1942, recipient presides over annual academic sessions. It is not a government national decoration.
## 2025 honours
- Sangita Kalanidhi: violinist **R. K. Shriramkumar**, known for accompaniment and scholarship; 2025 marked Dikshitar's 250th birth anniversary.
- Nritya Kalanidhi: **Urmila Sathyanarayanan**, Bharatanatyam.
- Sangita Kala Acharya: **Shyamala Venkateswaran** and **T. R. Govindarajan**; TTK: **Madambi Subramania Namboothiri**, **J. T. Jeyaraaj Krishnan and Jayasri Jeyaraaj Krishnan**.
- Selection in 2025 differs from presentation: music honours at the **1 January 2026 Sadas**, dance honour on **3 January 2026**. [Academy announcement](https://musicacademymadras.in/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/Awardee-2025.pdf).

topics.title: Gold deposits, exploration and monetary reserves
topics.subject: India & World Geography
topics.markdown:
## Two meanings of reserves
- **Geological resources/reserves** concern gold in the ground; **RBI monetary gold** is a component of official foreign-exchange reserves. They are not interchangeable.
- Mineral occurrence → exploration/resource estimate → economic reserve assessment → permissions/lease → production. A discovery or block auction is not a producing mine.
- Odisha reports concerned districts including Deogarh, Sundargarh, Koraput, Nabarangpur, Angul, Keonjhar and Mayurbhanj; quantity/grade and feasibility must precede claims of a “massive” commercial reserve.
- Karnataka: **Hutti, Raichur**, important operating producer; **Kolar Gold Fields closed in 2001**. Andhra Pradesh's Ramagiri/Jonnagiri and Jharkhand's Singhbhum/Lawa/Parasi are map anchors; avoid the stale blanket claim that Hutti is India's only possible operating gold project.
- **Lode deposits** occur in bedrock/veins; **placer deposits** concentrate transported particles in sediments. Reported occurrences do not establish equal grade or profitability.
- Domestic production may reduce some import dependence but not necessarily meet all demand. Assess tailings/water pollution, forest impacts, rehabilitation, applicable PESA/FRA rights, consultation and fair local benefits.

topics.title: IOS Sagar and Africa–India maritime engagement
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## Two initiatives announced in March 2025
| Initiative | Distinction |
|---|---|
| IOS Sagar | Mixed-crew deployment of INS Sunayna in south-west Indian Ocean |
| AIKEYME | Africa India Key Maritime Engagement exercise, co-hosted with Tanzania at/off Dar es Salaam |
- IOS participants listed: **Comoros, Kenya, Madagascar, Maldives, Mauritius, Mozambique, Seychelles, Sri Lanka and South Africa**, alongside India. They are nine friendly **Indian Ocean countries**, not nine African countries—Maldives and Sri Lanka are Asian.
- Planned April deployment, port calls and joint EEZ surveillance were not completed in March. Training in Kochi supports whole-ship familiarisation/interoperability. [Navy announcement](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=2114491&lang=2&reg=48).
- SLOC safety, anti-piracy, illegal-fishing/drug-trafficking response, HADR and capacity building support regional partnerships; joint surveillance respects host arrangements rather than transferring EEZ sovereignty.
- **MAHASAGAR**: Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions; builds on SAGAR's Security and Growth for All in the Region.
- Cooperation with Africa has its own priorities; it is not simply an extension of Act East or exclusively a response to China. Security provision depends on sustained resources, trust and local needs.
## 13–14 April 2025: AIKEYME begins
- The maiden **AIKEYME** harbour phase was inaugurated **13 April**, onboard **INS Chennai at Dar es Salaam**, by Tanzania's Defence Minister and India's Raksha Rajya Mantri Sanjay Seth. The exercise is co-hosted by India and Tanzania; the announced schedule was **13–18 April 2025**. [Inauguration](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=2121495&lang=2&reg=48), [12 April announcement](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2121218&lang=2&reg=3).
- Participants: **Comoros, Djibouti, Kenya, Madagascar, Mauritius, Mozambique, Seychelles and South Africa**, plus co-hosts **India and Tanzania**. This exercise list differs from the nine foreign countries supplying IOS Sagar personnel.
- INS Chennai (destroyer), INS Kesari (landing ship tank) and IOS Sagar/INS Sunayna feature in the engagement. Harbour activities support training/planning; sea activities support combined operations, interoperability and responses to shared maritime threats.
- **INS Sunayna sailed from Karwar on 5 April** with **44 naval personnel from nine friendly countries**. The source's deployment window is **5 April–8 May**; at the 14 April issue date, later port visits and EEZ patrols remain planned rather than completed.
- Announced port calls: Dar es Salaam, Nacala, Port Louis, Port Victoria and Malé; planned joint EEZ surveillance concerns Tanzania, Mozambique, Mauritius and Seychelles. Malé is in Maldives, an Asian island country.
- **Tanzania map:** east African Indian Ocean coast; **Dodoma** is the capital, Dar es Salaam a major port; neighbours shown include Kenya, Uganda, Rwanda, Burundi, DR Congo, Zambia, Malawi and Mozambique; Zanzibar/Pemba lie offshore and Lakes Victoria/Tanganyika are inland.
- Regional priorities include piracy, trafficking, illegal fishing, maritime terrorism, safe shipping and HADR. Do not reduce African cooperation to Act East or to rivalry with China; shared capacity and regional consent matter. The source's exact global oil-trade percentage is unnecessary without a defined denominator/date.

topics.title: Himalayan permafrost thaw and infrastructure risk
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Ground, not only surface ice
- **Permafrost** is ground remaining at or below 0°C for at least **two consecutive years**; it can include soil, sediment or rock and need not contain visible ice. The active layer above can thaw seasonally.
- Kashmir/Ladakh mapping cited remote-sensing/model estimates: 64.8% potentially covered, comprising continuous 26.7%, discontinuous 23.8% and sporadic 14.3%; Ladakh plateau estimate 87%. These are **study estimates**, not direct borehole confirmation everywhere.
- Continuous/discontinuous/sporadic describe spatial coverage, not merely what fraction of one soil sample is frozen. Study-area boundaries must be checked before generalising to administrative geography.
- Thaw can destabilise roads, buildings, hydropower sites and slopes; alters groundwater/base flow and may interact with glacier/lake hazards.
- Carbon-rich permafrost can release CO₂/methane, reinforcing warming; emissions vary with carbon stocks and moisture—not every Himalayan rock slope releases large methane volumes.
- **Chamoli 2021 was a rock–ice avalanche/debris-flow disaster**, not a straightforward glacial-lake outburst. South Lhonak, Sikkim, 2023 was a GLOF; do not interchange mechanisms.
- Combine ground-temperature loggers/boreholes, satellite mapping and lake/slope monitoring; calibrate models and plan resilient siting/drainage rather than assuming every mapped lake will burst.

topics.title: Glacier mass loss and cascading impacts
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## March 2025 global assessment
- WMO/WGMS: **2022–24 largest three-year glacier loss on record**; **2024 hydrological-year loss about 450 billion tonnes**, the fourth most negative annual result—not the single worst year.
- Cumulative loss since **1975 about 9,000 billion tonnes**; all 19 glacier regions lost mass in 2024 for the third year running. Keep mountain/peripheral glaciers separate from complete Greenland/Antarctic ice sheets. [WMO](https://wmo.int/news/media-centre/glacier-melt-will-unleash-avalanche-of-cascading-impacts).
- Glaciers lost roughly 5% of remaining ice during 2000–23 and contributed about **18 mm** sea-level rise; 18 mm over 23 years averages around 0.8 mm/year, not a fixed universal annual rate.
- **Mass balance = accumulation − ablation**. Cryosphere includes frozen water/ground; reduced snow/ice albedo increases absorbed energy and can reinforce warming.
- Glacier loss can initially increase runoff, followed by declining meltwater as ice shrinks. Seasonal water reliability, hydropower, irrigation, hazards and downstream livelihoods change differently by basin.
- Bakonzo communities' sacred associations in the Rwenzori illustrate cultural loss alongside ecological/economic harm.
- Priorities: emissions reduction, glacier/lake monitoring, GLOF warnings, water adaptation and careful mountain infrastructure. Paris temperature goals are collective commitments, not a mechanism that instantly refreezes lost glaciers.

topics.title: Indians on foreign death row: consular and legal assistance
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## March 2025 context
- MEA reporting cited 49 Indians on death row abroad, including 25 in UAE and 11 in Saudi Arabia. These are a **dated official response**, not a permanent total.
- Vienna Convention on Consular Relations, Article 36: consular notification/access; missions facilitate lawyers, family contact and welfare assistance where eligible. **Consular assistance does not override host-country courts**.
- Appeals, pardon/commutation and diplomatic representations follow local law. *Diyat* (blood money) applies in particular legal systems/cases; payment is not a universal guarantee of release.
- Qatar's eight former naval personnel had death sentences commuted in December 2023 and were released in February 2024; **seven returned immediately**, not all eight. Gurdip Singh's 2016 execution stay in Indonesia was not acquittal.
- **MLAT** concerns investigation/evidence; **sentenced-prisoner transfer** concerns serving a sentence elsewhere under applicable arrangements. Neither automatically repatriates every convicted citizen.
- Mains: timely legal access, translated records, fair trial/confession safeguards, family information and preventive migrant awareness; protect due process without presuming guilt or innocence from nationality.

topics.title: Anti-defection law and timely adjudication
topics.subject: Indian Polity
topics.markdown:
## Tenth Schedule
- **52nd Amendment, 1985** inserted the Tenth Schedule to curb political defections.
- Party member: voluntarily giving up membership, or voting/abstaining against an authorised direction without prior permission, unless condoned within **15 days**. Giving up membership can be inferred from conduct; formal resignation is unnecessary.
- Independent elected member: disqualified on joining a party. Nominated member: joining a party **after six months from taking the seat** attracts disqualification.
- **Merger exemption requires at least two-thirds of the legislature party**, subject to the Schedule's merger conditions. It is not permission for any two-thirds group to defect arbitrarily.
- **91st Amendment, 2003 removed the one-third split exemption**; it did not replace a one-third merger threshold with two-thirds. It also limits ministry size and restricts minister/remunerative political appointments of disqualified defectors.
## Decision and reform
- Speaker/Chairman decides; *Kihoto Hollohan* (1992) permits judicial review. The Schedule contains no express decision deadline.
- *Keisham Meghachandra* (2020): ordinarily decide within three months, absent exceptional circumstances; an independent tribunal was suggested, not automatically established.
- Stability and mandate protection versus legislators' deliberative freedom; partisan delay can change majorities. Consider transparent deadlines, fair hearings, narrower whips on government-survival matters and internal party democracy.

topics.title: Bhadra Tiger Reserve and soft release of elephants
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Map recall
- Western Ghats, **Karnataka**, Chikkamagaluru–Shivamogga landscape; Bhadra became a tiger reserve in **1998**.
- Bhadra River joins Tunga to form **Tungabhadra → Krishna**. Dry/moist deciduous, semi-evergreen and upland shola habitats support tigers, elephants and diverse birds.
- Other Karnataka tiger reserves: Bandipur, Nagarahole, Kali and Biligiri Ranganatha Temple.
## Human–elephant conflict
- **Soft release**: acclimatisation before freer movement, with monitoring, suitable habitat and veterinary care. Capturing and releasing a conflict elephant does not guarantee it will remain away from settlements.
- Assess carrying capacity, corridors, food/water, behaviour and risks to resident animals/nearby communities; combine early warnings and habitat protection with fair compensation.
- Tiger reserve, wildlife sanctuary and elephant reserve are distinct designations; do not infer one automatically from another.

topics.title: POCSO: child protection, safeguards and timely justice
topics.subject: Governance in India
topics.markdown:
## Framework
- **Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012**: gender-neutral protection of persons **below 18**; penetrative/non-penetrative assault, aggravated offences, sexual harassment and use of children in pornographic material.
- Under-18 consent is not adult legal consent under POCSO. Age evidence, context and child welfare matter; adolescent relationships require sensitive handling without inventing a statutory consent exception.
- Special Courts, child-friendly statement recording, identity protection, support and avoiding repeated testimony. Reporting to Special Juvenile Police Unit/local police is mandatory under section 19; section 21 penalises specified failures, with an exemption for children.
## Penalties after the 2019 amendment
| Offence | Statutory punishment anchor |
|---|---|
| Penetrative sexual assault | Minimum 10 years; may extend to life, plus fine |
| Penetrative assault on child below 16 | Minimum 20 years; may extend to natural-life imprisonment, plus fine |
| Aggravated penetrative assault | Minimum 20 years, natural-life imprisonment or death, plus fine |
| Sexual assault / aggravated sexual assault | 3–5 years / 5–7 years, plus fine |
| Sexual harassment | Up to 3 years, plus fine |
| Using child for pornographic purposes | Minimum 5 years; subsequent conviction minimum 7 years, plus fine |
- Section 29 presumptions concern specified offences; section 30 concerns culpable mental state. These do not dispense with foundational facts and fair trial safeguards.
- **Section 35**: child's evidence within **30 days of cognizance**, recording reasons for delay; trial **as far as possible within one year**. The source's six-month trial deadline is incorrect. [Statute](https://www.indiacode.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/9318/1/sexualoffencea2012-32.pdf).
- Implementation: trained investigators, counsellors, forensic capacity, compensation/support and judicial sensitivity; a stayed lower-court interpretation is not settled law.

topics.title: Parliamentary committees: scrutiny beyond the floor
topics.subject: Indian Polity
topics.markdown:
## Structure and role
- Articles **105 and 118**, House rules and parliamentary practice underpin committee work. Standing committees are continuing institutions; many memberships are reconstituted annually. Ad hoc committees finish a specified task and dissolve.
- **24 department-related standing committees**: 16 serviced by Lok Sabha, eight by Rajya Sabha; **31 members each (21 LS + 10 RS)**. Ministers are not members.
- Examine demands for grants, referred Bills, annual reports and long-term policy. Referral of every Bill is not mandatory; committees do not themselves vote grants or enact law.
| Financial committee | Membership | Main focus |
|---|---|---|
| PAC | 22: 15 LS + 7 RS | Accounts/CAG findings and spending regularity |
| Estimates | 30, all LS | Economy, efficiency and alternative policies |
| Public Undertakings | 22: 15 LS + 7 RS | Public-enterprise reports/accounts and performance |
- Committees can call evidence/records under applicable rules; do not assume every committee can summon every minister without limitation.
- Smaller groups permit detailed, often cross-party examination and expert/public input. Reports are **recommendatory**, not binding court orders.
- Strengthen research support, timely referrals, attendance and action-taken follow-up; balance confidential deliberation with published findings and meaningful consultation.

topics.title: High Courts: appointments, independence and jurisdiction
topics.subject: Indian Polity
topics.markdown:
## Constitutional position
- Part VI: **214** High Courts for States; **231** permits a common High Court for two or more States or States and a UT, introduced by the 7th Amendment (1956). Article **230** concerns extending/excluding jurisdiction over UTs; statutory reorganisation also matters.
- Chief Justice and other judges: Constitution fixes no numerical strength. **217** appointment by President after constitutional consultation; appointment collegium: CJI + two senior-most SC judges. Transfer **222** follows the wider transfer collegium process.
- Qualifications: citizen, ten years' judicial office or ten years as an advocate of a High Court/successive High Courts. No “distinguished jurist” route as for SC, and no constitutional minimum age.
- Retirement **62** (SC: 65); resign to President; Governor administers oath. Age questions are decided by President after consulting CJI.
## Independence and removal
- Removal for **proved misbehaviour or incapacity**: each House supports the address by majority of total membership **and two-thirds present and voting**, followed by Presidential order (217/218 with 124(4)).
- Judges Inquiry Act: motion signed by at least 100 LS or 50 RS members; admission by presiding officer; statutory committee comprises a SC judge/CJI, HC Chief Justice and distinguished jurist. This is distinct from an in-house inquiry.
- **223** acting Chief Justice; **224** additional judges for temporary business/arrears (up to two years) and acting judges, subject to age limit; **224A** retired judges with required consent and prior Presidential consent.
## Jurisdiction
| Provision | Recall |
|---|---|
| 215 | Court of record; contempt jurisdiction |
| 226 | Writs for fundamental rights **and other legal purposes**; wider subject scope than SC Article 32 |
| 227 | Superintendence over subordinate courts/tribunals, excluding armed-forces courts/tribunals under this Article |
| 228 | Withdrawal of qualifying cases involving substantial constitutional questions |
| 235 | Control over subordinate judiciary |
- Territorial writ jurisdiction includes where cause of action arises wholly/partly; respondent need not always be located inside the State. The Article 227 military exclusion does not erase all Article 226 judicial review.
- Original civil jurisdiction varies with statute/charter; election petitions follow election law. First appeals may involve law/fact; second civil appeals require a **substantial question of law**.
- District-judge appointments: Governor in consultation with HC (**233**); other judicial-service appointments follow **234**. These are not Presidential High Court appointments.
- BNS/BNSS came into force in July 2024 with transitional savings; old IPC/CrPC references in the source should not be treated as the only current criminal codes.

topics.title: Pamban railway bridge and independent safety clearance
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Engineering and map
- New bridge links **Mandapam–Rameswaram/Pamban Island, Tamil Nadu**; RVNL project, about **2.08 km**, India's first vertical-lift railway sea bridge.
- **72.5 m navigational span** rises vertically by up to 17 m; deck is about 3 m above the old bridge. The source's 63 m figure is not the new lift-span length. [Railways](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleseDetailm.aspx?PRID=2118895&lang=2&reg=48).
- Old bridge opened in **1914**; Scherzer rolling-bascule leaves rotate upwards, unlike the new vertical lift. Future double-track provision differs from initial commissioned track capacity.
- March 2025: safety trials/clearance context; **inauguration followed on 6 April 2025**, not already on March 27.
## CRS
- **Commission of Railway Safety**, under Ministry of Civil Aviation; headquarters Lucknow. Inspects and authorises railway openings under the Railways Act framework and investigates specified accidents.
- Separate oversight from the railway operator helps independent assessment of structural strength, track/signalling, navigation clearance and operating procedures.
## 6 April 2025: inauguration
- The new Pamban railway bridge was inaugurated on **6 April 2025**. Its lift span is **72.5 m**, not the inconsistent 63 m figure repeated in this daily PDF. Sensors, electromechanical operation and train-control interlocking coordinate lifting with railway traffic; trains must stop while the span opens for shipping. [Railways](https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=2119836&lang=2&reg=48).

topics.title: Martian dust: exposure hazards and mission design
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Why dust matters
- Fine, abrasive, charged regolith can enter seals/habitats and affect machinery, solar power and human exposure. Silica, perchlorates, iron compounds and potentially toxic metals raise health concerns.
- Inhalation may damage lungs; perchlorates can interfere with iodine uptake/thyroid function. Risk depends on dose, composition and duration: **no human has yet developed a clinically observed Martian dust disease**.
- Earth coal-dust “black lung” is an analogy, not evidence that Martian dust contains coal or causes the identical disease.
- Dust storms recur irregularly, not precisely every three Martian years; a Martian year is about **687 Earth days**. Opportunity's 2018 storm-related loss differs from InSight's gradual dust-driven power decline in 2022.
## Mitigation
- Suitports/airlocks, dust exclusion and cleaning, filtration, abrasion-resistant components, exposure sensors, robotic handling and protected power systems.
- Mission medicine must address delayed evacuation, monitoring and informed consent. Iodine/vitamin supplements are not established universal antidotes; treatment requires evidence.
- Balance redundancy, mass/power costs, crew safety and long-duration feasibility. The supplied essay prompt has no verified UPSC year and belongs to practice, not official PYQs.

topics.title: India–Russia relations and strategic autonomy
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## Historical anchors
- Diplomatic relations began **13 April 1947**, before Indian independence. **1971** Treaty of Peace, Friendship and Cooperation; **2000** strategic partnership; **2010** special and privileged strategic partnership.
- Defence: BrahMos joint venture, Su-30MKI, S-400 and INDRA exercises. SIPRI's **36% share** concerns the volume of Indian arms imports in **2020–24**, not all defence expenditure or installed equipment.
- Civil nuclear cooperation: Kudankulam; different units have different construction/operational status. Space: Aryabhata (1975), Bhaskara-I (1979) and Gaganyaan training links.
## Economy and diplomacy
- FY 2023–24 bilateral trade about **US$65.7 billion**; **US$100 billion by 2030** was a target, not achieved trade. Oil imports dominate; diversify exports, connectivity and investment.
- National-currency settlement can ease payment issues but does not automatically remove sanctions/legal risks. INSTC and maritime routes require viable logistics and compliance.
- BRICS, SCO and UN cooperation coexist with India's US/European partnerships, China-related concerns and advocacy of dialogue on Ukraine.
- Strategic autonomy means issue-based independent decisions; diversify supplies while retaining useful cooperation, protecting sovereignty and managing technology/spares dependence.

topics.title: HIV: treatment cascade, prevention and rights
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Biology and prevention
- HIV is a **retrovirus** attacking CD4 immune cells; advanced untreated infection can progress to AIDS. Antiretroviral therapy suppresses replication and improves survival but is not a routine cure.
- Transmission: sexual exposure, infected blood/needles and mother-to-child; not ordinary touch, shared utensils or casual social contact. Safe blood, prevention services and sustained treatment reduce risk. [WHO](https://www.who.int/en/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/hiv-aids).
## 95–95–95 cascade
- By-2025 targets: **95% of all people living with HIV know status → 95% of diagnosed people receive ART → 95% of treated people achieve viral suppression**.
- Denominators change at each step; do not read this as 95% of all infected people at every stage. [UNAIDS](https://www.unaids.org/en/resources/documents/2024/progress-towards-95-95-95).
- NACP Phase V (2021–26): prevention/testing/treatment and reduction ambitions relative to 2010; the source's approximately 2.4 million burden and 44% incidence decline are dated estimates, not current counts.
- Treat All/free ART and Sampark reconnecting patients to care support retention. HIV/AIDS Act **2017**: non-discrimination, informed consent and confidentiality with statutory exceptions.
- Address stigma, migrant/key-population access, counselling, medicine continuity and resistance monitoring; registrations alone do not establish viral suppression.

topics.title: Prachand Prahaar: integrated tri-service firepower
topics.subject: Internal Security of India
topics.markdown:
## March 2025 exercise
- **25–27 March, Arunachal Pradesh**, Eastern Command: tri-service integration of surveillance, decision-making and precision engagement in a high-altitude setting.
- Sensors/UAVs/airborne and other surveillance inputs → shared picture → target identification → coordinated fires → assessment.
- Naval aviation can contribute over land; participation does not imply naval ships operating in mountains. Integration improves awareness, not perfect knowledge of every target.
- **Poorvi Prahar (2024)** was a distinct aviation-focused exercise. Prachand Prahaar is also distinct from the **LCH Prachand helicopter**.
- Importance: interoperability, rapid coordination, logistics and deterrence along sensitive frontiers; test communications, weather limitations and deconfliction.

topics.title: Indian Himalayan peaks: height and map recall
topics.subject: India & World Geography
topics.markdown:
## Peaks are not ranges
| Peak | Approx. height | Map anchor |
|---|---|---|
| Kanchenjunga | 8,586 m | Sikkim–Nepal boundary; world's third highest |
| Nanda Devi | 7,816 m | **Kumaon**, Uttarakhand |
| Kamet | 7,756 m | Chamoli/Garhwal Himalaya |
| Saltoro Kangri | 7,742 m | Saltoro Range, Karakoram |
| Saser Kangri I | 7,672 m | Saser Muztagh, Karakoram |
| Mamostong Kangri | 7,516 m | Rimo Muztagh, Karakoram |
| Rimo I | 7,385 m | Rimo Muztagh, Karakoram |
| Hardeol | 7,151 m | Kumaon/Milam region |
| Chaukhamba I | 7,138 m | Garhwal/Gangotri massif |
| Trisul I | 7,120 m | Kumaon Himalaya |
- **Nanda Devi is in Kumaon**, not Garhwal. Kanchenjunga is a boundary peak, not wholly inside India.
- **K2 (8,611 m)** lies in territory claimed by India and administered by Pakistan. A list based on territory under Indian administration is different from one using India's territorial claim.
- Heights vary slightly by survey; the source list is not a definitive ranking of every subsidiary summit.

topics.title: ATF and sustainable aviation fuel
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Fuel and emissions
- Conventional **ATF** is jet fuel, generally kerosene-based. **SAF** uses approved waste/biomass or synthetic pathways and certified blends; arbitrary bio-oils cannot be put directly into aircraft.
- SAF can reduce **life-cycle emissions**; combustion still emits CO₂. Feedstock, land/water use, renewable energy, transport and processing determine net savings.
- Challenges: cost, reliable sustainable feedstock, competing uses, certification, scale and refinery/airport compatibility.
- India's announced **indicative international-flight blending targets: 1% in 2027, 2% in 2028, 5% in 2030**, not 1% in 2025. CORSIA concerns international aviation emissions; a target is not evidence all flights already comply. [Civil Aviation Ministry](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2255021&lang=1&reg=3).
- Mains: combine efficient aircraft/operations, credible life-cycle accounting, domestic SAF scale-up and safeguards against food/land competition.

topics.title: PM-AASHA: farmer price support and consumer stability
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Integrated scheme
- **Pradhan Mantri Annadata Aay SanraksHan Abhiyan**, launched 2018; September 2024 continuation integrated farmer/consumer price interventions, with **₹35,000 crore through 2025–26**. [Cabinet decision](https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=2055990&lang=2&reg=48).
| Component | Function |
|---|---|
| PSS: Price Support Scheme | Physical procurement of notified pulses/oilseeds/copra at MSP under conditions |
| PSF: Price Stabilisation Fund | Buffers and releases to moderate essential-commodity price volatility |
| PDPS: Price Deficiency Payment Scheme | Compensates an eligible price gap for notified oilseeds; no physical government purchase |
| MIS: Market Intervention Scheme | Market intervention for qualifying perishable horticultural produce |
- PSS normal ceiling: **25% of national production** from 2024–25; **tur, urad, masur exempted for 2024–25**, with 100% procurement provision. This is a dated, conditional procurement policy, not automatic purchase of every farmer's entire crop.
- NAFED **eSamridhi** and NCCF **eSamyukti** facilitate pre-registration. State requests, crop quality, operations and storage affect access.
- PDPS coverage was enhanced to **40% of State oilseed production**, implementation period to four months, in the September decision.
- MSP support to growers and affordable consumer prices require different tools. Improve registration access, prompt payment, transparent stocks and diversification without unlimited fiscal/storage burdens.

topics.title: Contempt of court and legitimate criticism
topics.subject: Indian Polity
topics.markdown:
## Law and limits
- **Articles 129 (SC) and 215 (HC)**: courts of record with contempt powers. **Contempt of Courts Act, 1971** defines and regulates contempt.
- **Civil**: wilful disobedience of a court order or wilful breach of an undertaking. **Criminal**: specified scandalising/lowering authority, prejudicing proceedings or obstructing justice.
- Fair and accurate reporting and fair criticism of a judicial act have statutory protection. **Truth may be a defence**, when public interest and bona fides satisfy section 13, amended in **2006**.
- Criticism is not contempt merely because a judge dislikes it; protect justice administration while permitting accountability and expression. Context, interference and statutory safeguards matter.
- Parliament can legislate on contempt within constitutional competence; statutory definitions do not mean SC/HC constitutional powers originate only in the Act.
- PYQ 2022: statements **1, 2 and 4** are correct. Statement 3 is false: the **Act**, not the Constitution, defines civil and criminal contempt.

topics.title: LCH Prachand: high-altitude attack helicopter
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Platform and procurement
- HAL's **Light Combat Helicopter, Prachand**: armed high-altitude operations; Kargil experience highlighted the capability need. First flight **2010**; IAF induction **3 October 2022**.
- Twin **Shakti** engines, developed through HAL–Safran cooperation; relates to indigenous rotary-wing experience but differs from Dhruv utility transport and heavy-lift helicopters.
- High-altitude performance depends on load/weather; manufacturer altitude claims do not guarantee identical capability in every configuration.
- **28 March 2025 contracts: 156 helicopters—66 IAF, 90 Army—₹62,700 crore excluding taxes**, including training/associated equipment. The source's older proposed number is outdated. [MoD](https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=2116411&lang=2&reg=48).
- Order, phased production, delivery, training and operational induction are distinct; local supply chains and maintenance matter alongside indigenous design.

topics.title: Drones and Indian UAV programmes
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Uses and regulation
- UAVs support surveillance, mapping, agriculture, infrastructure inspection, deliveries and disaster response; FPV means the operator sees a camera feed, not necessarily autonomy or permission for beyond-visual-line-of-sight flight.
- **Drone Rules 2021**, amended in 2022: remote pilot certificate terminology. Exemptions cover **nano**, and **micro for non-commercial use**, not every micro flight. [2021 rules summary](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1749154&lang=2&reg=48).
- Green-zone flights normally need no prior airspace permission within conditions; yellow/red zones require relevant permissions. Check the applicable map and operational restrictions; military systems have a distinct regulatory scope.
- **₹120 crore drone/component PLI**, three-year scheme; **Drone Shakti** announced in Budget 2022 encourages drone services. Neither announcement grants universal flight permission.
## Programme distinctions
| Name | Correct category |
|---|---|
| ABHYAS | High-speed **expendable aerial target**; not a piloted fighter trainer or missile |
| Lakshya | Pilotless aerial target; not a cruise-missile strike system |
| SWiFT | Autonomous flying-wing technology demonstrator; not an anti-tank missile |
| CATS | **Combat Air Teaming System**, manned–unmanned teaming concept |
| Rustom / TAPAS | UAV surveillance programmes; TAPAS is a MALE platform, not a light combat aircraft |
| Nishant | Tactical surveillance UAV |
| Netra UAV | Small quadrotor; distinct from manned **Netra AEW&C** on EMB-145 |
| Imperial Eagle, Golden Hawk, Pushpak | Small UAV programmes/demonstrators; do not label them passenger transports or piloted trainers |
- The source classification table mislabels multiple programmes. [DRDO ABHYAS](https://drdo.gov.in/drdo/en/offerings/products/high-speed-expendable-aerial-target-abhyas).
- Benefits need indigenous components, skilled operators and viable services; manage collision, privacy, cyber security and misuse risks with proportionate rules and counter-UAS capabilities.

topics.title: Regional Rural Banks: inclusion and financial health
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Institutional anchors
- Began under a **1975 ordinance**, followed by **RRB Act, 1976**, on Narasimham working-group recommendations: combine rural familiarity with commercial-bank resources.
- Original ownership **Union 50% : sponsor bank 35% : State 15%**; later amendments permit capital flexibility, so this historical structure should not be treated as an immutable prohibition on other capital.
- **RBI regulation; NABARD supervision**. Lending/deposits and government-payment delivery serve rural households, farmers, artisans and small enterprises.
- Priority-sector target: **75% of ANBC or credit-equivalent off-balance-sheet exposure, whichever is higher**, not an undefined 75% of all assets.
## Read ratios carefully
| Indicator | Meaning / caution |
|---|---|
| CRAR | Capital relative to risk-weighted assets; resilience measure |
| Credit–deposit ratio | Loans relative to deposits; higher is not always safer/better |
| NPA ratio | Asset-quality stress; decline may reflect recovery, write-offs or denominator growth |
| Profit | Sustainability; FY 2023–24 aggregate ₹7,571 crore is a dated result |
- Challenges: geographic concentration, technology/cyber capacity, operating costs, staff and local credit appraisal. Consolidation may improve scale but must preserve last-mile service and accountability.

topics.title: Money Bills and Financial Bills
topics.subject: Indian Polity
topics.markdown:
## Three categories
| Category | Introduction and recommendation | Rajya Sabha / joint sitting |
|---|---|---|
| Money Bill, **110** | Only listed money matters and incidental provisions; LS only, President's recommendation | RS recommends within **14 days**; LS may reject recommendations; no joint sitting |
