- Dwarka was among **HRIDAY** heritage cities: urban amenities and conservation-sensitive planning support pilgrimage/tourism. Preserve coastal heritage through documentation, scientific conservation, responsible visitor management and community participation.

topics.title: Archaeological Survey of India
topics.subject: Governance in India
topics.markdown:
## Institution and mandate
- **ASI established in 1861**, associated with **Alexander Cunningham**, its first Archaeological Surveyor and later Director-General; attached office of the **Ministry of Culture**, headquarters **New Delhi**. [PIB institutional history](https://www.pib.gov.in/newsite/erelcontent.aspx?lang=2&reg=48&relid=78804)
- Undertakes exploration/excavation, conservation of centrally protected monuments/sites, epigraphy, archaeological documentation/publication, museum/site management and scientific/underwater research. Regional circles and specialist archaeology, science, epigraphy and horticulture units support these functions.
- **AMASR Act, 1958** governs monuments/sites of national importance, excavations and protection of specified remains; the **Antiquities and Art Treasures Act, 1972** concerns antiquities/art treasures. Not every historic building in India is ASI-protected.
- AMASR's 2010 framework generally provides **100 m prohibited area**, followed by a **further 200 m regulated area**, measured from protected limits; legal permissions and relevant exceptions must be distinguished. “200 m regulated” does not mean merely the first 200 m from the monument.
## Conservation and interpretation
- Remote sensing, material science and radiocarbon dating contribute to investigation; radiocarbon dating requires suitable organic material and does not directly date all stone architecture.
- Renewed Dwarka/Bet Dwarka exploration in 2025 illustrates maritime archaeology; scientific findings and traditions require separate treatment. [ASI underwater initiative](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=2104411&lang=2&reg=48)
- HRIDAY was an urban heritage-development programme. **Adopt a Heritage** partnerships support amenities/visitor management; they do not automatically privatise ownership, replace ASI's mandate or fund every restoration.
- Priorities: authentic conservation, records/digitisation, trained conservators, protection from encroachment/pollution and accessible interpretation; visitor revenue should not displace archaeological integrity.

topics.title: Khelo India and youth sports
topics.subject: Governance in India
topics.markdown:
## Bihar Youth Games: April 2025 preview
- Source announces the **7th Khelo India Youth Games, 4–15 May 2025**, in **Patna, Rajgir, Gaya, Bhagalpur and Begusarai**. These were scheduled dates at the issue date; Delhi also hosted specialised events including shooting, gymnastics and track cycling.
- **2025 KIYG was under-18**, not the source's recycled school under-17/college under-21 table. [Sports Ministry confirmation](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2139650&lang=2&reg=3)
## Evolution and purpose
- **2018:** Khelo India School Games, New Delhi; **2019:** renamed Youth Games, Pune/Maharashtra; **2020:** Assam; the **2021 edition held in 2022** in Haryana; **2023:** Madhya Pradesh; **2024:** Tamil Nadu; **2025:** Bihar.
- Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports/SAI ecosystem: grassroots participation, sports infrastructure, talent identification, training and competition. Youth, university, winter and para competitions serve different groups; avoid collapsing their eligibility.
- Talent support follows selection and scheme conditions, not automatic grants to every participant. The source's **₹5 lakh annually for eight years** reflects an earlier talent-development formulation; amounts/components evolved and should not be treated as an unchanging 2025 entitlement.
- Khelo India mobile app (2019) supports fitness assessment and sports information; digital engagement complements coaching/facilities.
- Bihar hosting can broaden access and regional sporting infrastructure, tourism and employment. Durable gains require maintenance, qualified coaches, safe participation, gender/disability inclusion and athlete pathways beyond the tournament.
- Mains: distinguish **participation → talent identification → sustained development → elite outcomes**; hosting and medal counts alone do not demonstrate universal fitness or lasting local benefits.

topics.title: Stubble burning, market failure and governance
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Why burning persists
- Rice harvest followed quickly by wheat sowing, combine-harvester residue, labour/machinery costs and weak straw markets make burning an inexpensive private choice despite high social costs.
- Procurement/MSP incentives, water-intensive cropping, delayed paddy calendars and credit dependence interact with the short sowing window. Source interviews describe farmer perceptions of unequal enforcement and middlemen/debt constraints; these qualitative findings are not proof that every farmer faces identical conditions or that MSP never rises.
- Burning adds particulates and gases to regional pollution. Transported smoke combines with local emissions and poor dispersion/temperature inversion. Source **20–40% PM2.5 contribution** is episode/model dependent, not a uniform whole-winter or year-round Delhi share.
## Governmentality and market failure
- **Michel Foucault's governmentality** concerns governing conduct through institutions, knowledge, norms and incentives, including self-regulation; it is broader than simply “non-coercive government.”
- **Externality:** farmer's avoided clearance cost excludes downstream health/environmental damage. **Coordination/market failure:** straw collection, storage, transport and assured demand may be missing even where equipment exists.
- Punishment alone cannot repair absent affordable alternatives; incentives alone require monitoring and reliable service delivery.
## Response chain
- **In situ:** Happy Seeder for sowing into residue, mulching/decomposition and Super Straw Management Systems where appropriate.
- **Ex situ:** balers/collection → storage/transport → biomass pellets, energy, packaging and other viable uses. Paddy straw is not universally suitable animal fodder without treatment/assessment.
- Custom-hiring centres, timely machine availability, direct farmer support, accessible credit, viable diversification/procurement alternatives and stable biomass offtake reduce the private cost of compliance.
- Pair targeted enforcement with farmer participation, local crop/weather calendars and verified outcomes; address urban/industrial/transport emissions concurrently. Assess adoption, fires, farmer costs and ambient pollution rather than subsidies distributed alone.

topics.title: Tardigrades: cryptobiosis and extreme survival
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Identity and habitat
- **Water bears / moss piglets**, phylum **Tardigrada**: microscopic, segmented, free-living invertebrates, usually under 1 mm; roughly 1,300 described species in the source's estimate.
- Four pairs of short legs, commonly bearing claws (number/form varies); plump body, tough cuticle and fluid-pressure support. A buccopharyngeal apparatus with piercing stylets extracts food from plant cells or small prey.
- Marine, freshwater and terrestrial habitats include deep seas, mountains, glaciers and deserts. Terrestrial moss/lichen dwellers need a water film for active life. **Space exposure is an experiment, not a natural habitat.**
## Survival mechanism
Water loss / adverse conditions  
↓  
Legs retract; body contracts into a **tun**  
↓  
**Cryptobiosis**: metabolism becomes almost undetectable; desiccation-induced form is **anhydrobiosis**  
↓  
Rehydration permits renewed activity under suitable conditions.
- Tuns can persist for years; some long-duration revival reports extend to decades. Survival depends on species, exposure duration and preparation. Extreme temperature, pressure, radiation and vacuum tolerance does not mean normal growth in those conditions; **extremotolerant** is a useful distinction from organisms thriving at extremes.
- Source illustrations show very low/high temperature limits and near-total water loss: treat these as experimental tolerance bounds, not a universal operating range for every species.
- Astrobiology and stress-biology research examine membrane/DNA protection, desiccation resistance and biological preservation. In **September 2007**, ESA's Foton-M3 carried dehydrated tardigrades for space-exposure experiments; surviving vacuum does not establish extraterrestrial origins. [ESA experiment](https://www.esa.int/Science_Exploration/Human_and_Robotic_Exploration/Research/Tiny_animals_survive_exposure_to_space), [NASA research](https://science.nasa.gov/biological-physical/investigations/cell-science-04/).

topics.title: Consumer Price Index and inflation measurement
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## What CPI measures
- CPI tracks retail price changes in a representative, weighted household consumption basket of **goods and services**. It helps assess inflation, purchasing power and living costs; a population average need not match every household's expenses.
- For this **April 2025** coverage, NSO/MoSPI publishes monthly **CPI-Rural, CPI-Urban and CPI-Combined**, base **2012=100**; weights derive from the NSS 68th-round **2011–12** consumption survey. [MoSPI CPI portal](https://www.cpi.mospi.gov.in/Default1.aspx).
- Fixed-basket/Laspeyres intuition: **CPI = current cost of base-period basket ÷ base-period cost × 100**. Official compilation aggregates weighted price relatives; inflation is the percentage change in the index, not the index itself.
## Series and uses
| Series | Compiler / principal use |
| --- | --- |
| CPI Rural, Urban, Combined | NSO; household inflation; Combined is monetary-policy benchmark |
| CPI-IW | Labour Bureau; industrial workers; wage and DA indexation |
| CPI-AL | Labour Bureau; agricultural labourers; minimum-wage/cost-of-living analysis |
| CPI-RL | Labour Bureau; rural labourers including agricultural and other rural occupations |
| CPI-UNME | Historical CSO series; discontinued, with linked indices used temporarily pending broad CPI-Urban |
- DA for government employees/pensioners generally uses **CPI-IW**, rather than mechanically applying CPI-Combined. Appropriate series also inform wage negotiations and contractual indexation; price data support socioeconomic and poverty analysis. [MoSPI UNME discontinuation decision](https://www.mospi.gov.in/sites/default/files/press_release/t4_20jan11.pdf).
## CPI-Combined weights: 2012 series
| Group | Weight % |
| --- | ---: |
| Food and beverages | 45.86 |
| Housing | 10.07 |
| Fuel and light | 6.84 |
| Clothing and footwear | 6.53 |
| Pan, tobacco and intoxicants | 2.38 |
| Miscellaneous | 28.32 |
- Miscellaneous covers health, education, transport/communication, household services, recreation and personal care. Housing is measured in the urban basket; its combined weight does not imply a rural housing component. [Official weight table](https://www.mospi.gov.in/sites/default/files/press_release/cpi_oct.pdf).
## Monetary policy and PYQ logic
- RBI's flexible inflation-targeting agreement dates to **February 2015**; the **2016 RBI Act amendment** gave statutory backing. Target: headline all-India CPI inflation, **4% with ±2 percentage-point tolerance** for the period relevant to these notes. Earlier policy monitored multiple indicators, so avoid treating the transition as a simple statutory WPI-to-CPI substitution. [RBI framework](https://rbi.org.in/scripts/PublicationsView.aspx?Id=18086).
- **2020 Prelims: answer (a), 1 and 2 only.** CPI has greater food weight and includes services; WPI measures goods and is not RBI's inflation-target benchmark.
- For the WPI **2011–12 series**, **24.38%** is the broader **Food Index** (food articles plus manufactured food products), not food articles alone. Do not confuse this with CPI's food-and-beverages group. [Office of Economic Adviser release](https://eaindustry.nic.in/pdf_files/cmonthly.pdf).

topics.title: Indian monsoon: circulation, rainfall and resilience
topics.subject: India & World Geography
topics.markdown:
## Seasonal circulation
- Monsoon derives from Arabic **mausim** (season): a large-scale seasonal reversal of winds, with marked wet/dry seasons. Land–sea thermal contrast, pressure gradients, shifting tropical convergence, ocean conditions and relief act together.
| Season | Circulation / rainfall |
| --- | --- |
| Southwest, June–September | Moist oceanic inflow; Arabian Sea and Bay of Bengal branches; roughly 75% of annual Indian rainfall |
| Northeast, October–December | Seasonal retreat and northeasterly flow; moisture gained over the Bay of Bengal supplies southeastern peninsular India, especially Tamil Nadu and coastal Andhra Pradesh |
- Normal southwest onset over **Kerala around 1 June**; onset dates vary. Active/break spells and uneven distribution matter alongside seasonal totals. [IMD monsoon information](https://mausam.imd.gov.in/responsive/monsooninformation_monsoon_activity.php).
## Mechanism and controls
Summer heating of land and northwest India  
↓  
Thermal low + northward tropical convergence/monsoon trough  
↓  
Cross-equatorial inflow turns southwesterly  
↓  
Ocean moisture + convergence + mountain lifting → rainfall.
- **ITCZ:** convergence/low-pressure belt shifts north in boreal summer; the established monsoon trough and embedded disturbances organise rainfall.
- **Tibetan Plateau and Himalayas:** elevated heating and a barrier to cold/dry extratropical air help shape circulation; their roles cannot be reduced to one heat-source explanation.
- **Subtropical westerly jet:** lies south of the Himalayas in winter and shifts north in summer. **Tropical easterly jet:** upper-level summer circulation associated with the monsoon; its presence alone does not determine onset or rainfall totals.
- **Somali/Findlater jet:** strong low-level cross-equatorial flow near East Africa and over the Arabian Sea helps transport moisture toward India. [IMD research on mountains and jets](https://mausamjournal.imd.gov.in/index.php/MAUSAM/article/view/3089).
## Regional contrasts
- Western Ghats' windward slopes: heavy orographic rain; interior Deccan: rain-shadow effects.
- Northeast, including Meghalaya's Mawsynram/Cherrapunji: exceptionally wet because moist inflow meets relief; northern plains: generally moderate to high monsoon rain with strong regional variation.
- Western Rajasthan and parts of Gujarat: lower, erratic rainfall; **Gujarat as a whole is not uniformly arid**. Eastern coastal areas gain important autumn/winter rain as northeasterlies cross the Bay.
## Why distribution matters
- Kharif rice, pulses and cotton: onset controls sowing; dry spells/excess rain affect yields and food security. Rural incomes, consumer demand and food inflation respond; good rainfall is one contributor to growth, not a guarantee.
- Rivers, aquifers, lakes and reservoirs recharge; irrigation and hydropower depend on stored water and inflows.
- Floods, landslides and poor urban drainage damage roads, railways, buildings and livelihoods. Cholera is waterborne; **dengue and malaria are mosquito-borne**, with vector risks influenced by standing water and weather. [WHO vector-borne diseases](https://www.who.int/en/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/vector-borne-diseases).
- Rain supports vegetation and biodiversity; intense events can erode soil and degrade habitats.
## Forecasting and adaptation
- **India Meteorological Department (IMD)** monitors onset, advance, rainfall and warnings using satellites, Doppler radar, weather balloons and numerical models. National Monsoon Mission strengthens dynamical forecast capability.
- Forecasts → timely crop decisions and flood warnings → storage/drainage management → insurance and recovery.
- PM Fasal Bima Yojana addresses eligible crop-loss risks; watershed development, rainwater harvesting, water conservation and urban drainage/resilient infrastructure reduce exposure. The source's generic “National Watershed Project” label should be read as watershed initiatives, without inventing a specific notified scheme.
- Crop diversification, drought-tolerant varieties and climate-resilient infrastructure complement early warning. Assess **where, when and how intensely** rain falls, not just whether the national total is above/below normal.

topics.title: Vasuki indicus: giant Eocene snake
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Fossil and significance
- IIT Roorkee researchers described **Vasuki indicus** in **Scientific Reports, April 2024**; the April 2025 issue revisits that discovery. Fossils were collected in **2005** from the Panandhro lignite mine, Kutch, Gujarat.
- **27 vertebrae**, middle Eocene, approximately **47 million years old**; belongs to extinct **Madtsoiidae**. Vertebral measurements give estimated length **10.9–15.2 m**, with uncertainty across estimation methods; comparable to Colombia's Titanoboa rather than a conclusively measured longest snake.
- Robust vertebrae suggest a large, slow terrestrial ambush predator, probably using constriction. Turtles, crocodilians, catfish and primitive whales occurred in associated deposits; actual prey is uncertain.
- Warm Eocene environments and ectothermy help interpret reptile gigantism. Fossils also illuminate snake evolution, Indian-plate biogeography and dispersal; they do not predict imminent giant snakes under modern warming.
- Name honours the mythological serpent Vasuki; cultural naming is separate from scientific identification. Among living snakes, reticulated pythons are longest; green anacondas are especially heavy.
[Original study](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-024-58377-0).

topics.title: Kailash Mansarovar Yatra
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## April 2025 diplomatic context
- India and China agreed in **January 2025** to resume the pilgrimage in **summer 2025**, after suspension since 2020 amid the pandemic and strained relations. At this issue date, resumption was a planned confidence-building measure; diplomatic cooperation does not settle the boundary dispute. [Official January outcome](https://www.eoibeijing.gov.in/news_detail.php?newsid=1528).
- MEA organises the annual pilgrimage with China, Uttarakhand/Sikkim/Delhi administrations and ITBP. Eligible Indian citizens require passports and medical fitness; pilgrims bear costs, with no MEA subsidy.
| Route | Recall |
| --- | --- |
| Lipulekh, Uttarakhand | Traditional route resumed in 1981; demanding high-altitude trekking; sensitive India–Nepal–China border region |
| Nathu La, Sikkim | Introduced 2015; substantially motorable, though high-altitude health risks remain |
## Geography and faith
- **Mount Kailash (~6,638 m)** and freshwater **Lake Mansarovar** lie in Tibet Autonomous Region, China, in the Trans-Himalayan landscape. The wider region contains headwaters of **Indus, Sutlej, Brahmaputra/Yarlung Tsangpo and Karnali**; these do not all flow directly out of Mansarovar.
- Hindu traditions associate Kailash with Shiva; Jain tradition associates Ashtapada with first Tirthankara Rishabhanatha; Tibetan Buddhism with Chakrasamvara/Demchok; Bon regards the landscape as sacred.
- Cultural diplomacy, people-to-people contact and route coordination can rebuild trust; border sensitivity, environmental limits and pilgrim health require cooperation.
[MEA pilgrimage information](https://www.mea.gov.in/faq-kmy.htm).

topics.title: Ranthambore Tiger Reserve
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Location and ecology
- Eastern **Rajasthan**, Sawai Madhopur–Karauli landscape, at the meeting of **Aravalli and Vindhyan** terrain; **Banas** to the north, **Chambal** to the south.
- Among the original nine Project Tiger reserves in **1973**; Ranthambore National Park declared **1980**. Reserve landscape includes **Kailadevi** and **Sawai Mansingh** sanctuaries; the National Chambal Sanctuary is a distinct protected area, not automatically a reserve component. [NTCA assessment](https://ntca.gov.in/assets/uploads/Reports/MEE/Evaluation_reports_TRs.pdf).
- Dry deciduous woodland and grasslands; **Dhok (Anogeissus pendula)** dominant. Tigers, leopards, sloth bears, striped hyenas and jackals; prey include sambar, chital, nilgai and wild boar; diverse terrestrial/water birds.
- Ranthambore Fort is part of UNESCO's **Hill Forts of Rajasthan**, within the park landscape.
## Coexistence
- The issue reports a fatal tiger attack on a child: proximity to wildlife requires rapid local response and conflict prevention.
- Livestock grazing, settlements, habitat fragmentation, poaching and excessive tourism can increase pressure. Combine corridor protection, managed visitor access, community eco-development, early warning and timely locally applicable compensation.

topics.title: National Commission for Women
topics.subject: Indian Polity
topics.markdown:
## Institution and composition
- **Statutory**, not constitutional: constituted in **January 1992** under the **National Commission for Women Act, 1990**. The 1974 Committee on the Status of Women helped build the case for a national watchdog; administrative ministry is Women and Child Development.
- Central Government nominates **Chairperson + five members + member-secretary**. Chairperson must be committed to women's cause; members have relevant legal, labour, voluntary-sector, health, education or other experience. At least **one SC and one ST member** among the five. Member-secretary is an appropriate expert or civil servant.
- Section 4: term specified by Centre, **not exceeding three years**; resignation provisions differ for a serving government member-secretary.
- Removal grounds: insolvency; conviction/sentence for moral turpitude; unsoundness of mind declared by competent court; refusal/incapacity to act; absence without leave from **three consecutive meetings**; abuse of position prejudicial to public interest. Opportunity of hearing applies. Mere other paid employment is not an enumerated ground.
[Act, Sections 3–4](https://cdn.ncw.gov.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/01/ncwact_3.pdf).
## Functions and powers
- **Section 10**: investigate safeguards; report annually/otherwise to Centre; review laws; take complaints and suo motu notice; research discrimination; advise development planning; inspect jails/remand homes and other custodial institutions holding women; support litigation involving large groups of women.
- Centre consults NCW on major policy matters affecting women (**Section 16**).
- For specified investigations NCW has civil-court powers: summon/examine witnesses on oath, require documents, receive affidavits, requisition public records and issue examination commissions. Its recommendations are advisory; it is not a criminal court imposing punishment.
- April 2025 context: NCW formed a panel to investigate reported violence affecting women in Murshidabad.
## Effectiveness and reform
- Main constraints: follow-up on recommendations, staff/resources, rural/tribal access, awareness and preventive action. Statutory SC/ST representation already exists; assess effectiveness rather than claiming the law provides none.
- Improve legal literacy, regional outreach, legal-aid referrals, trauma-sensitive staff training, transparent complaint tracking and coordination with State commissions/police. Extra enforcement powers would require legal change, with safeguards.
- Constitutional links: **Articles 14, 15(3), 39(a)/(d)** and India's **CEDAW** commitments.
- **Law Commission Report 257 (2015)** concerns guardianship/custody reforms, not an NCW punitive-powers recommendation. [Official report](https://lawcommissionofindia.nic.in/report-no-257-custody-laws/).

topics.title: Northeast India: development and integration
topics.subject: Governance in India
topics.markdown:
## Strategic assets
- Eight States: **Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Sikkim, Tripura**. Borders with **Bangladesh, Bhutan, China, Myanmar and Nepal** give the region a central place in **Act East**; the narrow Siliguri corridor reinforces connectivity concerns.
- **India–Myanmar–Thailand Trilateral Highway**, **Kaladan multimodal project** and **SASEC** improve regional links; projects under development should not be treated as fully operational corridors.
- Eastern Himalayan/Indo-Burma biodiversity, forest carbon, water resources and substantial hydropower potential; potential capacity is not installed output. Languages, living root bridges and Nagaland's Hornbill Festival support cultural tourism.
- Organic/temperate horticulture, ginger (including Karbi Anglong), floriculture, medicinal plants, bamboo and sports talent offer diversified livelihoods.
## Constraints → practical responses
| Constraint | Response |
| --- | --- |
| Insurgency and ethnic conflict, including Manipur violence since 2023 | Dialogue, accountable security, fair representation and locally trusted reconciliation |
| Poor road/rail/digital links; delayed projects | Last-mile connectivity, coordinated execution, reliable power/internet and transparent monitoring |
| Farmer dependence on intermediaries; weak certification/storage/markets | Producer organisations, credit, processing, quality certification and market links |
| Floods, landslides, erratic rainfall and ecologically risky construction | Basin planning, early warning, resilient infrastructure and cumulative environmental assessment |
| Border insecurity and Golden Triangle narcotics routes | Coordinated police/border response, community intelligence and treatment/prevention |
| Weak governance and social distrust | Fiscal/local planning capacity, participation and consistent rights-sensitive delivery |
## Policy options
- Cultural exchanges and indigenous-knowledge research; ASEAN academic links; digital skills/BPO and enterprise hubs; better sports facilities and coaching; bamboo and medicinal-plant value chains; responsible homestays/ecotourism circuits.
- These are **proposed interventions**, not evidence that named 'Digital Silk Road', 'Indigenous Knowledge Universities' or an 'Olympic Training Centre' were launched.
- Balance growth and hydropower with biodiversity, community land rights and hazard exposure; region-wide literacy/ethnic-count figures require a stated dataset/year.
[Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region](https://www.mdoner.gov.in/).
## Mains practice
Discuss the challenges and strategic initiatives required to enhance socio-economic development and integration of the Northeast region of India. Suggest innovative policy interventions in light of recent developments.

topics.title: Almonds: horticulture and cardiometabolic evidence
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Crop and trade recall
- **Prunus dulcis**, **Rosaceae**; deciduous tree, edible seed of a drupe, marketed as a tree nut. Native to western/central Asian regions.
- Cold winters provide dormancy/chilling; warm dry summers aid maturation; well-drained loamy soil is useful. Indian temperate cultivation is concentrated in **Jammu & Kashmir**, with Himachal Pradesh and other suitable Himalayan areas.
- India depends heavily on imports; **United States/California** and **Australia** are important suppliers. California's Mediterranean climate supports a major almond industry; exact import/production shares vary by year and whether measured in-shell or shelled.
- Value-added food processing, storage and horticultural diversification can improve farmer returns. MIDH and food-processing infrastructure schemes are relevant broader programmes; source does not establish a separate almond-specific NMSA scheme.
## April 2025 health report
- Newspaper describes a **2025 perspective/evidence synthesis** in *Current Developments in Nutrition*, drawing on meta-analyses and a July 2024 roundtable funded by the **Almond Board of California**; it is not one new trial proving universal benefits.
- Evidence suggests small improvements in **LDL cholesterol** and **diastolic blood pressure**, no consistent weight gain, and improved glycaemic responses in some populations. Almonds provide unsaturated fats, protein, fibre and vitamin E.
- Dose, dietary substitution, baseline health and study duration affect results; heterogeneous/underpowered studies leave research gaps. Findings support a balanced dietary pattern rather than a cure for hypertension, diabetes or guaranteed weight loss.
[Original perspective](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11786730/).

topics.title: Leptobrachium aryatium: new Northeast frog
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Identification
- New **Megophryidae** frog described in **Zootaxa, 14 April 2025**, from **Garbhanga Reserve Forest, Assam**, with reported range into adjoining **Ri-Bhoi, Meghalaya**. Named for **Arya Vidyapeeth College, Guwahati**; earlier material had been identified as *L. smithi*.
- Distinct **orange upper iris/black remainder**, net-like dark throat markings and diagnostic calls; broad-headed stocky frog. Adult snout–vent lengths approximately **49–55 mm males**, **53–62 mm females**.
- Integrative taxonomy combined morphology → **mitochondrial 16S rRNA** phylogeny → call analysis, distinguishing it from related *L. sylheticum* and *L. smithi*.
## Conservation recall
- Garbhanga lies near **Deepor Beel**, Assam's Ramsar wetland, in an elephant-corridor landscape. Habitat connectivity protects amphibians as well as large mammals.
- Amphibians' sensitivity to water quality, habitat disturbance and climate makes them useful bioindicators; a new description is not itself an IUCN threat-category assessment.
- Protect forest/stream microhabitats, monitor populations and control fragmentation/pollution. Source's sanctuary proposal should be distinguished from a formally gazetted designation.
[Original description](https://www.mapress.com/zt/article/view/zootaxa.5621.1.4); [research institution announcement](https://ustm.ac.in/event/33078-2/).

topics.title: Gutti Koya displacement and rehabilitation
topics.subject: Social Problems In India
topics.markdown:
## Displacement and present difficulties
- The issue calls for durable rehabilitation of **Gutti Koya/Gond communities displaced from Chhattisgarh during counterinsurgency from 2005**, many now living in Andhra Pradesh/Telangana. Source estimates nearly **50,000** affected; use as a reported estimate, not a settled census.
- Forced grouping into roadside camps sought to separate insurgents from civilian support, disrupting forest livelihoods and community ties. Historical village grouping in Mizoram during the 1960s offers a comparison; it should not be presented as the sole cause of the later peace accord.
- They are **internally displaced persons (IDPs)**: crossing a State boundary within India does not make them international refugees. Housing insecurity, disputed occupation, missing documents, education/welfare access and intergenerational exclusion persist.
- Reports allege evictions, house demolition and planting on cultivated plots; safe rehabilitation must address these allegations and rights. Some displaced people assist anti-Maoist operations through terrain/language knowledge; basic rights do not depend on security service.
## Forest rights and constitutional precision
- **FRA Section 3(1)(m)** recognises in-situ rehabilitation, including alternative land, for eligible forest-dwelling STs/other traditional forest dwellers **illegally evicted or displaced before 13 December 2005 without legal rehabilitation**. It is not an automatic blanket grant to every later migrant settlement.
- Claims depend on statutory eligibility/evidence and prescribed procedures. **Section 4(5)** bars eviction/removal until recognition and verification are complete; Gram Sabha participation is central. PESA applies in notified Fifth Schedule areas, not automatically to every settlement.
- **Article 342** ST lists are State/UT specific. Migration does not erase ethnic identity; it can affect destination-State entitlement. President initially specifies the list after consultation; subsequent inclusion/exclusion requires **Parliamentary law**, not a fresh executive notification alone.
[Forest Rights Act and rules](https://tribal.nic.in/downloads/FRA/FRAActnRulesBook.pdf).
## Rehabilitation design
- Centre and origin/destination States should jointly verify displaced families, documentation and claims; offer voluntary safe return or supported settlement, housing, livelihoods, schooling and health access; provide grievance review and time-bound monitoring.
- A national IDP framework drawing on UN Guiding Principles could coordinate protection and durable solutions; India has no comprehensive dedicated IDP statute.
- **Bru–Reang settlement agreement: 16 January 2020**, not 2019. Centre, Tripura, Mizoram and Bru representatives agreed permanent settlement in Tripura for roughly **34,000**, with housing/financial support. This negotiated model offers lessons, not automatic legal equivalence or proof every family had completed rehabilitation by April 2025.
[Official Bru agreement context](https://www.pmindia.gov.in/en/news_updates/pm-says-bru-reang-agreement-provides-succour-and-relief-to-over-35000-refugees/).

topics.title: Rang Mahal gateway: Hyderabad heritage restoration
topics.subject: Indian Art and Culture
topics.markdown:
## Historical and architectural significance
- Surviving gateway of Khair-un-Nissa’s Rang Mahal in the former British Residency precinct, Hyderabad; associated with Khair-un-Nissa and **James Achilles Kirkpatrick**, British Resident at the Nizam’s court, in the early nineteenth century.
- The palace no longer survives; gateway features include **paired tapering columns, incised stucco, flaring overhangs and jharokhas**. The entrance to a pleasure garden illustrates Deccan aristocratic architecture and cultural interaction.
- The issue reports restoration with the **Deccan Heritage Foundation** and the university occupying the former Residency precinct. DHF lists restoration of the Rang Mahal pavilion and garden among completed projects. [DHF project register](https://www.deccan-heritage-foundation.org/restoration-projects/).
## Conservation approach
- Protect surviving original fabric, including remaining columns; document condition before intervention, use compatible repairs and maintain the restored site.
- Adaptive reuse: cultural programmes, interpretation, conservation training for students/local communities, garden revival and responsible tourism.
- Link heritage conservation with urban green space and community participation. HRIDAY and Smart Cities illustrate urban-heritage policy themes; the issue does not establish that either funded this restoration.
- The Residency precinct has broader colonial history; a specific gateway connection to **1857** requires supporting evidence rather than inference from its location.

topics.title: Central Consumer Protection Authority
topics.subject: Governance in India
topics.markdown:
## Statutory institution
- **CCPA**, under **Section 10, Consumer Protection Act 2019**, protects consumers as a class against rights violations, unfair trade practices and misleading advertising. Relevant provisions commenced **24 July 2020**; Act replaced the 1986 framework. [India Code commencement](https://www.indiacode.nic.in/indiacode/handle/123456789/21423?view_type=browse).
- Chief Commissioner and other Commissioners appointed by Central Government; the Act does not permanently prescribe exactly two Commissioners divided into goods/services. An investigation wing is headed by a Director-General.
## Powers and limits
| Provision | Function |
|---|---|
| Sections 18–19 | Investigate on complaint, government direction or own motion; refer matters to relevant regulators; file complaints before consumer commissions/intervene in proceedings |
| Section 20 | Recall unsafe goods, withdraw dangerous services, reimburse prices and stop unfair practices |
| Section 21 | Direct discontinuance/modification of misleading ads; impose specified penalties and prohibit endorsements |
- Manufacturer/endorser misleading-ad penalty: up to **₹10 lakh**, subsequent contravention **₹50 lakh**; endorsement prohibition up to **one year**, subsequent contravention **three years**, subject to statutory safeguards.
- CCPA enforcement is distinct from individual compensation adjudication by District/State/National consumer commissions. Licence suspension is not a blanket CCPA administrative power; the Act separately provides court-ordered consequences for specified offences. [Consumer Protection Act](https://www.indiacode.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/15256/1/eng201935.pdf).
## Digital-market relevance
- E-commerce claims, deceptive advertising and systemic unsafe-product sales make proactive enforcement valuable.
- Improve investigation capacity, consumer awareness, regulator coordination and platform accountability; digital and cross-border transactions complicate evidence collection and enforcement.

topics.title: Prison overcrowding and electronic monitoring
topics.subject: Governance in India
topics.markdown:
## Dated prison picture
- **31 December 2022:** **5,73,220** inmates against capacity **4,36,266**; occupancy about **131.4%**, undertrials **4,34,302 (75.8%)** (the issue rounds this to 75.7%). Occupancy measures total inmates/capacity; undertrial does not mean convicted.
- Supreme Court publication **Prisons in India: Mapping Prison Manuals and Measures for Reformation and Decongestion**, released by President on **5 November 2024**. [President’s release](https://www.presidentofindia.gov.in/press_releases/president-india-releases-three-publications-supreme-court-india).
## Proposed alternative
- Source describes phased tagging of selected low/moderate-risk undertrials with good conduct, following risk assessment and feasibility/community-readiness evaluation. This is a reform recommendation, not a universal implemented bail scheme.
- Potential benefits: less custodial crowding/cost, family contact and rehabilitation while supervising compliance. US, UK, Canada, Australia and Malaysia offer differing bail/parole/home-confinement models; results depend on design.
## Legal safeguards
- Prisons are a **State List** subject. **Model Prisons and Correctional Services Act 2023**, shared with States/UTs **10 May 2023**, is a model for local enactment; it provides for tracking during temporary release/leave, not automatic national authority to tag all undertrials. [MHA reforms](https://www.mha.gov.in/en/commoncontent/prison-reforms-pr-section).
- **Frank Vitus v NCB, 8 July 2024:** a bail condition enabling constant tracking violates Article 21 privacy; Court deleted the Google Maps PIN condition. A dropped PIN is not itself a live-tracking technology. [Judgment](https://www.narcoticsindia.nic.in/Judgments/Frank_Vitus_vs_Narcotics_Control_Bureau_on_8_July_2024.pdf).
- Require lawful, necessary, proportionate conditions; judicial oversight, short retention/access controls, review and grievance mechanisms. Avoid widening supervision to people otherwise entitled to ordinary bail or shifting unaffordable device costs onto poor accused.
- Faster trials, legal aid, effective bail and periodic undertrial review remain central; technology cannot resolve every cause of incarceration.

topics.title: Coal-power pollution and rice–wheat yields
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Study and estimated agricultural cost
- Stanford-led study used electricity generation/wind data for **144 Indian power stations** and satellite NO₂ observations to estimate coal-related pollution over cropland; effects detected up to **100 km** away.
- Eliminating the modelled coal emissions during important **January–February and September–October** growing periods could increase annual rice output value by **US$420 million** and wheat by **US$400 million**. These are counterfactual estimates, not realised compensation or measured nationwide uniform losses.
- Some exposed areas show yield effects approaching **10%**; Chhattisgarh has particularly high exposure, with substantial estimated gains in parts of West Bengal and Madhya Pradesh. [Stanford study explanation](https://news.stanford.edu/stories/2025/02/coal-emissions-cost-india-millions-crop-damages).
## Pollutants and appropriate controls
| Pollutant | Impact/control distinction |
|---|---|
| NOₓ, including NO₂ | Plant stress; ozone/secondary-particle formation; combustion controls and suitable denitrification technologies |
| SO₂ | Acidification/secondary particles; **flue-gas desulfurisation (FGD)** uses sorbents to remove sulphur compounds |
| Particulates/fly ash | Health, light/soil/water effects; **electrostatic precipitators** remove particles, not gaseous NO₂ |
| CO₂ | Climate forcing; efficiency and cleaner energy reduce emissions |
- Supercritical/ultra-supercritical plants improve thermal efficiency; they do not eliminate all pollutants or substitute for pollutant-specific controls.
## Policy application
- Prioritise high-exposure plants near cropland; strengthen emission monitoring/enforcement, cleaner power, ash management and agriculture–environment coordination.
- Include food/feed and farmer-income losses alongside health/climate costs. Agroforestry and resilient farming complement emissions reduction rather than neutralise the source.
- Source’s 2024 Hunger Index rank **105/127** is contextual, not evidence that coal caused that ranking; a Ministry of Coal budget increase likewise does not directly measure electricity output or plant pollution.

topics.title: Primary health care: access, trust and financial protection
topics.subject: Social Problems In India
topics.markdown:
## Comprehensive care
- Primary care combines **promotion → prevention → treatment → rehabilitation → palliation**, including NCDs, mental health, elderly care, communicable disease and environmental/social determinants.
- **Ayushman Bharat (2018)** originally has two complementary components: Health and Wellness Centres (now **Ayushman Arogya Mandirs, AAMs**) for comprehensive primary care, and **PM-JAY** for eligible secondary/tertiary hospitalisation with **₹5 lakh/family/year** cover.
- **PM-ABHIM (2021)** is a separate infrastructure mission supporting laboratories, surveillance and critical-care preparedness; **ABDM** supports digital health infrastructure.
- **1,75,418 AAMs operational as of 10 December 2024**. Out-of-pocket spending share of total health expenditure fell **48.8% (2017–18) → 39.4% (2021–22)**; a falling share does not establish a fall in absolute per-capita spending or exclusive causation by one scheme. [Health Ministry](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2084188&lang=2&reg=48).
## Quality, affordability and confidence
- Catastrophic health expenditure depends on the indicator: a **40% capacity-to-pay** threshold is one method; SDG monitoring also uses **10%/25% of household income or expenditure**. Distinguish measurement from insurance entitlement.
- **IPHS (introduced 2007)** specifies facility/service norms; **NQAS** evaluates eight domains: service provision, patient rights, inputs, support services, clinical care, infection control, quality management and outcomes. [NHSRC standards](https://nhsrcindia.org/national-quality-assurance-standards).
- Public trust improves when care is timely, clean, respectful and dependable. Staffing/absenteeism, uneven quality, weak referrals, digital gaps and urban migrant access can undermine use.
- Ensure free/affordable essential medicines and diagnostics, continuity of NCD care, NUHM urban primary services, community oversight and transparent patient-experience audits. Digital records and telemedicine require functioning referral systems and privacy protections.

topics.title: Cardiovascular risk among young adults
topics.subject: Social Problems In India
topics.markdown:
## Distinctions and burden
- **Myocardial infarction (heart attack):** interruption of blood supply injures heart muscle, commonly after coronary plaque rupture and clot formation. Cardiac arrest is loss of effective pumping; heart failure is impaired pumping/filling. These diagnoses are not interchangeable.
- Warning features include chest discomfort, breathlessness, sweating, pain radiating to arm/jaw/back, dizziness and sometimes nausea; prompt emergency assessment matters.
- Source’s **17.9 million CVD deaths in 2019**, roughly **85% heart attack/stroke**, concerns all ages and broad cardiovascular disease; it does not quantify a new Indian youth heart-attack trend. [WHO cardiovascular overview](https://www.who.int/health-topics/cardiovascular-diseases/).
- Indian **28.1% of deaths in 2016 versus 15.2% in 1990** refers to CVD burden. The source’s **25.43% registered deaths in 2020** cannot be treated as a national heart-attack-only share without its medical-certification denominator and disease classification; the quoted **272/100,000 versus 235 globally** also needs year/standardisation for comparison.
## Risk and prevention
- Tobacco, harmful alcohol use, inactivity, unhealthy diet, obesity, raised blood pressure/glucose/lipids and air pollution increase cardiovascular risk; stress, poor sleep, stimulant drugs and family history also matter.
- COVID can affect the cardiovascular system, but finding viral RNA does not by itself establish the cause of every young person’s heart attack. ICMR’s 47-hospital case-control study of unexplained sudden deaths found no increased risk from COVID vaccination; sudden death is not synonymous with confirmed MI. [ICMR 2023–24 report](https://www.icmr.gov.in/icmrobject/uploads/Documents/1744706555_icmr_annualreport_2023-24_78804328_1.pdf).
- Promote healthy food, tobacco control, walkable/cyclable spaces, workplace wellness and appropriate primary-care risk assessment with reliable treatment/referral; integrate mental-health support and cardiac rehabilitation.
- Premature disease raises treatment costs, lost earnings and household stress, threatening human capital. Financial protection should accompany prevention and continuity of care; symptoms and personal risk require clinical assessment.

topics.title: Decarbonising India’s logistics sector
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Why green logistics matters
- Freight transport, storage and distribution connect producers with markets. Cleaner logistics supports competitiveness, energy security, urban air quality and India's **net-zero 2070** ambition.
- Road dependence and diesel trucks, energy-intensive warehouses and difficult-to-electrify aviation are major challenges. Rail and water transport can lower emissions per tonne-kilometre where routes, load factors and first/last-mile connections are suitable.
- The source reports logistics at **13.5% of national GHG emissions**, road transport at **88% of that**, and trucks at **38% of CO₂ emissions**; these have different or unspecified denominators. Treat them as source estimates requiring dataset/year verification rather than comparable shares. The source also reports roads handling about **70% of freight** and **90% of passenger movement**; passenger and freight shares are distinct metrics. Its 2022 modal-split image reinforces road dominance, with rail next and shipping/air much smaller.
## Measures and policy links
| Lever | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Multimodal networks | Connect rail freight, coastal shipping and inland waterways with efficient terminals and last-mile roads |
| Trucking | EV charging, cleaner fleets, route optimisation and consolidation of loads |
| Warehouses | Energy audits, efficient lighting/cooling, rooftop renewables and appropriate green-building ratings such as GRIHA |
| Shipping/aviation | Research sustainable fuels; assess lifecycle emissions, fuel availability and safety |
- **PM Gati Shakti** supports integrated infrastructure planning; **National Logistics Policy** supports efficient logistics systems and coordination. [Government logistics overview](https://static.pib.gov.in/WriteReadData/specificdocs/documents/2025/feb/doc202521495001.pdf).
- The source's Delhi–Jaipur overhead-electric-highway example and tripling waterborne cargo by 2030 are proposals/source-reported targets; implementation and the cargo baseline require verification.
- LNG, biofuels, hydrogen and ammonia differ in lifecycle carbon impact and hazards; LNG remains a fossil fuel. Solar assistance may reduce vessel energy demand but does not automatically power all ship operations.
## International benchmark and implementation
- **IMO 2023 strategy:** net-zero international-shipping GHG emissions **by or around 2050**; indicative reductions against 2008 of **at least 20%, striving for 30%, by 2030** and **at least 70%, striving for 80%, by 2040**. The source's 50%-by-2050 figure belongs to the older ambition. [IMO strategy](https://www.imo.org/en/OurWork/Environment/Pages/2023-IMO-Strategy-on-Reduction-of-GHG-Emissions-from-Ships.aspx).
- Rail use in China/US illustrates modal choice; the source's China 50% share needs a comparable metric before adoption.
- Constraints: capital costs, charging/fuel networks, reliability, technology maturity and inter-ministry coordination. Use PPPs, targeted incentives, green finance and R&D, while tracking actual emissions per tonne-kilometre and total emissions.
- **Efficient logistics → less empty running and energy use → lower costs and emissions**, provided growing freight demand does not outweigh efficiency gains.

topics.title: Right to peaceful protest and limits on strikes
topics.subject: Indian Polity
topics.markdown:
## Constitutional basis
- Peaceful protest draws principally on **Article 19(1)(a)** (speech/expression), **19(1)(b)** (peaceful assembly without arms) and **19(1)(c)** (associations/unions). Article 21 supports dignity and personal liberty; the specific assembly guarantee is in Article 19.
| Right | Restriction clause and grounds |
| --- | --- |
| Speech/expression | **19(2):** sovereignty/integrity, State security, friendly foreign relations, public order, decency/morality, contempt of court, defamation, incitement to an offence |
| Peaceful assembly | **19(3):** sovereignty/integrity and public order |
| Association | **19(4):** sovereignty/integrity, public order and morality |
- Restrictions must be imposed by law and be reasonable; the broader speech grounds cannot all be transferred to the assembly clause. [Constitution, Legislative Department](https://www.legislative.gov.in/documents).
## Courts and practical balance
- **Ramlila Maidan Incident (2012):** peaceful assembly/protest is constitutionally protected; arbitrary suppression violates that protection.
- **Amit Sahni v Commissioner of Police, 7 October 2020** addressed the Shaheen Bagh protests that began in 2019: public roads cannot be occupied indefinitely. Distinguish the protest's starting year from the judgment year.
- **Strike ≠ peaceful assembly:** there is no general fundamental right to strike. Labour legislation may regulate permitted industrial action, notice, dispute procedures and sector-specific restrictions; government servants do not possess a fundamental right to strike.
- Mains balance: facilitate peaceful dissent through proportionate policing, suitable locations and dialogue, while preserving public access, safety and others' rights.
- [Supreme Court, Amit Sahni judgment](https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/2020/2418/2418_2020_36_1501_24294_Judgement_07-Oct-2020.pdf).

topics.title: K2-18b and possible atmospheric biosignatures
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## April 2025 finding
- Cambridge-led researchers used **JWST's Mid-Infrared Instrument (MIRI)** to report evidence for **dimethyl sulphide (DMS) and/or dimethyl disulphide (DMDS)** in K2-18b's atmosphere at approximately **3-sigma** significance. Overlapping spectral signatures mean both molecules were not independently established.
- DMS/DMDS have biological sources on Earth, including marine microorganisms. A possible atmospheric biosignature motivates follow-up observations and chemical modelling; it is not proof of extraterrestrial organisms. **3-sigma is not a probability that life exists.** [Original research, 16 April 2025](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.12267).
## Planet and observing method
| Feature | Recall |
| --- | --- |
| Discovery | 2015, Kepler's K2 mission |
| Distance | Approximately 120–124 light-years |
| Size | Approximately **2.6 Earth radii** |
| Mass | Approximately **8.6–8.9 Earth masses**, a mass estimate rather than “8.6 times bigger” |
| Orbit | About 33 days around a cool M-type red dwarf, in its habitable zone |
- Often described as a **sub-Neptune** and possible **Hycean** candidate: hydrogen-rich atmosphere with a proposed ocean beneath it. Habitable-zone location allows potential liquid water under suitable conditions; the actual ocean, surface conditions and habitability remain unresolved.
- Earlier Webb spectra found **methane and carbon dioxide**. Transit spectroscopy measures wavelength-dependent starlight passing through the atmosphere; researchers infer molecules from absorption features and atmospheric models. [Cambridge announcement](https://www.cam.ac.uk/stories/strongest-hints-of-biological-activity).
- **JWST:** launched in **2021**, NASA–ESA–CSA collaboration; infrared observations from an orbit around **Sun–Earth L2** enable early-universe studies and exoplanet spectroscopy.
## Scientific reasoning and India
- Repeat observations, instrument/systematic checks, alternative atmospheric models and laboratory studies of abiotic production are essential. Methane reports on Mars and debated phosphine claims on Venus illustrate that chemical detection and biological interpretation are separate questions.
- Indian opportunities: spectroscopy/infrared instrumentation, planetary and astrobiology research, international collaboration, education and planetary-protection standards. **AstroSat** and **XPoSat** expand astronomy capability; XPoSat launched in **January 2024**, rather than being an upcoming mission in April 2025. Gaganyaan develops human-spaceflight capability rather than directly detecting exoplanet life.
- **Spectral feature → molecular inference → possible biosignature → independent verification** is the evidence chain; subsequent findings should be dated separately from this April report.
- [ISRO XPoSat launch](https://www.isro.gov.in/ISRO_EN/PSLV_C58_XPoSat_Mission.html).

topics.title: Bhagavad Gita and Natyashastra: UNESCO documentary heritage
topics.subject: Indian Art and Culture
topics.markdown:
## April 2025 inscription
- **India's nominated manuscript holdings at Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (BORI), Pune** entered UNESCO's **Memory of the World International Register in 2025**: the **Manuscript Collection of Bhagavadgītā** and **Manuscript of the Nāṭyaśāstra of Bharatamuni**. Recognition concerns preserved documentary collections, rather than every edition of either text or a World Heritage site. [UNESCO Gita entry](https://www.unesco.org/en/memory-world/manuscript-collection-bhagavadgita-ancient-samgraha-grantha-indian-thought-world-wide-readership-and), [Natyashastra entry](https://www.unesco.org/en/memory-world/manuscript-natyasastra-bharatamuni-seminal-text-indian-performing-art).
- The 2025 round added **74 collections**, taking the international total to **570**; this is a dated total. [UN India announcement](https://india.un.org/en/293100-unesco-adds-bhagavadg%C4%ABt%C4%81-and-n%C4%81%E1%B9%ADya%C5%9B%C4%81stra-memory-world-register).
## Programme distinction
| UNESCO mechanism | What it safeguards |
|---|---|
| Memory of the World, launched **1992** | Documentary heritage: manuscripts, archives, recordings, audiovisual holdings; preservation and access |
| World Heritage Convention, **1972** | Cultural/natural sites of outstanding universal value |
| Intangible Cultural Heritage Convention, **2003** | Living practices, knowledge and expressions |
- MoW operates through **international, regional and national** structures; inscription on one register does not automatically mean inscription on another. It promotes conservation, digitisation, cataloguing and wider access while respecting cultural contexts. International nominations are normally considered in biennial cycles, with up to two national nominations per cycle; joint nominations are distinct. [UNESCO programme](https://www.unesco.org/en/memory-world/about).
## Texts to remember
- **Bhagavad Gita:** **700 verses, 18 chapters**, within the **Bhishma Parva of the Mahabharata**; Krishna–Arjuna dialogue in the epic's narrative. Dharma, **Karma Yoga**, **Jnana Yoga** and **Bhakti Yoga** connect duty, action, knowledge and devotion. Its literary/religious setting should not be mistaken for proof of literal historical events or a secure composition date.
- **Natyashastra:** Sanskrit performing-arts treatise traditionally attributed to **Bharata Muni**; ancient compilation, with approximate dating commonly spanning **2nd century BCE–2nd century CE**, rather than a known author's precise publication date. Covers **natya** (drama), **abhinaya** (expression/performance), **rasa** (aesthetic experience), **bhava** (emotion) and **sangita** (music).
- **Verse-count caution:** the source's 36,000 refers to a larger Natya/Gandharvaveda tradition in UNESCO's description. Do not present it unqualified as the size of the commonly studied Natyashastra, normally described as about **6,000 verses in 36 chapters**. [IGNOU teaching material](https://www.egyankosh.ac.in/bitstream/123456789/84054/1/Block-3.pdf).
## Earlier documentary examples and significance
- **Rigveda manuscripts: 2007**, correcting the source's 2005; **Saiva manuscripts in Pondicherry: 2005**. Other international entries include Abhinavagupta's works and the first NAM summit archives (**2023**), and Dutch East India Company archives (**2003**, multinational holdings). [UNESCO Rigveda](https://www.unesco.org/en/memory-world/rigveda).
- World examples in the source: Sri Lanka's **Mahavamsa**, Sakubei Yamamoto drawings, Shaiva Siddhanta manuscripts, Frankfurt Auschwitz trial recordings and Sheikh Mujibur Rahman's **7 March 1971** speech recording. Documentary value includes historical evidence and transmission across generations.
- India's benefits: preservation of fragile manuscripts, scholarly access, cultural diplomacy and soft power. Recognition creates an opportunity for sustained archival care; it does not by itself finance or complete conservation.

topics.title: Keonjhar: geography, tribal culture and mineral economy
topics.subject: India & World Geography
topics.markdown:
## Location and population
- **Keonjhar/Kendujhar**, northern **Odisha**, is an inland district; the source map places it within Odisha, not on the coast. Forested uplands and the **Baitarani**, associated with **Gonasika**, connect ecology, sacred geography and livelihoods.
- **Census 2011**: population **18,01,733**; Scheduled Tribes approximately **45%**. These are dated district figures, not current Odisha-wide proportions. [District demography](https://kendujhar.odisha.gov.in/en/about-district/demogrpahy), [Census ST abstract](https://censusindia.gov.in/nada/index.php/catalog/42194/study-description).
- Source-listed communities include **Munda, Kolh/Ho, Bhuiyan, Juang, Saanti/Sounti, Bathudi, Gond, Santhal, Oraon and Kondh**. **Juang is a PVTG**; this classification does not apply to every tribe in the district. [Tribal Affairs official list](https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=1577166&lang=2&reg=48).
## Festivals and dances
| Tradition | Revision cue |
|---|---|
| **Sarhul** | Munda spring festival; sal flowers and sacred grove worship |
| **Sohrai** | Munda cattle/agricultural prosperity festival |
| **Karmapuja** | Adivasi community worship and agrarian associations |
| **Chaitra/Uda Parab** | Seasonal festival associated locally with Chhau |
| **Changu** | Named for accompanying drum; prominent among Bhuiyans |
| **Juang and Ho dances** | Community celebration, song and percussion |
- Other source-listed festivals include **Nuakhai, Raja Parab, Baruni Jatra and Rath Jatra**; their presence does not make each unique to Keonjhar. [District culture account](https://kendujhar.odisha.gov.in/en/tourism/culture-Heritage).
- **Chhau** entered UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage Representative List in **2010**. Styles: **Seraikella (Jharkhand), Purulia (West Bengal), Mayurbhanj (Odisha)**. **First two use masks; Mayurbhanj does not**—correcting the source's blanket mask description. This is a living performance tradition, separate from UNESCO documentary heritage. [UNESCO Chhau](https://ich.unesco.org/en/RL/chhau-dance-00337).
## Mineral economy and inclusion
- Keonjhar is especially associated with **iron-ore mining**, alongside forest-resource use and agriculture. The source's broad iron-ore/chromite wording should not displace **Sukinda, Jajpur** as Odisha's principal chromite-location cue. [Government mining annexure](https://sansad.in/getFile/loksabhaquestions/annex/173/AU1616.pdf?source=pqals).
- Mining employment/revenue coexist with displacement, forest/water pressures and livelihood disruption. Development requires community participation, recognised land/forest rights, rehabilitation, accessible education/healthcare and environmental monitoring; mineral output alone does not demonstrate inclusive prosperity.

topics.title: Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor and the three-stage nuclear programme
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## PFBR at Kalpakkam
| Feature | Revision fact |
|---|---|
| Developer | BHAVINI, a DAE public-sector enterprise |
| Design output | 500 MWe; Tamil Nadu |
| Fuel | Uranium–plutonium mixed oxide (MOX) |
| Neutrons/coolant | Fast neutrons; liquid sodium; no neutron moderator |
| Breeding | Fertile U-238 blanket → fissile Pu-239 |
- **4 March 2024:** commencement of core loading witnessed by the Prime Minister. Core loading, first criticality, grid connection and commercial operation are separate milestones. The April 2025 article forecasts readiness in 2026; this is a forecast, not proof of commissioning. [PMO milestone](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2011347&lang=2&reg=48).
## Three-stage pathway
**Natural-uranium PHWR → recovered plutonium → fast breeders → eventual thorium/U-233 systems.**
1. PHWRs use heavy water as moderator/coolant and produce electricity and plutonium in spent fuel.
2. Fast breeders use plutonium-bearing fuel and breed further fissile material from U-238. Reprocessing/recycling links the stages.
3. Thorium-232 can breed U-233 for future thorium-based systems. AHWR is a development option; India does not already operate a commercial AHWR fleet. PFBR's present uranium blanket is not evidence of established commercial thorium operation.
## Significance and constraints
- Breeding improves utilisation of uranium resources and builds fissile inventory for long-term energy security. Indigenous design/manufacture supports technological capability and low-carbon electricity.
- Sodium transfers heat effectively without slowing neutrons substantially, but reacts with air/water: leak detection, separation of circuits and engineered safety matter.
- Delays, cost escalation, regulatory demonstration, fuel-cycle infrastructure, waste management and public confidence constrain deployment. Reprocessing recovers uranium/plutonium; radioactive waste still needs secure management. Avoid treating any design as accident-proof.

topics.title: Wheat cultivation, production estimates and food security
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Cultivation
- Wheat is a major **rabi cereal**, second to rice in India's cereal-production volume; central to northern/northwestern diets, procurement and PDS food security.
| Requirement | Revision cue |
|---|---|
| Season | Usually sown October–December; harvest spring/early summer varies by region |
| Climate | Cool growing season; warm, dry, sunny ripening |
| Source teaching ranges | About 10–15°C sowing, 21–26°C ripening; 50–100 cm rainfall |
| Soil | Well-drained loam/clay loam; irrigation important in major producing belts |
| Main states | Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Punjab, Haryana and Rajasthan; also Bihar, Gujarat and Maharashtra |
- Terminal heat shortens grain filling; rain/hail/winds near maturity can damage grain and cause lodging. Timely sowing, appropriate varieties, irrigation and ICAR/IMD advisories matter.
## April 2025 estimates and satellite monitoring
- March **second advance estimate** placed 2024–25 wheat output around **115.4 million tonnes**, about 1.9% above 2023–24; the supplied article rounds it to 115.3. It is an estimate, not a final harvest total. [Agriculture Ministry series, 10 March 2025](https://desagri.gov.in/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Time-Series-2nd-AE-2024-25-Eng.pdf).
- The page image highlights ISRO's crop forecast: **NRSC's CROP framework** combines remote sensing for near-real-time sowing/harvest monitoring. ISRO separately estimated 122.724 million tonnes across eight major states as of 31 March 2025; that pilot estimate must not be substituted silently for the ministry's national estimate. [ISRO framework](https://www.isro.gov.in/Wheat_Crop_Area_and_Production_Estimation_in_India.html).
## Food security and sustainability
- Production affects MSP procurement, buffer stocks, PDS availability, food inflation and rural incomes. Global production rank does not establish export rank; trade shares/destinations change with year and policy.
- **13 May 2022 wheat-export prohibition** included exceptions for specified prior commitments and government-authorised food-security requests. The source's export destinations/share describe a dated trade situation, not unrestricted exports in April 2025. [DGFT notices via APEDA](https://apeda.gov.in/dgft-trade-notice).
- Response: heat-tolerant/short-duration varieties, zero tillage, crop rotation, water efficiency, soil-health measures, extension/KVKs and crop monitoring. Improve dry-grain storage and logistics; a general cold-chain prescription is not essential for ordinary wheat grain.
- Balance domestic affordability, predictable trade policy and farmer incentives; diversify intensive monocultures to reduce groundwater pressure and pest/nutrient risks.

topics.title: Perovskite photovoltaics and aqueous recycling
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Technology and study
- Perovskite names an **ABX₃ crystal structure**, not a substance made only of organic material. Halide perovskites can act as the light-absorbing layer in solar cells; silicon and perovskite cells/tandems are distinct designs.
- Advantages: high laboratory efficiency, potentially economical processing, thin/light devices and possible flexibility. Lead-containing formulations, moisture/heat stability and large-area durable manufacture remain challenges; not all perovskites contain lead.
- A **12 February 2025 Nature study** demonstrated aqueous recovery of degraded perovskite and recycling of other valuable cell components. It reported **99.0 ± 0.4% by mass recovery of perovskite** and comparable device performance after **five recycling rounds**. This is not a blanket 99% recovery claim for every layer. [Original study](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-024-08408-7).
## Recycling concept
**Used device → separate layers → recover/repair perovskite crystals and other components → fabricate new device.**
- Aqueous chemistry uses **sodium acetate**, **sodium iodide** and **hypophosphorous acid**; acetate helps dissolve lead iodide, while the optimised iodide/acid system supports recovery of suitable crystals. Other layers use solvents including ethanol/ethyl acetate.
- Treat this as controlled laboratory recycling, not a home procedure. Water-based processing reduces dependence on hazardous solvents; it does not make lead-containing effluent harmless or remove chemical handling requirements.
## Circular-economy assessment
- Recovering absorbers, glass, substrates, charge-transport layers and electrodes can conserve resources and reduce waste. Laboratory cell efficiency above 25% in the field does not establish commercial module efficiency or lifetime.
- Scale-up needs reliable collection, separation, lead containment, wastewater management, energy/solvent accounting and quality control. Use **life-cycle assessment** across raw materials, manufacture, use and end of life; commercial/environmental benefits depend on the complete system.
- Practice recall: high efficiency/potential low production cost explain interest; the study's three named aqueous additives are acetate, iodide and hypophosphorous acid.

topics.title: Heatwaves, inequality and heat action plans
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Heat risk and inequality
- WMO identified **2024 as the warmest year on record**, global mean temperature **1.55 ± 0.13°C above 1850–1900**. One calendar year's exceedance is not identical to breaching the Paris Agreement's long-term warming threshold. [WMO 2024 report](https://wmo.int/publication-series/state-of-global-climate/state-of-global-climate-2024).
- Heat exposure reflects temperature, humidity, solar radiation, wind, work intensity and night-time cooling. High humidity limits evaporative cooling; heat-related illness can become life-threatening. Body temperature around 37°C is not a universal outdoor danger threshold.
- Outdoor/agricultural/construction workers face lost working capacity and wages; crops/livestock and food security are affected. Older people, migrants, informal workers and poorly housed households may lack cooling, water and access to services.
- Gendered exposure can arise from caregiving, unpaid work, access to resources and local social norms; vulnerability is context-specific. Avoid treating all women as having the same clothing or work pattern.
## Action plans
- **Ahmedabad's 2013 heat-health action plan** was a pioneering South Asian city initiative, combining early warning, public communication and health preparedness. [Original implementation study](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4024996/).
| Immediate preparedness | Structural adaptation |
|---|---|
| Local alerts; communication in accessible languages | Cool/reflective roofs, shade, ventilation and urban trees |
| Drinking-water access and shaded rest/cooling spaces | Heat-sensitive housing and public-space design |
| Adjust outdoor work hours and rest breaks | Wage-loss protection and inclusive access to cooling |
| Health-worker training and surveillance | Funded local coordination across health, labour and planning |
- Plans should integrate humidity, hot nights and neighbourhood vulnerability; assign responsibilities, finance implementation and track outcomes. Link health preparedness with NPCCHH and disaster-management institutions.
- Air conditioning protects users but can increase electricity demand, emissions and outdoor waste heat; passive cooling, efficient appliances and cleaner electricity reduce this adaptation trade-off.
- The source's **20 days earlier**, workforce/GDP/work-hours figures and **23 states/140 cities** counts lack a consistent cited denominator/time series here; do not memorise them as verified national totals. Prioritise exposure, feasible protection and accountable local implementation.

topics.title: Bullseye Galaxy and collisional rings
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Discovery and mechanism
- **LEDA 1313424**, nicknamed Bullseye, is a collisional ring galaxy. February 2025 observations identified **nine star-filled rings**: Hubble resolved eight and the W. M. Keck Observatory confirmed the ninth.
- A blue dwarf galaxy passed through its centre about **50 million years ago**. Gravitational disturbance → outward/inward density waves in gas → compressed regions and star formation → rings.
- A gas trail links the galaxies, now separated by about **130,000 light-years**. Bullseye's diameter is about **250,000 light-years**. A faded tenth ring is a hypothesis.
- Ring positions test dynamical models; this is an unusually numerous ring system, not the first ring galaxy. [NASA discovery account](https://science.nasa.gov/missions/hubble/hubble-investigates-galaxy-with-nine-rings/).
## Galaxy evolution and dark matter
- Authors discuss a possible route towards a **giant low-surface-brightness galaxy**: an extended diffuse disk with substantial gas. This is an evolutionary interpretation, not an observed completed transformation.
- Gas motions and mass distribution can constrain the gravitational dark-matter halo. Rings do not by themselves demonstrate non-gravitational dark-matter interactions or directly detect dark-matter particles. [Research paper](https://assets.science.nasa.gov/content/dam/science/missions/hubble/releases/2025/02/STScI-01JK935WCAXXH6T0GG33FEDR5J.pdf).

topics.title: Light-controlled bioresorbable pacemaker
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## April 2025 research
- Northwestern researchers reported a **1.8 × 3.5 × 1 mm** temporary pacemaker, smaller than a rice grain, in Nature. Its biocompatible components dissolve after use, avoiding surgical retrieval.
- An internal galvanic battery uses two metal electrodes and body fluids as electrolyte; finite chemical energy supplies pacing. A chest wearable detects an abnormally low heart rate and sends **infrared light pulses** through tissue to activate the implant.
- Heart-rate sensing → wearable light pulse → implant electrical stimulation → controlled heartbeat. The implant needs external control, although it has no connecting pacing wire and incorporates its own battery.
- The small implant can fit a syringe tip, supporting less invasive delivery; injection still penetrates tissue. This is not a phone-controlled, permanently self-powered replacement for all implanted pacemakers.
## Significance and limits
- Intended for **short-term pacing**, especially after cardiac surgery and potentially for newborns with congenital heart defects. Several implants responsive to different light wavelengths could enable coordinated pacing at multiple sites.
- Validation involved animal models and donated human hearts; this was **preclinical research**, not established human clinical efficacy or routine regulatory approval.
- Potential gains: fewer retrieval-related infections/tissue injuries and lower surgical burden. Human trials, safe stimulation/dissolution timing, controller reliability, manufacturing and clinician training remain necessary; cost savings are prospective.
[Northwestern research announcement](https://news.northwestern.edu/stories/2025/03/worlds-smallest-pacemaker-is-activated-by-light).

topics.title: Creative economy and grassroots innovation
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Concept and economic role
- Creative economy draws on creativity, skills, cultural expression and intellectual property: design, crafts, architecture, publishing, audiovisual content, music and related services. **Creativity generates ideas; innovation applies and scales them.**
- UNCTAD reports 2022 creative-services exports of **US$1.4 trillion** and creative-goods exports of **US$713 billion**, respectively 29% and 19% above 2017. Export totals are not total worldwide industry revenue. Source's Indian valuation, employment and export figures use inconsistent years/definitions and should not be combined into one benchmark. [UNCTAD outlook](https://unctad.org/publication/creative-economy-outlook-2024).
## Grassroots innovation pathway
- Mitticool clay refrigeration illustrates electricity-free evaporative cooling ([NIF](https://www.nif.org.in/upload/dwn_files/Annual-Report-2022-23-NIF.pdf)); pedal-operated washing devices and amphibious bicycles illustrate locally adapted ingenuity. Their commercial potential depends on safety, usability, design and demand.
- Scouting → prototype/testing → appropriate IP and finance → incubation/design → production → market access. NIF and GIAN can support scouting, mentoring and commercialisation.
- Barriers: funding gaps, weak visibility and infrastructure, costly/complex IP processes, fragmented markets and limited scaling support. Indigenous knowledge also requires consent, attribution and fair benefit-sharing; formal patents do not cover every creative activity.
- Policy options: proof-of-concept funds, PPP incubation, creative clusters, simpler IP assistance, design education, digital market access and district-level support. **“One District, One Innovation” is an editorial proposal**, distinct from the existing ODOP initiative.
- **World Intellectual Property Day: 26 April 2025**, theme **IP and Music: Feel the beat of IP**. [WIPO](https://www.wipo.int/en/web/ipday/2025/index).

topics.title: Skull Hill and Martian geology
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Observation: 11 April 2025
- Perseverance's **Mastcam-Z** imaged Skull Hill near **Port Anson**, on lower Witch Hazel Hill at the **Jezero crater rim**. It is a dark, angular, pitted **float rock**—a loose rock transported from its original setting—contrasting with pale outcrop.
- Pits may result from loss of clasts or wind scouring. Possible provenance includes eroded igneous outcrop or impact ejecta; colour alone cannot identify a meteorite.
- NASA noted that SuperCam analysis of **nearby similar rocks** was inconsistent with a meteorite origin. This does not establish a final composition/provenance for Skull Hill itself. [NASA field report](https://science.nasa.gov/blog/origins-uncertain-skull-hill-rock/).
## Scientific meaning
- Images → morphology; spectroscopy/chemistry → mineral and elemental composition; geological context → formation/transport interpretation. In-situ instruments already constrain hypotheses; Earth sample analysis would add capabilities, rather than being the only possible evidence.
- Jezero preserves ancient lake/delta environments. Perseverance, launched in 2020, studies geology and past habitability, searches for biosignatures and caches samples. **A suggestive rock nickname or shape is not a fossil or evidence of alien life.**
- Source illustrations of a skull/alien are decorative, not observations. Ice-protected photosynthesis is a modelling hypothesis about possible habitable conditions; it does not demonstrate Martian microbes.
- Mission lessons: combine orbital mapping, high-resolution imaging and compositional instruments; manage sample-return engineering, contamination and cost. Proposed future Indian instruments/cooperation are recommendations, not confirmed mission commitments.
